info.title: Healthier Business Hub API
info.description:
The Healthier Business Hub API gives a client programmatic access to the portals it uses: Hub candidates, Occupational Health, Online Training, Practical Training, Virtual BLS Training, Clinical Interviews, Clinical Appraisals, References, Registration Monitoring and DBS & Right To Work.

**Authentication.** Exchange an API key for a bearer token with `POST /api/v2/auth/token`, send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`, and renew it with `POST /api/v2/auth/refresh`. An access token lasts 60 minutes and a refresh token 7 days. Each endpoint names the scope a key needs in `x-required-scope` (`{portal}:{resource}:{read|write}`; a `:write` scope also grants the matching `:read`).

**Responses.** A single record is `{ "data": { ... } }`. A list is `{ "data": [ ... ], "meta": { ... }, "links": { ... } }` and takes `page`, `per_page` and `sort`. Dates and times are ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z` suffix; a date without a time is `YYYY-MM-DD`. Money is integer pence with `currency: "GBP"`. A person is addressed by `candidate_ref` (a uuid), never by an internal id.

**Errors.** Every error is `{ "error": "snake_case_code", "message": "...", "details": { ... }, "request_id": "..." }`. Quote the `request_id` (also the `X-Request-Id` header of every answer) when you contact support.

**Rate limits.** Each key has an hourly limit. Every answer carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; a `429` adds `Retry-After`.

**Idempotency.** Send an `Idempotency-Key` header on every `POST` that creates something. The same key with the same body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

**Webhooks.** Register an endpoint with `POST /api/v2/webhooks` and choose events. Every delivery is a signed `POST`; see the `webhooks` section of this document for each event.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Exchange an API key for a bearer token, renew it, see which key a token belongs to, and revoke it. Authentication is one exchange for every portal: the same four calls under `/api/v2/auth` serve all of them.

get.summary: Show the key behind the token
get.description:
Tells you which key a token belongs to: the Hub client id, and the key's `name`, `prefix` (its first eight characters, to recognise it), `scopes` and `expires_at`. Use it as the first call of a deployment to check that the key carries the scopes your integration needs, to show which key is configured without revealing it, or as a cheap test that a token still works (Zapier and similar tools use it as the connection test). The secret part of the key and the token's own expiry are never returned; `expires_at` is when the key expires (null if it does not), not the token.

Send the access token in the `Authorization` header. A missing header is `401 unauthenticated`; an unknown, revoked or expired token is `401 invalid_token`; the usual `403 key_inactive` and `403 ip_not_allowed` checks of the key apply. The answer is the object itself and is not wrapped in `data` (like the other authentication answers). It counts against the key's hourly limit and carries the `X-RateLimit-*` headers. No scope is needed. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

200.description: The key the token belongs to: the client id and the key's name, prefix, scopes and expiry. Not wrapped in `data`.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Show the key behind the token: GET /api/v2/auth/me
# Needs curl and jq. Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.
set -eu

BASE_URL="${HUB_BASE_URL:-https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk}"
API_KEY="${HUB_API_KEY:-hbk_replace_with_your_api_key}"

# 1. Exchange the API key for a bearer token. It lasts 60 minutes: keep it and reuse it.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o token.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/auth/token" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"api_key\": \"$API_KEY\"}")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' token.json)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(jq -r '.access_token' token.json)

# 2. Show the key behind the token.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o response.json -w '%{http_code}' -X GET "$BASE_URL/api/v2/auth/me" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' response.json)" >&2
  jq '.details // empty' response.json >&2
  exit 1
fi
jq . response.json

PHP (curl)
x-codeSamples.source:
<?php

// Show the key behind the token: GET /api/v2/auth/me
// Plain PHP 8.1 or newer with ext-curl and ext-json: no packages. Run: php sample.php
// Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.

$baseUrl = rtrim(getenv('HUB_BASE_URL') ?: 'https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk', '/');
$apiKey = getenv('HUB_API_KEY') ?: 'hbk_replace_with_your_api_key';

/**
 * One HTTP call with curl. Returns [status, raw body].
 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body  a JSON string, or an array with CURLFile values for multipart/form-data
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubHttp(string $method, string $url, array $headers, string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    $curl = curl_init($url);
    curl_setopt_array($curl, [
        CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => $method,
        CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => $headers,
        CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
        CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 60,
    ]);

    if ($body !== null) {
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, $body);
    }

    $raw = curl_exec($curl);

    if ($raw === false) {
        throw new RuntimeException('Network error: '.curl_error($curl));
    }

    return [curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE), $raw];
}

/** Prints the standard error body {error, message, details, request_id} and stops. */
function hubFail(int $status, string $raw): never
{
    $error = json_decode($raw, true);
    fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("HTTP %d %s: %s (request_id %s)\n", $status, $error['error'] ?? 'error', $error['message'] ?? $raw, $error['request_id'] ?? '-'));

    if (! empty($error['details'])) {
        fwrite(STDERR, json_encode($error['details'], JSON_PRETTY_PRINT)."\n");
    }

    exit(1);
}

/** The bearer token: exchanged on first use, renewed from the refresh token when asked (a new exchange if it is refused). */
function hubToken(bool $renew = false): string
{
    global $baseUrl, $apiKey;
    static $tokens = null;
    $json = ['Accept: application/json', 'Content-Type: application/json'];

    if ($renew && $tokens !== null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/refresh", $json, json_encode(['refresh_token' => $tokens['refresh_token']]));
        $tokens = $status === 200 ? json_decode($raw, true) : null;
    }

    if ($tokens === null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/token", $json, json_encode(['api_key' => $apiKey]));

        if ($status !== 200) {
            hubFail($status, $raw);
        }

        $tokens = json_decode($raw, true);
    }

    return $tokens['access_token'];
}

/**
 * A call with the bearer token; renews the token once on 401 invalid_token. Returns [status, raw body].
 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubRequest(string $method, string $path, array $headers = [], string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    global $baseUrl;
    $send = fn (string $token): array => hubHttp($method, $baseUrl.$path, ['Accept: application/json', 'Authorization: Bearer '.$token, ...$headers], $body);
    [$status, $raw] = $send(hubToken());

    if ($status === 401 && (json_decode($raw, true)['error'] ?? null) === 'invalid_token') {
        [$status, $raw] = $send(hubToken(renew: true));
    }

    if ($status >= 400) {
        hubFail($status, $raw);
    }

    return [$status, $raw];
}

[$status, $raw] = hubRequest('GET', '/api/v2/auth/me');

echo json_encode(json_decode($raw, true), JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE), "\n";

post.summary: Get a new token pair with a refresh token
post.description:
Trades a refresh token for a new access token and a new refresh token, without sending the API key again. Use it when a call answers `401 invalid_token` because the access token expired (after one hour), or ahead of that. If the refresh token is no longer good, fall back to `POST /auth/token` with the key. Send only `refresh_token` in a JSON body; there is no `Authorization` header.

A refresh token works once. The call revokes the whole pair you used (the old access token stops working at once too) and answers with a new pair of the same lifetimes as at the exchange (3600 and 604800 seconds, so a client that keeps refreshing stays signed in without limit while its key stays valid). Store the new refresh token before you use the new access token. Two processes that refresh with the same token at the same moment cannot both win: the second gets `401 invalid_token` and must exchange the key again, so keep one refresher per pair.

Errors, in the order they are checked: `422 validation_failed` when `refresh_token` is missing, not text or longer than 100 characters; `401 invalid_token` when the token is unknown, already used, revoked or past its seven days (the answer does not say which); `403 key_inactive` when the key behind it is switched off or expired; `403 ip_not_allowed` when the key has an allowlist and the caller's address is not on it. Who may call it: anyone who holds a refresh token; no scope is needed. Not idempotent and not counted against the hourly limit of the key.

Rate limit: 10 calls a minute for each caller address (the limit is not keyed to the token, so every refresh from one address shares it), then `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

refresh_token.description: The `refresh_token` of the pair you hold (up to 100 characters). It works once: this call revokes it together with its access token, so store the new refresh token from the answer. An unknown, used, revoked or expired token is `401 invalid_token`.

requestBody.description: The refresh token of the pair you hold. This is the only field; no `Authorization` header is needed.

200.description: A new token pair with fresh lifetimes (3600 seconds and seven days). The pair you sent is revoked: the old access token and refresh token no longer work.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Get a new token pair with a refresh token: POST /api/v2/auth/refresh
# Needs curl and jq. Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.
set -eu

BASE_URL="${HUB_BASE_URL:-https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk}"
API_KEY="${HUB_API_KEY:-hbk_replace_with_your_api_key}"

# 1. Exchange the API key for a bearer token. It lasts 60 minutes: keep it and reuse it.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o token.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/auth/token" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"api_key\": \"$API_KEY\"}")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' token.json)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Renew the pair with the refresh token. The refresh token you send is revoked at once: keep the new one.
REFRESH_TOKEN=$(jq -r '.refresh_token' token.json)
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o refreshed.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/auth/refresh" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"refresh_token\": \"$REFRESH_TOKEN\"}")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' refreshed.json)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
jq '{token_type, expires_in, refresh_expires_in}' refreshed.json

post.description:
Ends the session of the token you send: the access token in the `Authorization` header and the refresh token that came with it both stop working at once. Use it when a token may have leaked, when a worker that held it is retired, or when a session ends. Nothing is sent in the body. The answer is `{ "status": "revoked" }` and is not wrapped in `data`.

Only this pair is revoked. The API key is untouched, so you can exchange it again with `POST /auth/token`, and other pairs made from the same key keep working. To stop a key altogether, switch it off, delete it or regenerate it on the Developer page. Calling revoke twice with the same token answers `401 invalid_token` the second time, because a revoked token is no longer accepted anywhere. A missing header is `401 unauthenticated`. The call counts against the key's hourly limit, needs no scope and is not idempotent in the `Idempotency-Key` sense (repeating it simply fails as above).

200.description: The pair was revoked: `{ "status": "revoked" }` (not wrapped in `data`). The API key still works for a new exchange.

post.summary: Exchange an API key for a token pair
post.description:
Trades your API key for a short-lived access token and a longer-lived refresh token. It is the first call of every integration and the only sign-in call there is: one exchange serves every portal the key has scopes for (there are no token routes under the portals), and the portals themselves are chosen by the scopes of the key, not by anything you send here. Send only `api_key` in a JSON body (the `hbk_` key from the Developer page of Hub, 52 characters). There is no `Authorization` header and no client id.

The answer is a `token_type` of `Bearer`, an `access_token` valid for `expires_in` seconds (3600, one hour) and a `refresh_token` valid for `refresh_expires_in` seconds (604800, seven days) that can be used once. Both are opaque random strings of 80 characters; Hub keeps only a hash of each, so a lost token cannot be shown again. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every other call. Each exchange makes a new, independent pair: earlier pairs stay valid until they expire or are revoked, and there is no limit on how many are live. Keep one pair per process and renew it with `POST /auth/refresh` rather than exchanging the key on every call.

Who may call it: anyone who holds a key; no scope is needed, and the scopes of the key are not checked here (they are checked on every call that uses the token). The checks run in this order: `422 validation_failed` when `api_key` is missing, not text or longer than 100 characters; `401 invalid_credentials` when no key matches (a revoked or regenerated key is unknown too); `403 key_inactive` when the key is switched off or past its expiry; `403 ip_not_allowed` when the key has an IP allowlist and the caller's address is not on it. A successful exchange records the key's last-used time. The call is not idempotent (it never takes `Idempotency-Key`; a repeat just makes another pair) and it does not count against the key's hourly limit.

Rate limit: 10 calls a minute for each caller address and key value together, then `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`; this limit is separate from, and much tighter than, the hourly limit of the key.

get.description:
Lists the client's webhook endpoints, whoever created them (this API, the Developer page, or an import from an old portal API, which shows `imported: true`). Newest first unless you sort. Each row shows the address, the events it receives, whether it is on, the timeout, the outcome of the last delivery (`last_delivered_at`, `last_response_code`) and `consecutive_failures`, so you can spot an endpoint that is failing before Hub switches it off. The signing secret is never included; only its first characters (`secret_prefix`).

Filters: `is_active` (`true` or `false`), `search` (part of the name or the address, at most 100 characters) and `created_from` / `created_to` (when the endpoint was created; each bound is a whole UTC day). `sort` accepts `id` (the default, newest first), `name` and `created_at`; prefix with `-` for descending. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `name`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches the endpoint name or URL.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: is_active
parameters.description: `true` returns only active endpoints, `false` only switched-off ones. One of: `true`, `false`, `1`, `0`.

200.description: One page of the client's webhook endpoints.

post.description:
Registers an address to receive the events you choose, from any portal, signed with one secret per endpoint. Typical sequence: `GET /webhooks/events` to pick names, this call, `POST /webhooks/{webhook}/test` to check your receiver, then verify `X-Hub-Signature` on every delivery (see the `webhooks` section for the algorithm and code samples).

The answer holds the `signing_secret` (`whsec_` and 48 characters): store it now, it is shown only once, here and when you rotate it. Everything else about the endpoint can be read again later. Send `name` (up to 100 characters), `url` and `events` (at least one); `is_active` (default true) and `timeout_seconds` (5 to 30, default 10) are optional. The address must be a full `https` URL of up to 2048 characters, with no username or password, that resolves to a public server: addresses on private networks, `http` and credentials in the URL are refused with `422` on `url`. Hub checks the address again before every delivery and does not follow redirects, so give the final address (a `3xx` counts as a failed delivery). Only events listed by `GET /webhooks/events` are accepted (`422` on `events.N` otherwise).

From now on every matching event of the client is sent to the address, whatever portal it comes from; you can register several endpoints and an event goes to each one that picked it. The call is not idempotent and does not take `Idempotency-Key`: repeating it creates a second endpoint with its own secret, so list your endpoints before you retry after a lost answer. The answer is the endpoint plus `signing_secret` and `notice`, not wrapped in `data`.

The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:write`.

201.description: The endpoint was created. Store `signing_secret` now.

example.name: Orders system
example.notice: Store the signing secret now. It is not shown again.

put.description:
Changes the fields you send (`name`, `url`, `events`, `is_active`, `timeout_seconds`); fields you leave out keep their value. The rules are those of creating an endpoint, so a new `url` is checked the same way and `events` must name events from `GET /webhooks/events`. `events` replaces the whole list: send every event you still want, not only the new one. Send `timeout_seconds: null` to go back to the default of 10 seconds.

Fix the receiver first: deliveries that failed while it was off are not sent again on their own (use `POST /webhooks/{webhook}/deliveries/{delivery}/redeliver` for the ones you need). Turning an endpoint off (`is_active: false`) stops new events at once. The signing secret does not change; use `POST /webhooks/{webhook}/rotate-secret` for that. Another client's endpoint, or one that was deleted, answers `404 not_found`.

The same body repeated gives the same result, so a retry is safe. The answer is the updated endpoint, not wrapped in `data`. The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:write`.

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint id (integer), from `GET /api/v2/webhooks`.

200.description: The updated endpoint (not wrapped in `data`).

delete.description:
Deletes the endpoint. No new event is sent to it from that moment, and deliveries that were still waiting for a retry fail with the message that the endpoint was switched off or removed (nothing more is sent to the address). The delivery history is no longer reachable through the API, and the signing secret stops being valid. A deleted endpoint cannot be brought back: create a new one, which gets a new secret. To stop events without losing the endpoint and its history, use `PUT /webhooks/{webhook}` with `is_active: false` instead. The answer is `{ "message": "Webhook deleted." }`. The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:write`.

get.summary: List the deliveries of an endpoint
get.description:
Lists the endpoint's deliveries, one row per event sent to it, newest first unless you sort: the event (`event_type`, `event_id`), the `status`, how many attempts have been made (`attempt`), the HTTP status your server returned (`response_code`, null when it did not answer) and when it was delivered. The `status` is `pending` (queued, no attempt yet), `retrying` (an attempt failed and another is scheduled), `delivered` (your server answered with a 2xx status) or `failed` (the last attempt failed, or the endpoint was off). Use the list to find failed deliveries to redeliver and to see why an endpoint is failing; the error text and the beginning of your response are shown on the Developer page, not in this list.

Filters: `status` (one of the four values above), `event_type` (an exact event name, `webhook.test` included) and `created_from` / `created_to` (when the event was queued; each bound is a whole UTC day). `sort` accepts `id` (the default, newest first), `created_at` and `delivered_at`; prefix with `-` for descending. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25). Another client's endpoint answers `404 not_found`.

The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint id (integer), from `GET /api/v2/webhooks`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`, `delivered_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only deliveries with this status: `pending`, `delivered` or `failed`.

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description: Only deliveries of this event, for example `online-training.course.completed`.

200.description: One page of the endpoint's deliveries, newest first.

post.description:
Sends the same event again to the same endpoint as a fresh series of attempts: same body, same `event_id`, same delivery id (`X-Hub-Delivery-Id`), new `X-Hub-Timestamp` and a new signature made with the endpoint's current secret. Because the `event_id` is unchanged, a receiver that ignores event ids it has already handled stays correct. Use it after you fixed your receiver, for a delivery that `failed`; it works on a delivery in any status, including `delivered` (the event is then simply sent a second time).

The answer only says the delivery was queued again (`{ "message": ... }`); the attempt counter goes back to 0, the status to `pending`, and the usual schedule applies (up to 5 attempts, 25 failed deliveries in a row switch the endpoint off). If the endpoint is switched off or has been deleted by then, the delivery fails at once with that message; switch the endpoint on first. A delivery that belongs to another client's endpoint, or to a different endpoint than `{webhook}`, answers `404 not_found`. Each call queues another series; there is no `Idempotency-Key`. The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:write`.

post.description:
Creates a new signing secret (`whsec_` and 48 characters) for the endpoint and returns it once, in `signing_secret`. The old secret stops being valid at once: every delivery from now on is signed with the new one, including deliveries that were already queued and are waiting for a retry, because the signature is made when each attempt is sent. A receiver that still holds only the old secret will therefore reject them. Change the secret in your verifier first, or at the same moment, and keep the old one only until the in-flight retries (up to about 80 minutes) are done if you want to accept both for a short time. Rotate when a secret may have leaked, when someone who knew it leaves, or on a schedule.

The call is not idempotent: every call makes a new secret and invalidates the previous one, so do not retry it blindly after a lost answer (read the endpoint's `secret_prefix`, or just rotate again). The answer is the endpoint plus `signing_secret` and `notice`, not wrapped in `data`. Another client's endpoint answers `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:write`.

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint id (integer), from `GET /api/v2/webhooks`.

200.description: The endpoint with its new signing secret, shown only now.

example.name: Orders system
example.notice: Store the signing secret now. It is not shown again.

The event has the standard envelope (`event_id`, `event_type` `webhook.test`, `occurred_at`) and a `data` of `message` ("HB Compliance Hub webhook test event") and `endpoint_id`. get.description:
Lists the client's candidates in Hub, the people every other portal API refers to. `candidate_ref` is the uuid that identifies a person in all of them: take it from here, or from the answer of `POST /hub/candidates`, and use it in paths, bodies and filters of the portal APIs. Each row shows identity, roles, the overall compliance status and the next expiry date; the services a candidate has with each portal are on `GET /hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}`. Inactive candidates are listed too (`is_active` false); filter them out with `is_active=true`.

Filters: `search` (every word must match the name, email, a role or your own `candidate_reference`; at most 100 characters), `status` or `compliance_status` (the same filter under two names: `compliant`, `expiring_soon`, `expired`, `pending` or `na`), `role` (an exact role name the candidate holds), `is_active` (`true` or `false`), `added_from` / `added_to` (when the candidate was added) and `updated_from` / `updated_to` (when they were last changed). Each range works on whole UTC days: `_from` is the start of the UTC day of the value, `_to` its end, so a time of day in the value is ignored; a `_to` before the `_from` is `422` on `_to`. `sort` accepts `name` (the default, ascending), `email`, `added_at` and `updated_at`; prefix with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25); a page past the last is empty and `meta.total` stays correct.

Use it to find a candidate before creating one (an email address can exist once per client) and to keep your own records in step: poll with `updated_from` set to the last time you looked. The key needs the scope `hub:candidates:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. Errors: `422 validation_failed` for a bad filter, date, `sort` or paging value; the standard `401`, `403` and `429` of every call.

parameters.name: per_page

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `name`, `email`, `added_at`, `updated_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search

parameters.name: updated_from

parameters.name: added_to

post.description:
Adds a candidate exactly as the Add Candidate page does, with no service set up (every service starts `not_required`; the portal APIs set up what they need when you use them). It is the only way to create a person through the API: portals never create one for you, they take the `candidate_ref` this call returns. Send `first_name`, `last_name` and `email`; `phone`, `roles` (up to 10), `specialties` (up to 10), `candidate_reference`, `compliance_officer` and `is_active` are optional.

Side effects: the candidate is created in Hub and in the account's HB Portal record, and unless `is_active` is false the candidate is emailed their activation link (as every portal does for a candidate it adds). No email is sent for an inactive candidate, or when the account is set to activate candidates by hand; a failure to send never undoes the candidate, and the email can be sent again from the Emails menu on the candidate page. The action is recorded in the candidate's activity as made by the person who created the API key (or, if that person is gone, the client's first user).

Duplicates and errors: an email address the client already has is `422 validation_failed` on `email`: look the person up with `GET /hub/candidates?search=` and use their `candidate_ref`. Other field errors are `422` on the field. `422` on `email` also answers an account that has no HB Portal client yet. If the account has no Hub user to add the candidate as, the answer is `409 conflict`.

Idempotency: send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters). The same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and creates nothing; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`; only a successful answer is remembered, so a call that failed validation can be corrected under the same key. The key needs the scope `hub:candidates:write`; the call counts against the key's hourly limit.

first_name.description: The candidate's first name, up to 100 characters.

last_name.description: The candidate's last name, up to 100 characters.

email.description: The candidate's email address (up to 191 characters). It must not belong to another candidate of the client, otherwise `422` on `email`. The activation link is sent here.

phone.description: The candidate's phone number, up to 50 characters.

roles.description: The roles the candidate holds, at most 10, each up to 100 characters.

specialties.description: The candidate's specialties, at most 10, each up to 100 characters.

is_active.description: False to add the candidate as inactive; no activation email is sent. On an update, true makes the candidate active again and false makes them inactive. Default true when adding.

candidate_reference.description: The client's own reference for the candidate, up to 100 characters.

compliance_officer.description: The name of the client's compliance officer for this candidate, up to 150 characters.

201.description: Created. The new candidate, in the standard `data` envelope.

patch.description:
Changes a candidate's identity and Hub's own fields; only the fields you send change, and fields you leave out keep their value (a PATCH has no required field). It accepts `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `phone`, `roles`, `specialties`, `candidate_reference`, `compliance_officer` and `is_active`. `roles` and `specialties` replace the whole list, so send every value you want to keep. `phone`, `candidate_reference` and `compliance_officer` can be set to `null` to clear them.

Name, email and phone are also written to the candidate's HB Portal record (and the first and last name to their login), because the portals read them from there: a change here is what the portal APIs and emails show next. `is_active` makes the candidate active or inactive, as the buttons on the candidate page do (there is no delete; inactive is the equivalent). No email is sent. The change is recorded in the candidate's activity as made by the person who created the API key.

Errors: `422 validation_failed` on the field for an invalid value, and on `email` when another candidate of the client already uses that address; a malformed, unknown or other client's `candidate_ref` answers `404 not_found`. Sending the same body again gives the same result, so a retry is safe; the call does not take `Idempotency-Key`. The key needs the scope `hub:candidates:write`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

first_name.description: The candidate's first name, up to 100 characters.

last_name.description: The candidate's last name, up to 100 characters.

email.description: The candidate's email address (up to 191 characters). It must not belong to another candidate of the client, otherwise `422` on `email`. The activation link is sent here.

phone.description: The candidate's phone number, up to 50 characters.

roles.description: The roles the candidate holds, at most 10, each up to 100 characters.

specialties.description: The candidate's specialties, at most 10, each up to 100 characters.

candidate_reference.description: The client's own reference for the candidate, up to 100 characters.

compliance_officer.description: The name of the client's compliance officer for this candidate, up to 150 characters.

is_active.description: False to add the candidate as inactive; no activation email is sent. On an update, true makes the candidate active again and false makes them inactive. Default true when adding.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

get.description:
Lists the invitations the account has made, newest first by default. An invitation is an email with a one-time link that lets one candidate choose a session and book a place that the account pays for. `status` is `unsent` (created but not sent), `waiting` (sent, not yet used) or `used` (the candidate booked; `booking_id` is then set). Filter with `state` (the same three values), `candidate_ref` (a Hub candidate of the account, matched on the invited email address; otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`), `search` (part of the invited name or email, at most 100 characters), `created_from` and `created_to` (when the invitation was made) and `used_from` and `used_to` (when the booking that used it was made); a date alone is a UK calendar day, a date-time with `Z` or an offset is that instant. `sort` accepts `id` and `created_at` (prefix with `-` for descending; the default is newest first). The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

Only accounts that have booking invitations switched on can use this endpoint; for any other account it answers `403 invites_not_enabled`. The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Part of the invited name or email address as saved on the invitation. At most 100 characters.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-01`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range starts at UK midnight of that day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-31`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range ends at the last second of that UK day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: used_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `used` date is on or after this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-01`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range starts at UK midnight of that day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be after the matching `used_to`.

parameters.name: used_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `used` date is on or before this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-31`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range ends at the last second of that UK day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be before the matching `used_from`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only invitations in this state: `unsent` (made, not sent), `waiting` (sent, not yet used) or `used` (the candidate booked).

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only invitations to this candidate: the `candidate_ref` uuid of one of the account's Hub candidates, matched on the invited email address. An unknown candidate is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

post.description:
Invites a Hub candidate to book a place that the account pays for, with the same steps as the Invites page: the funds are checked, the invitation is made, and it is sent at once. The candidate receives an email with a one-time link that is valid for 8 weeks; the invited name and address are taken from the Hub candidate (the candidate must have an email address, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`: add it with `PATCH /api/v2/hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}`). The course is the one set for the account; you do not choose it, and the candidate chooses the session. `contact_name` and `contact_email` are optional: the person at the account who is copied in on the email. The link is also returned as `url`.

Typical sequence: create the invitation, wait for `practical-training.booking_invite.opened` (the candidate opened the link; sent once) and `practical-training.booking_invite.used` (the candidate booked; the booking then follows its own `booking.*` events), and read the result with `GET /booking-invites/{invite}`. Withdraw an unused invitation with `DELETE /booking-invites/{invite}`. Webhook sent by this call: `practical-training.booking_invite.sent`.

Credits and money: nothing is charged by this call. The place is paid for, with credits or balance, only when the candidate books. This call only checks that the account can pay: with booking credits for accounts that pay for invitations with credits, otherwise with the booking balance. When it cannot, the call answers `402 insufficient_credits` with `available` (`pays_with`, `balance_pence`, `credits`) beside the error, and no invitation is made. Some accounts are allowed to send invitations without funds.

A candidate invited in the last month is not invited again (unless the earlier invitation's booking was cancelled): the call answers `409 conflict`, no email is sent and no invitation is kept. Accounts without booking invitations get `403 invites_not_enabled`. An unknown candidate is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters): repeating the call with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does not send a second email; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without the header a repeat inside the month is a `409 conflict`. The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:write`.

x-credits.description: Not charged by this call. The call only checks that the account can pay for the place (booking credits, or booking balance, depending on the account); the place is paid for when the candidate books. A short balance is 402 insufficient_credits.

201.description: Created and sent. The invitation in the standard `data` envelope. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

delete.description:
Withdraws an invitation: the candidate's link stops working at once and the invitation disappears from the list (a later `GET /booking-invites/{invite}` answers `404 not_found`). `{invite}` is the invitation id. get.description:
Lists the account's practical training bookings, whoever made them (this API, the Bookings page, a booking link or an invitation), newest first by default. Each row carries the course, the location, the session dates, the booking and payment status, the price recorded on the booking, the attendance result and whether a certificate is available. Session times (`start_date`, `end_date`) are UTC instants with a `Z`: the session's UK local time converted to UTC, so a 09:00 session in British Summer Time is `08:00:00Z`. The candidate is shown as `candidate_ref` (the Hub candidate uuid) plus the name on the booking; the email, phone and job role are not returned: read them from the Hub candidate. `candidate_ref` is `null` for a booking made for someone who is not a Hub candidate of this account.

Filters: `status` (`pending`, `booked`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled`, `refunded`, `abandoned`; send it more than once, as `status[]=booked&status[]=pending`, for several; unknown values are ignored), `course_id`, `location_id`, `candidate_ref` (must be a Hub candidate of the account, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`), `start_date_from` and `start_date_to` (the session start; a date alone such as `2026-07-01` is that whole UK calendar day, a date-time with `Z` or an offset is that instant), `created_from` and `created_to` (when the booking was made; a date alone is a UK calendar day, which in British Summer Time starts at 23:00Z the day before), `upcoming=true` (the session has not started) or `past=true` (it has started), `attendance` (`passed`, `present` or `absent`) and `search` (part of the candidate's first name, last name or email on the booking, at most 100 characters). `sort` accepts `created_at` (the default, newest first), `start_date` and `status`; prefix with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `created_at`, `start_date`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-created_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Part of the candidate's first name, last name or email address as written on the booking (not the Hub candidate). At most 100 characters. A `%` or `_` in the text is matched literally.

parameters.name: start_date_from
parameters.description: Only bookings whose session starts on or after this moment. A date alone (`YYYY-MM-DD`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range starts at UK midnight of that day; an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC).  * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body  a JSON string, or an array with CURLFile values for multipart/form-data
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubHttp(string $method, string $url, array $headers, string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    $curl = curl_init($url);
    curl_setopt_array($curl, [
        CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => $method,
        CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => $headers,
        CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
        CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 60,
    ]);

    if ($body !== null) {

    }

    $raw = curl_exec($curl);

    if ($raw === false) {
        throw new RuntimeException('Network error: '.curl_error($curl));
    }

    return [curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE), $raw];

/** Prints the standard error body {error, message, details, request_id} and stops. */
function hubFail(int $status, string $raw): never
{
    $error = json_decode($raw, true);
    fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("HTTP %d %s: %s (request_id %s)\n", $status, $error['error'] ?? 'error', $error['message'] ?? $raw, $error['request_id'] ?? '-'));

    if (! empty($error['details'])) {
        fwrite(STDERR, json_encode($error['details'], JSON_PRETTY_PRINT)."\n");
    }

    exit(1);
}

/** The bearer token: exchanged on first use, renewed from the refresh token when asked (a new exchange if it is refused). */
function hubToken(bool $renew = false): string
{
    global $baseUrl, $apiKey;
    static $tokens = null;
    $json = ['Accept: application/json', 'Content-Type: application/json'];

    if ($renew && $tokens !== null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/refresh", $json, json_encode(['refresh_token' => $tokens['refresh_token']]));
        $tokens = $status === 200 ? json_decode($raw, true) : null;

        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/token", $json, json_encode(['api_key' => $apiKey]));

        if ($status !== 200) {

    }

    return $tokens['access_token'];
}

 *

function hubRequest(string $method, string $path, array $headers = [], string|array|null $body = null): array
{

post.description:
Books the place you hold (`hold_hash`) for a Hub candidate (`candidate_ref`), exactly as the Bookings page does. The session is the one the hold was made on; it is not sent again. The attendee's first name, last name, email, phone and job role (the candidate's first role) are taken from the Hub candidate; you do not send personal data. A candidate without a first name, an email address or a phone number answers `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref` with a message that names what is missing: add it with `PATCH /api/v2/hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}` and call again. Typical sequence: `GET /training-events`, `POST /training-events/{event}/hold`, `POST /bookings`.

`pay_option` decides how the place is paid for. `credits` takes one booking credit for the course and `balance` takes the session price from the booking balance; both are taken now, inside the same transaction as the booking, and the booking is confirmed at once (`booking_status` `booked`, `pay_status` `completed`). `invoice` (or `inv`) confirms the booking at once without taking credits or balance; it is allowed only when invoicing is switched on for the account and the session price is within the account's credit limit. `candidate_pays` leaves the booking `pending`, emails the candidate a payment link (with the agency copied in) and returns the same link as `payment_url`; the booking is confirmed when the candidate pays, and until then it holds no seat, so it cannot be cancelled through the API. When the candidate does not pay, the scheduled housekeeping (when it is running) sets the booking to `abandoned` after two days, or six hours before the session if that is earlier. Too few booking credits for the course, or too little balance for the price, is `402 insufficient_credits` (`available` shows `pays_with`, `balance_pence`, `credits` and `price_pence`); invoicing that is not switched on, or a price over the credit limit, is `422 booking_rejected` with the reason in `message`. Check `GET /credits` first.

For a confirmed booking the seat is taken, the confirmation emails are sent to the candidate and to the agency (`agency_email` when you send it, otherwise the account's notification address; `agency_contact_email` is stored on the booking as the contact and is used as the agency address for some accounts), Healthier Business is notified, and the webhooks run. Webhooks: `practical-training.booking.created` for every new booking, and `practical-training.training_event.seats_low` when the session is nearly full. A `candidate_pays` booking later sends `practical-training.booking.confirmed` when it is paid. The held place is removed once the booking is made; if the booking is rejected, the hold is kept so you can correct the call.

Other errors: `422 validation_failed` on `hold_hash` when the hold does not exist, belongs to another account or has expired (create a new hold), and on `candidate_ref` when it is not a Hub candidate of the account. A full session is `422 no_places_left`, as it is when you hold a place. `422 booking_rejected` also covers a session that is no longer open for booking, and a candidate who already has a pending, booked or rescheduled booking on the same session (matched on email).

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters): repeating the call with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does not book twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Only a successful answer is remembered. Without the header, repeating a call that succeeded fails because its hold is gone. The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:write`.

x-credits.description: Taken by this call when pay_option is credits (one booking credit for the course) or balance (the session price from the booking balance), and the booking is confirmed at once. invoice adds to invoicing; candidate_pays charges the candidate when they pay. Too few credits or too little balance is 402 insufficient_credits; invoicing that is not allowed is 422 booking_rejected.

201.description: Created. The booking in the standard `data` envelope, with `payment_url` when `pay_option` is `candidate_pays`. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

post.description:
Cancels a booking that holds a seat (`booking_status` `booked` or `rescheduled`) and returns the booking with its new status `cancelled`, or `refunded` when money or credit was paid back. The seat is released, the cancellation email is sent to the candidate with the agency copied in, and the webhook event `practical-training.booking.cancelled` is sent (once, with the final status and a `refund` object). There is no body.

What is paid back goes to the original payment method, by these rules (48 hours is measured to the session's start): a booking paid with `credits` gets its credit back, and one paid with `balance` gets its price back to the booking balance, when the session is 48 hours or more away, or when it is inside 48 hours and the account still has a free cancellation this month; otherwise nothing is returned (the cost is logged on the booking, nothing is charged automatically). A booking paid by card (`candidate_pays`) is refunded to the card: nothing inside 48 hours, 20% when the candidate has already used the online training, otherwise everything the card paid. An `invoice` or free booking has nothing to return, so it becomes `cancelled`. `refund` on the answer (and in the webhook) says what was returned: `method` (`credits`, `balance` or `card`), `amount_pence` and `currency` (or `credits`), and `partial`; it never shows card details.

Errors: `404 not_found` for a booking that is not the account's. `409 conflict` when the booking cannot be cancelled: it does not hold a seat (already cancelled or refunded, or a `pending` candidate-pays booking that has not been paid, which has no seat to release) or its session has already started. `503 service_unavailable` when a card refund is due and the payment provider did not make it: the booking is then left untouched, so you can call again. The call is safe to repeat: a booking is refunded at most once, and the second call answers `409 conflict`.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:write`.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

get.summary: Get the booking credits and balance
get.description:
Returns what the account can currently spend on bookings. Practical Training has two kinds of prepayment and this call shows both. `booking_credits` lists, for each course that still has credits, the number of credits left: a credit is one place on that course, it is a count of places, not money, and it can be fractional (a late reschedule fee can take part of a credit). Courses with no credits left are not listed. `booking_balance_pence` is the booking money balance in integer pence (`currency` is `GBP`); it can be zero or negative.

Use this call before you create a booking with `pay_option` `credits` or `balance`, to check that the account can pay: a booking that cannot be paid that way is rejected with `422 booking_rejected`. When the balance or a course's credits fall to a low level or to zero, the webhook events `practical-training.balance.low`, `practical-training.balance.depleted`, `practical-training.credits.low` and `practical-training.credits.depleted` are sent. You cannot top up through the API.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:credits:read` (moved here from `account:read`). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

get.summary: List the credit and balance movements
get.description:
Returns the ledger of the account's prepayments, newest first by default: one row for every confirmed deposit (a top-up or an adjustment) and every withdrawal (a booking paid with credits or balance, or a reschedule fee). Only confirmed movements are listed. A row belongs either to the booking money balance (`wallet` is `booking_balance`, and `amount_pence` holds the money) or to one course's credits (`wallet` is the course id as text, and `credits` holds the credit units). The amount is always positive; `type` says whether it was added (`deposit`) or taken out (`withdraw`). `description` and `booking_id` come from the movement's own record and are null when it has none.

Filter by `wallet` (`booking_balance` or a course id such as `12`), by `type`, and by date with `created_from` and `created_to` (a date such as `2026-10-01` is a UK calendar day, so the range runs from UK midnight of the first day to the end of the last UK day, an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time; a date-time with `Z` or an offset is that instant). Sort by `id` or `created_at` (prefix with `-` for descending). A wallet value that matches none of the account's wallets returns an empty page, not an error. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `practical-training:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-01`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range starts at UK midnight of that day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-31`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range ends at the last second of that UK day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Only movements of this wallet: `booking_balance` for the money balance, or a course id (for example `12`) for that course's credits. At most 100 characters. A value that matches none of the account's wallets returns an empty page.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only movements of this type: `deposit` (money or credits added) or `withdraw` (money or credits taken out).

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

get.description:
Returns the Practical Training account that the API key belongs to: the Hub client id, the account name, the contact and the email addresses held on the account, and whether the account is active. Use it once after you obtain a token to confirm that the key is attached to the account you expect. Everything else in this API is scoped to this one account, and you cannot read another client's data through it.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:account:read`, and the client must have a Practical Training account, otherwise every call of this portal answers `403 portal_unavailable`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. The calls of this portal share a throttle of 120 requests a minute per access token (`429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header when you exceed it), in addition to the hourly limit per key that applies to every v2 call.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

get.description:
Returns the sessions that this account can book: sessions that are active, not hidden, and start in the future, and that are either public or were created for this account (another client's private session is never listed). Each row shows the course, the location, the start and end time, the number of places still free (`remaining_slots`) and the price this account pays for one place (`cost_inc_vat_pence`: the account's rate for the course when it has one, otherwise the session's own price). Session times (`start_date`, `end_date`) are UTC instants with a `Z`: the session's UK local time converted to UTC, so a 09:00 session in British Summer Time is `08:00:00Z`.

This is the first step of booking: choose a session here, hold a place on it with `POST /training-events/{event}/hold`, then book with `POST /bookings`. `remaining_slots` is a snapshot; a place is only taken when the booking is made (holding does not reserve a seat), so the session can still fill before you book. Narrow the list with `course_id`, `location_id`, `start_date_from` and `start_date_to` (a date such as `2026-11-01` is a whole UK calendar day, from the start of the first day to the end of the last; a date-time with `Z` or an offset is that instant) and `available_only=true` (only sessions with at least one free place). `sort` accepts `start_date` (the default, earliest first), `remaining_slots` and `cost`; prefix with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `practical-training:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `start_date`, `remaining_slots`, `cost`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-start_date`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: start_date_from
parameters.description: Only sessions that start on or after this moment. A date alone (`YYYY-MM-DD`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range starts at UK midnight of that day; an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Compared with the session's start. Must not be after `start_date_to`.

parameters.name: start_date_to
parameters.description: Only sessions that start on or before this moment. A date alone (`YYYY-MM-DD`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range ends at the last second of that UK day; an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Compared with the session's start. Must not be before `start_date_from`.

parameters.name: course_id
parameters.description: Only sessions of this course (the `id` from `GET /courses`).

parameters.name: location_id
parameters.description: Only sessions at this location (the `id` from `GET /locations`).

parameters.name: available_only
parameters.description: `true` returns only sessions with at least one free place (`remaining_slots` above 0). `false` or leaving it out also lists full sessions.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

delete.description:
Releases a held place before it expires, so that the account can hold another (an account may hold one place at a time). `{hash}` is the `hold_hash` returned when the place was held. Call it when the candidate decides not to book. Releasing is not needed after `POST /bookings`: a successful booking removes its hold itself. A hold that does not exist, has already been used or released, or belongs to another client answers `404 not_found`. A hold that has passed its `expires_at` but has not yet been cleaned up is released normally.

Nothing is charged and no webhook event is sent. The call is naturally repeatable: the second call answers `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `practical-training:holds:write`.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: The hold token returned when the place or timeslot was held.

200.description: The hold was released. `data.hold_hash` repeats the token that was released and `data.released` is always `true`. The account can hold another place straight away.

hold_hash.description: The `hold_hash` of the hold that was released.

post.description:
Holds one place on a session for 30 minutes so that you can collect the candidate's details and then book it with `POST /bookings`. The hold has no body; the session is the `{event}` in the path. The answer contains the `hold_hash`, which you send to `POST /bookings` as `hold_hash`, the time the hold ends (`expires_at`) and the seconds left (`expires_in_seconds`).

An account may hold only one place at a time. While a hold is live, a second call answers `409 conflict` and the body carries the existing hold in `hold`, so you can use it or release it with `DELETE /training-events/hold/{hash}`. A session with no free place answers `422 no_places_left`. A session that does not exist, is not open for booking or belongs to another client answers `404 not_found`.

A hold does not take a seat and does not charge credits or balance; nothing is sent to the candidate. The seat is taken, and the account charged, only when the booking is created, and the places can be taken by other bookings in the meantime, so a booking can still fail with `422 booking_rejected` even with a live hold. A hold that is not used ends after 30 minutes. When the scheduled clean-up has removed it, the webhook event `practical-training.slot_hold.expired` is sent; the clean-up runs about every five minutes, but a hold already counts as expired from `expires_at` (booking with it answers `422` on `hold_hash`).

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters): repeating the call with the same key within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of answering `409 conflict` because of your own hold. Without the header, a retry after a lost answer is a `409` that carries your hold.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:holds:write`.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: The training event id (integer).

201.description: Created. The new record, in the standard `data` envelope.

get.description:
Lists the alerts of your account for this portal, newest first by default, 25 to a page by default. Registration Monitoring lists registration alerts (every type that does not start with `dbs_` or `rtw_`); DBS & Right To Work lists the `dbs_` and `rtw_` alerts. Acknowledged alerts are included: filter with `acknowledged=false` for the ones that still need a person, which is what a work queue should read. Further filters are `severity` (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`), `type` (an exact alert type, see `type` of an alert), `worker_id` and `created_from` and `created_to` (the day the alert was raised). `sort` orders by `created_at`, `severity` or `type`; the default is newest first.

Where alerts come from: each completed registration check that changes a worker's status, the first check of a worker, and a change of a regulator warning or condition flag raise one; the DBS Update Service raises one when a certificate shows new information or a non-blank certificate is found; the right to work check raises one when the result is no right to work, when a passport image cannot be verified or has a low authenticity score, and when a share code is invalid; and the expiry reminders raise right to work and share code alerts as an expiry approaches. A DBS or right to work alert also sends the `dbs-rtw.alert.raised` webhook. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. A DBS certificate number in an alert's text is always masked (only the last four characters show, for example `********7890`). The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:alerts:read` or `dbs-rtw:alerts:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `created_at`, `severity`, `type`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-created_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only alerts raised whose date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only alerts raised whose date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: acknowledged
parameters.description: `false` returns only open alerts (the ones that still need a person), `true` only acknowledged ones. Left out, both are returned. `1` and `0` also work.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Only alerts of this severity: `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only alerts of this exact type, for example `registration_expired`. See `type` of an alert for the types of this portal. At most 100 characters; a value that is not a type returns an empty list.

parameters.name: worker_id
parameters.description: Only alerts about this worker: a worker id from `GET /workers`.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

data.title: Jane Doe - Registration Lapsed
data.description: NMC registration 12A3456E status changed from active to lapsed.

post.description: Acknowledges open alerts of the portal in one call. Send `ids` (up to 500 alert ids) to acknowledge those; send `type` to acknowledge every open alert of that type; send neither to acknowledge **every open alert of the portal**, so send an explicit `ids` or `type` unless that is what you mean. When `ids` is sent, `type` is ignored. Only open alerts of this portal and your account count: ids that do not exist, belong to another client or to the other portal, or are already acknowledged are skipped without an error. The answer is how many were acknowledged (`acknowledged_count`, possibly 0). No email or webhook is sent and nothing is checked or billed. Errors: `422 validation_failed` for more than 500 ids or an id that is not an integer. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:alerts:write` or `dbs-rtw:alerts:write`.

type.description: An alert type: every open alert of this type in the portal is acknowledged (for example `rtw_share_code_expiry_14_days`). Ignored when `ids` is sent.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

get.description: Lists the account's monthly bills, newest period first, 25 to a page by default. A bill that is still a draft is never shown; every other status is (`generated`, `amended`, `ready_for_collection`, `submitted_to_gocardless`, `paid`, `failed`, `cancelled`). Amounts are integer pence with `currency` `GBP`. `period_from` and `period_to` filter by the month the bill covers, and `sort` orders by `period_start` or `id`. Bills are read only here: the invoice PDF is `GET /billing/bills/{id}/invoice`, and payment is by Direct Debit set up in Hub. Both monitoring portals list the same bills. Nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:billing:read` or `dbs-rtw:billing:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `period_start`, `id`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-period_start`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: period_from
parameters.description: Only bills whose period starts on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `period_to`.

parameters.name: period_to
parameters.description: Only bills whose period starts on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `period_from`.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

get.description:
Returns what the account's monitoring costs. There are no per check or per credit charges in Registration Monitoring and DBS & Right To Work: one monthly subscription covers registration, DBS and right to work monitoring, and every active worker (a registration, a DBS-only or a right-to-work-only worker) counts once towards it. The answer shows the free trial (it starts when the account's first worker is created and lasts one month), whether the account may run checks (`trial.eligible`: during the trial, or with Direct Debit set up and billing allowed, or under a manual access override), the billing type chosen, this month's estimate under each billing type from today's number of active workers and the pricing tiers in force. Amounts are integer pence with `currency` `GBP`.

The billing type is chosen once in Hub and the Direct Debit is set up there; the set-up link is never returned by the API. Both portals return the same figures. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:billing:read` or `dbs-rtw:billing:read`.

  exit 1

post.description:
Asks for up to 200 workers to be checked now, with the same rules and side effects as `POST /workers/{id}/verify`. Send `worker_ids`, or leave it out to check every active worker of the portal (at most 200: with more active workers the call is refused with `422 too_many_workers` and you must send `worker_ids` in batches of up to 200). Ids that are not active workers of your account in this portal are silently left out, not reported. One job is queued per worker and track: in DBS & Right To Work a worker enrolled for both tracks gets two jobs unless you send `track` (`dbs` or `rtw`) to check one track only; in Registration Monitoring the only track is `registration`.

The answer is `202` with `jobs` (`worker_id`, `track`, `job_id`) for every check that was queued and `refused` for those that were not, each with the reason (a worker may be refused for the reasons in `POST /workers/{id}/verify`, while the rest are queued). Poll each `job_id` on `GET /verify/jobs/{job}`. When nothing at all could be queued the call answers `422 verification_refused` with the list in `details.refused`; when there is no active worker to check it answers `422 no_active_workers`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same job ids) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of queueing the checks again; without it every call queues new jobs. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:write` or `dbs-rtw:verification:write`.

worker_ids.description: The ids of the workers to check, at most 200. Leave it out to check every active worker of the portal (refused with `too_many_workers` when there are more than 200). Ids that are not active workers of your account in this portal are left out without an error.

track.description: Check one track only: `registration` in Registration Monitoring; `dbs` or `rtw` in DBS & Right To Work. Left out, every track each worker is enrolled for is checked, so a worker enrolled for both DBS and right to work gets two jobs.

202.description: Accepted. The checks that were queued (`jobs`) and those that were refused with their reason (`refused`), in the standard `data` envelope. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

get.summary: Show the progress of a verification job
get.description:
Returns the state of a job created by `POST /workers/{id}/verify` or `POST /verify/batch`: `status` (`pending`, `processing`, `completed`, `failed`), how many workers it handled (`processed_count` of `total_workers`), how many checks worked (`success_count`) and failed (`failed_count`), how many workers changed status (`status_changes_found`), when it started and ended, and `error_message` when it failed. Poll it every few seconds, not faster than your rate limit allows; a job stays readable after it ends. `completed` means the job ran, not that every check succeeded: look at `failed_count` and at the worker's check history.

A job belongs to the portal that created it: a registration job is only visible in Registration Monitoring, a DBS or right to work job only in DBS & Right To Work, and a job of another client is `404 not_found` (so is a job of the other portal). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:read` or `dbs-rtw:verification:read`.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description: The verification job id (integer) returned by `POST /workers/{worker}/verify` or `POST /verify/batch`.
