post.description:
Uploads a CSV (`multipart/form-data`, field `file`, `csv` or `txt`, at most 10 MB) and queues it. The call answers `202` with the import row at once and the file is read by a background job: poll `GET /worker-imports/{id}`. The first row of the file is the header; get the column names from `GET /worker-imports/template` and check a file first with `POST /worker-imports/preview`, which uses the same rules and stores nothing. `column_mapping` maps an expected field to the header it is read from (without it the import reads the headers as they are, so they must be the field names, and `first_name` and `last_name` must be present or the import fails; the import never guesses a mapping, so send the `suggested_mapping` of a preview as `column_mapping` to use it). `check_frequency` (default `monthly`), `monitoring_start_date` (default today), `consent_given` (default false) and `is_active` (default true) are used for every row that does not carry its own value.

Each row is validated with the same rules as the preview: a row that fails is counted in `failed_count` with its line number and message and the others go on. A row that names a worker that already exists (the same regulator and registration number; the same DBS certificate number for a DBS-only row; the same name and share code for a right-to-work-only row) updates that worker, restoring it if it was removed; any other row creates one. Imported workers are not linked to Hub candidates. DBS & Right To Work rows can enrol a DBS certificate (12 digits, with `dbs_surname`) and a right to work check by `share_code` only: other document types need an upload and cannot be imported. **A row's `consent_given` defaults to false**: an import does not require the consent that `POST /workers` requires, so send `consent_given` true only when the workers have agreed to be monitored. No webhook is sent for an import; the checks that follow raise alerts and webhooks as usual. The imported workers count towards the monthly bill while they are active.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and file within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same import) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of importing the file twice. The import is not limited to the portal of the path: a file whose rows are of the other portal's kind is processed all the same. Errors: `422 validation_failed` for a missing or oversized file, a file that is not `csv` or `txt`, or a `check_frequency` that is not allowed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:write` or `dbs-rtw:imports:write`.

file.description: The CSV file, `csv` or `txt`, at most 10 MB. The first row is the header; blank rows are skipped.

column_mapping.description: Which header of the file holds each field, as an object: the key is an expected field (see `GET /worker-imports/template`), the value the header (compared in lower case, trimmed), or null or an empty string to leave the field unmapped. Send it as `column_mapping[first_name]=First name` in a multipart form. Without it the file's headers must already be the field names.

items.description: The file header that holds one field.

check_frequency.description: The check frequency for rows that carry none: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Default `monthly`.

monitoring_start_date.description: The monitoring start date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, for rows that carry none. Default today.

consent_given.description: Whether the workers have agreed to be monitored, for rows that carry no `consent_given` of their own. Default false: an import does not require consent, so set this to true only when the workers have agreed.

is_active.description: Whether the workers are monitored, for rows that carry no `is_active` of their own. Default true. An inactive worker is not checked.

202.description: Accepted. The import is queued: its id, `status` `pending` and the counts, in the standard `data` envelope. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and file returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

get.description:
Lists the professional registrations your account monitors, 25 to a page by default (`per_page` 1 to 100), sorted by last name unless `sort` says otherwise. Every worker of the account that has a regulator is listed, active or not (`is_active` filters them); workers that are monitored only for DBS or right to work belong to the DBS & Right To Work API and are not shown. The list is scoped to the client of the API key, and a worker of another client never appears.

`search` takes words that must each match the first name, last name, email, registration number or profession. `regulator` is one of the fourteen regulator keys, `status` is a worker status or `not_checked` for a registration that has never been checked, and `check_frequency` is the schedule. `candidate_ref` narrows the list to the worker linked to that Hub candidate (only workers that Hub staff linked have one); a `candidate_ref` that is not one of your Hub candidates is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`. A filter value that is not allowed (an unknown regulator or frequency) is `422 validation_failed` too.

Read only: nothing is changed, checked, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `last_name`, `first_name`, `next_check_due_at`, `last_checked_at`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-last_name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text, at most 100 characters. Every word must match (anywhere in the text, ignoring case) at least one of the fields searched: first name, last name, email, registration number, profession.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only workers created whose date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only workers created whose date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only the worker linked to this Hub candidate: the `candidate_ref` uuid from the Hub core API. Only workers that Hub staff linked to a candidate have one. A value that is not one of your Hub candidates is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

parameters.name: regulator
parameters.description: Only registrations of this regulator, as a lower case key. One of: `nmc`, `gmc`, `hcpc`, `gdc`, `goc`, `gphc`, `ahcs`, `swe`, `sssc`, `scw`, `niscc`, `psni`, `gosc`, `gcc`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only workers whose last check found this status: `active`, `lapsed`, `suspended`, `conditions`, `caution`, `removed`, `erased`, `registered_no_licence`, `not_found`, `manual_review`, `invalid_pin` or `error`. `not_checked` returns the workers that have never been checked successfully. At most 50 characters; a value that is not a status returns an empty list.

parameters.name: is_active
parameters.description: `true` returns only workers that are monitored, `false` only workers that are switched off. `1` and `0` also work.

parameters.name: check_frequency
parameters.description: Only workers checked at this frequency: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly` (or `daily`, which some workers carry but which cannot be set through the API).

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

post.description:
Starts monitoring one professional registration. The worker is created active, with the monitoring start date you give (today when you give none), the check frequency you give (the account's default for registrations, `monthly` when it has none) and consent recorded as given at this moment. The call returns the worker with `201`. It does not link the worker to a Hub candidate: `candidate_ref` is null, and a `hb_candidate_id` in the body is ignored.

If the same regulator and registration number were removed from your account earlier, that worker is restored (same id, earlier checks and alerts kept) and updated with the values you send, instead of a second one being created.

Nothing is checked by this call and nothing is charged by it. The first check is made by the next monitoring run, or at once when you ask for it with `POST /workers/{id}/verify`. When the check completes the worker gets its status, expiry date and restrictions, an alert is raised for the first result and the `registration-monitoring.worker.initial_verification` webhook is sent. Every later status change raises an alert and sends `registration-monitoring.worker.status_changed`. Monitoring is part of the account's subscription (see `GET /billing/usage`): the worker counts towards the monthly bill while it is active, and checks stop when the free trial is over and Direct Debit is not set up.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of creating a second worker, and the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without the header a repeated call is refused anyway when the registration is already monitored (`422 validation_failed` on `registration_number`).

Errors: `422 validation_failed` with `details` naming the field: `consent_given` when it is not true (the worker must have agreed to be monitored), `registration_number` when the regulator and number are already monitored for your account, `date_of_birth` when it is missing for an NMC registration, `regulator` when it is not one of the fourteen keys, and the usual type and length errors. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write`.

201.description: Created. The new worker, in the standard `data` envelope. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

post.summary: Change the monitoring settings of several workers
post.description:
Applies the same settings as `PATCH /workers/{id}/monitoring-settings` to up to 500 workers in one call: send `worker_ids` and at least one of `check_frequency`, `monitoring_start_date` and `is_active` (and, in DBS & Right To Work, `dbs_check_frequency` and `rtw_check_frequency`). The answer is the number of workers changed (`updated_count`). Errors: `422 validation_failed` for an empty or oversized `worker_ids`, a value that is not allowed, or a body with no setting to change; `422 workers_not_found` when an id is unknown, belongs to another client or to the other portal. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write` or `dbs-rtw:workers:write`.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

put.description:
Changes who the worker is: name, contact details, date of birth, profession, compliance officer, notes and the registration itself (regulator and number). Send only the fields to change; `PUT` and `PATCH` behave the same and a field you leave out keeps its value. How often and whether the worker is checked is not changed here: use `PATCH /workers/{id}/monitoring-settings`.

Changing `regulator` or `registration_number` points the worker at a different registration; the next check reads the new one, the checks already made stay in the history and nothing is re-checked by this call. No check, email, alert, webhook or charge is triggered by an edit. The call returns the worker as it is now.

Errors: `422 validation_failed` with `details` naming the field: `registration_number` when the regulator and number are already monitored for your account by another worker, `date_of_birth` when it is missing or emptied for an NMC registration (the NMC check needs it), `regulator` when it is not one of the fourteen keys, and the usual type and length errors. A worker of another client, or a DBS or right to work worker, is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

first_name.description: The worker's first name, at most 255 characters.

last_name.description: The worker's last name, at most 255 characters.

email.description: The worker's email address, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

phone.description: The worker's telephone number, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

date_of_birth.description: The worker's date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`, before today. It is required for an NMC registration and cannot be cleared there; for the other regulators send null to clear it.

profession.description: The worker's profession, free text, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

compliance_officer_name.description: The person responsible for the worker's compliance, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

notes.description: Free text notes, at most 5000 characters; send null to clear them.

regulator.description: The regulator key: `nmc`, `gmc`, `hcpc`, `gdc`, `goc`, `gphc`, `ahcs`, `swe`, `sssc`, `scw`, `niscc`, `psni`, `gosc` or `gcc`. Changing it points the worker at a register of another regulator.

registration_number.description: The registration number (PIN) the regulator issued, at most 255 characters. The regulator and number pair must not already be monitored for your account by another worker.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

patch.description:
Changes who the worker is: name, contact details, date of birth, profession, compliance officer, notes and the registration itself (regulator and number). Send only the fields to change; `PUT` and `PATCH` behave the same and a field you leave out keeps its value. How often and whether the worker is checked is not changed here: use `PATCH /workers/{id}/monitoring-settings`.

Changing `regulator` or `registration_number` points the worker at a different registration; the next check reads the new one, the checks already made stay in the history and nothing is re-checked by this call. No check, email, alert, webhook or charge is triggered by an edit. The call returns the worker as it is now.

Errors: `422 validation_failed` with `details` naming the field: `registration_number` when the regulator and number are already monitored for your account by another worker, `date_of_birth` when it is missing or emptied for an NMC registration (the NMC check needs it), `regulator` when it is not one of the fourteen keys, and the usual type and length errors. A worker of another client, or a DBS or right to work worker, is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

first_name.description: The worker's first name, at most 255 characters.

last_name.description: The worker's last name, at most 255 characters.

email.description: The worker's email address, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

phone.description: The worker's telephone number, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

date_of_birth.description: The worker's date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`, before today. It is required for an NMC registration and cannot be cleared there; for the other regulators send null to clear it.

profession.description: The worker's profession, free text, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

compliance_officer_name.description: The person responsible for the worker's compliance, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

notes.description: Free text notes, at most 5000 characters; send null to clear them.

regulator.description: The regulator key: `nmc`, `gmc`, `hcpc`, `gdc`, `goc`, `gphc`, `ahcs`, `swe`, `sssc`, `scw`, `niscc`, `psni`, `gosc` or `gcc`. Changing it points the worker at a register of another regulator.

registration_number.description: The registration number (PIN) the regulator issued, at most 255 characters. The regulator and number pair must not already be monitored for your account by another worker.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

get.summary: List the evidence files of a registration
get.description:
Lists the files captured by the checks of one worker, newest first by default, 25 to a page by default. Each check of a registration can capture a screenshot of the regulator's register page and a saved copy of the page; an NMC check can add sanction PDFs and a GDC check determination PDFs for conditions or a caution. The evidence is what lets you show an auditor what the register said on the day. A worker with no files yet (one that has never been checked, for example) gets an empty list.

The rows carry `download_url`, which points to `GET /evidence/{file}/download`; the files are never served from a public address and need your bearer token. `captured_from` and `captured_to` filter by the day the file was captured, and `sort` orders by `captured_at`, `id` or `file_size`. A worker of another client, or a DBS or right to work worker, is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is checked, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `captured_at`, `id`, `file_size`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-captured_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: captured_from
parameters.description: Only files captured whose date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `captured_to`.

parameters.name: captured_to
parameters.description: Only files captured whose date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `captured_from`.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

patch.summary: Change the monitoring settings of a worker
patch.description:
Changes how often a worker is checked and whether monitoring is on. Send at least one of `check_frequency`, `monitoring_start_date` and `is_active` (and, in DBS & Right To Work, `dbs_check_frequency` and `rtw_check_frequency`); a body with none of them is `422 validation_failed`. In Registration Monitoring `check_frequency` is the schedule of the registration. In DBS & Right To Work `check_frequency` sets every track the worker is enrolled for, and `dbs_check_frequency` or `rtw_check_frequency` sets one track and wins over `check_frequency` for it; a track the worker is not enrolled for is left alone.

Side effects: a changed frequency reschedules the next check of the track while the worker is active, counted from the last check (or the start date when there has been none) for a registration and from now for DBS and right to work, so the new `next_check_due_at` is in the answer. Switching a worker off (`is_active` false) clears every next check date and stops scheduled checks; switching it on again reschedules each track from its frequency. Nothing is checked immediately, no email, alert or webhook is sent, and nothing is charged by this call, but an active worker counts towards the monthly bill (`GET /billing/usage`), so switching a worker off removes it from the bill from then on.

The answer holds `registration` (Registration Monitoring) or `dbs` and `rtw` (DBS & Right To Work, null for a track the worker is not enrolled for). A worker of another client or of the other portal is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write` or `dbs-rtw:workers:write`.

Lists every check made for one worker on one track, newest first, 25 to a page by default. In Registration Monitoring the track is `registration` and each row is a registration check (`status`, `status_changed`, `previous_status`, `expiry_date`, ...). parameters.description: Only checks made whose date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `checked_to`.

parameters.name: checked_to
parameters.description: Only checks made whose date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `checked_from`.

parameters.description: Ignored: Registration Monitoring has one track, `registration`.

post.description:
Asks for one worker to be checked now instead of waiting for the schedule: a registration against the regulator's register (Registration Monitoring), or the DBS certificate against the DBS Update Service or the right to work against the Home Office service or the passport image (DBS & Right To Work). The call creates a verification job and answers `202` with its `job_id` at once; the check runs in the background. Poll `GET /verify/jobs/{job}` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`, read the result on the worker (`GET /workers/{id}`) and in its history (`GET /workers/{id}/verification`), and the evidence on `GET /workers/{id}/evidence`.

Registration Monitoring has one track (`registration`) and ignores `track`. In DBS & Right To Work send `track` (`dbs` or `rtw`) when the worker is enrolled for both; for a worker enrolled for one track it is optional. A `track` that is not `dbs` or `rtw` is `422 invalid_track`, and omitting it for a worker enrolled for both is `422 track_required`.

The rules are the ones a person pressing Re-check in Hub meets, and a refusal is `422 verification_refused` with the reason in `message`: manual re-checks are not enabled for the account, the worker is not active, the worker is not enrolled for the track, the account may not run checks (the free trial has ended and Direct Debit is not set up, or the regulator's connector is switched off or has used its monthly allowance), or the regulator's connector is paused. When the check ends it can change the worker's status: a change raises an alert and the `registration-monitoring.worker.status_changed`, `dbs-rtw.dbs.status_changed` or `dbs-rtw.rtw.status_changed` webhook, and the first registration result sends `registration-monitoring.worker.initial_verification`. A manual check is not charged separately: monitoring is part of the account's subscription (`GET /billing/usage`). Where the verification engine is switched off the request is only recorded: the job stays `pending` and no regulator is called.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body for the same worker within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same `job_id`) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of queueing a second check; without it every call queues a new job. Another client's worker, or one of the other portal, is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:write` or `dbs-rtw:verification:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

schema.description: Registration Monitoring has one track, so the body can be left out.

track.description: Ignored: Registration Monitoring has one track, `registration`. Accepted so one client can serve both monitoring portals.

202.description: Accepted. The check is queued: the job id, the track and the job status, in the standard `data` envelope. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

get.description:
Lists the alerts of your account for this portal, newest first by default, 25 to a page by default. Registration Monitoring lists registration alerts (every type that does not start with `dbs_` or `rtw_`); DBS & Right To Work lists the `dbs_` and `rtw_` alerts. Acknowledged alerts are included: filter with `acknowledged=false` for the ones that still need a person, which is what a work queue should read. Further filters are `severity` (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`), `type` (an exact alert type, see `type` of an alert), `worker_id` and `created_from` and `created_to` (the day the alert was raised). `sort` orders by `created_at`, `severity` or `type`; the default is newest first.

Where alerts come from: each completed registration check that changes a worker's status, the first check of a worker, and a change of a regulator warning or condition flag raise one; the DBS Update Service raises one when a certificate shows new information or a non-blank certificate is found; the right to work check raises one when the result is no right to work, when a passport image cannot be verified or has a low authenticity score, and when a share code is invalid; and the expiry reminders raise right to work and share code alerts as an expiry approaches. A DBS or right to work alert also sends the `dbs-rtw.alert.raised` webhook. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. A DBS certificate number in an alert's text is always masked (only the last four characters show, for example `********7890`). The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:alerts:read` or `dbs-rtw:alerts:read`.

parameters.name: sort

/**

 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body  a JSON string, or an array with CURLFile values for multipart/form-data
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubHttp(string $method, string $url, array $headers, string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    $curl = curl_init($url);
    curl_setopt_array($curl, [
        CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => $method,
        CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => $headers,
        CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
        CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 60,
    ]);

    if ($body !== null) {
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, $body);
    }

    $raw = curl_exec($curl);

    if ($raw === false) {
        throw new RuntimeException('Network error: '.curl_error($curl));
    }

    return [curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE), $raw];

/** Prints the standard error body {error, message, details, request_id} and stops. */
function hubFail(int $status, string $raw): never
{
    $error = json_decode($raw, true);
    fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("HTTP %d %s: %s (request_id %s)\n", $status, $error['error'] ?? 'error', $error['message'] ?? $raw, $error['request_id'] ?? '-'));

    if (! empty($error['details'])) {
        fwrite(STDERR, json_encode($error['details'], JSON_PRETTY_PRINT)."\n");
    }

    exit(1);
}

function hubToken(bool $renew = false): string
{
    global $baseUrl, $apiKey;
    static $tokens = null;
    $json = ['Accept: application/json', 'Content-Type: application/json'];

    if ($renew && $tokens !== null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/refresh", $json, json_encode(['refresh_token' => $tokens['refresh_token']]));

    }

    return $tokens['access_token'];

 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body

function hubRequest(string $method, string $path, array $headers = [], string|array|null $body = null): array
{

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Download a DBS certificate PDF: GET /api/v2/dbs-rtw/evidence/dbs/120
# Needs curl and jq. Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.
set -eu

BASE_URL="${HUB_BASE_URL:-https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk}"
API_KEY="${HUB_API_KEY:-hbk_replace_with_your_api_key}"

# 1. Exchange the API key for a bearer token. It lasts 60 minutes: keep it and reuse it.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o token.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/auth/token" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"api_key\": \"$API_KEY\"}")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' token.json)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(jq -r '.access_token' token.json)

# 2. Download a DBS certificate PDF.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o dbs.pdf -w '%{http_code}' -X GET "$BASE_URL/api/v2/dbs-rtw/evidence/dbs/120" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' dbs.pdf)" >&2
  jq '.details // empty' dbs.pdf >&2
  rm -f dbs.pdf
  exit 1
fi
echo "Saved dbs.pdf"

post.description:
Asks for up to 200 workers to be checked now, with the same rules and side effects as `POST /workers/{id}/verify`. Send `worker_ids`, or leave it out to check every active worker of the portal (at most 200: with more active workers the call is refused with `422 too_many_workers` and you must send `worker_ids` in batches of up to 200). Ids that are not active workers of your account in this portal are silently left out, not reported. One job is queued per worker and track: in DBS & Right To Work a worker enrolled for both tracks gets two jobs unless you send `track` (`dbs` or `rtw`) to check one track only; in Registration Monitoring the only track is `registration`.

The answer is `202` with `jobs` (`worker_id`, `track`, `job_id`) for every check that was queued and `refused` for those that were not, each with the reason (a worker may be refused for the reasons in `POST /workers/{id}/verify`, while the rest are queued). Poll each `job_id` on `GET /verify/jobs/{job}`. When nothing at all could be queued the call answers `422 verification_refused` with the list in `details.refused`; when there is no active worker to check it answers `422 no_active_workers`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same job ids) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of queueing the checks again; without it every call queues new jobs. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:write` or `dbs-rtw:verification:write`.

worker_ids.description: The ids of the workers to check, at most 200. Leave it out to check every active worker of the portal (refused with `too_many_workers` when there are more than 200). Ids that are not active workers of your account in this portal are left out without an error.

track.description: Check one track only: `registration` in Registration Monitoring; `dbs` or `rtw` in DBS & Right To Work. Left out, every track each worker is enrolled for is checked, so a worker enrolled for both DBS and right to work gets two jobs.

202.description: Accepted. The checks that were queued (`jobs`) and those that were refused with their reason (`refused`), in the standard `data` envelope. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

get.summary: Show the progress of a verification job
get.description:
Returns the state of a job created by `POST /workers/{id}/verify` or `POST /verify/batch`: `status` (`pending`, `processing`, `completed`, `failed`), how many workers it handled (`processed_count` of `total_workers`), how many checks worked (`success_count`) and failed (`failed_count`), how many workers changed status (`status_changes_found`), when it started and ended, and `error_message` when it failed. Poll it every few seconds, not faster than your rate limit allows; a job stays readable after it ends. `completed` means the job ran, not that every check succeeded: look at `failed_count` and at the worker's check history.

A job belongs to the portal that created it: a registration job is only visible in Registration Monitoring, a DBS or right to work job only in DBS & Right To Work, and a job of another client is `404 not_found` (so is a job of the other portal). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:read` or `dbs-rtw:verification:read`.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description: The verification job id (integer) returned by `POST /workers/{worker}/verify` or `POST /verify/batch`.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

post.description:
Uploads a CSV (`multipart/form-data`, field `file`, `csv` or `txt`, at most 10 MB) and queues it. The call answers `202` with the import row at once and the file is read by a background job: poll `GET /worker-imports/{id}`. The first row of the file is the header; get the column names from `GET /worker-imports/template` and check a file first with `POST /worker-imports/preview`, which uses the same rules and stores nothing. `column_mapping` maps an expected field to the header it is read from (without it the import reads the headers as they are, so they must be the field names, and `first_name` and `last_name` must be present or the import fails; the import never guesses a mapping, so send the `suggested_mapping` of a preview as `column_mapping` to use it). `check_frequency` (default `monthly`), `monitoring_start_date` (default today), `consent_given` (default false) and `is_active` (default true) are used for every row that does not carry its own value.

Each row is validated with the same rules as the preview: a row that fails is counted in `failed_count` with its line number and message and the others go on. A row that names a worker that already exists (the same regulator and registration number; the same DBS certificate number for a DBS-only row; the same name and share code for a right-to-work-only row) updates that worker, restoring it if it was removed; any other row creates one. Imported workers are not linked to Hub candidates. DBS & Right To Work rows can enrol a DBS certificate (12 digits, with `dbs_surname`) and a right to work check by `share_code` only: other document types need an upload and cannot be imported. **A row's `consent_given` defaults to false**: an import does not require the consent that `POST /workers` requires, so send `consent_given` true only when the workers have agreed to be monitored. No webhook is sent for an import; the checks that follow raise alerts and webhooks as usual. The imported workers count towards the monthly bill while they are active.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and file within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same import) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of importing the file twice. The import is not limited to the portal of the path: a file whose rows are of the other portal's kind is processed all the same. Errors: `422 validation_failed` for a missing or oversized file, a file that is not `csv` or `txt`, or a `check_frequency` that is not allowed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:write` or `dbs-rtw:imports:write`.

get.summary: List DBS and right to work workers
get.description:
Lists the workers your account monitors for DBS and right to work, 25 to a page by default (`per_page` 1 to 100), sorted by last name unless `sort` says otherwise. A worker is listed when it is enrolled for a DBS certificate, a right to work check or both, active or not (`is_active` filters them); workers that are monitored only for a professional registration belong to the Registration Monitoring API and are not shown. The list is scoped to the client of the API key.

`search` takes words that must each match the first name, last name, email or profession. `check_type` keeps the workers enrolled for `dbs` or for `rtw`. `compliant` is `true` for workers whose every enrolled track is in good standing (DBS status `BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO`, right to work status `has_right`; a track not yet checked is not in good standing) and `false` for the others. `candidate_ref` narrows the list to the worker linked to that Hub candidate (only workers that Hub staff linked have one); a `candidate_ref` that is not one of your Hub candidates is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`. A filter value that is not allowed is `422 validation_failed` too.

Read only: nothing is changed, checked, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:workers:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `last_name`, `first_name`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-last_name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text, at most 100 characters. Every word must match (anywhere in the text, ignoring case) at least one of the fields searched: first name, last name, email, profession.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only workers created whose date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only workers created whose date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only the worker linked to this Hub candidate: the `candidate_ref` uuid from the Hub core API. Only workers that Hub staff linked to a candidate have one. A value that is not one of your Hub candidates is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

parameters.name: check_type
parameters.description: Only workers enrolled for this check: `dbs` (a DBS certificate) or `rtw` (right to work). A worker enrolled for both appears under either value.

parameters.name: compliant
parameters.description: `true` returns only workers whose every enrolled track is in good standing (DBS status `BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO` and right to work status `has_right`, each only when the worker is enrolled for it; a track not yet checked is not in good standing). `false` returns the others. `1` and `0` also work.

parameters.name: is_active
parameters.description: `true` returns only workers that are monitored, `false` only workers that are switched off. `1` and `0` also work.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

post.summary: Add a worker to DBS and right to work monitoring
post.description:
Enrols one worker for a DBS Update Service check, a right to work check, or both: send `dbs_certificate_number` with `dbs_surname` and `date_of_birth` for DBS, and `rtw_document_type` (with `rtw_share_code`, or an upload) for right to work. At least one of the two is required, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `dbs_certificate_number`. The worker is created active, with the monitoring start date you give (today when you give none), the frequencies you give for each track (the account's default for the track when you give none) and consent recorded as given at this moment. The call returns the worker with `201`. It does not link the worker to a Hub candidate: `candidate_ref` is null.

Send `multipart/form-data` when you upload a file, JSON otherwise. A passport document type (`uk_passport`, `irish_passport`, `irish_passport_card`) needs `rtw_passport_image` (an image); every other document type except `share_code` needs `rtw_document_file` (`jpg`, `jpeg`, `png` or `pdf`); each upload is at most 10 MB. A passport is read from the image, a share code is checked against the Home Office service, and the other document types are stored for manual handling and are not verified automatically. For a share code worker also send `date_of_birth`: the Home Office check needs it, and a check without it ends with an error (this call does not require it for a share code worker). A share code is three groups of three letters or digits, like `ABC DEF GHI`; it is stored in upper case. A DBS certificate number is exactly 12 digits and must not already be monitored for your account.

Nothing is checked by this call and nothing is charged by it. The first checks are made by the next monitoring run, or at once when you ask for them with `POST /workers/{id}/verify`. A DBS check sets the worker's DBS status and stores a certificate PDF; a right to work check sets the right to work status and stores a screenshot. A change of status raises the `dbs-rtw.dbs.status_changed` or `dbs-rtw.rtw.status_changed` webhook, and findings (new DBS information, a missing right to work, an expiring share code) raise an alert, an email to the account and the `dbs-rtw.alert.raised` webhook. Monitoring is part of the account's subscription (see `GET /billing/usage`): the worker counts towards the monthly bill while it is active, and checks stop when the free trial is over and Direct Debit is not set up.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body (uploads included) within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of creating a second worker, and the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

Errors: `422 validation_failed` with `details` naming the field: `consent_given` when it is not true, `dbs_certificate_number` when it is not 12 digits, is already monitored, or when neither track is given, `dbs_surname` and `date_of_birth` when they are missing for a DBS enrolment, `rtw_share_code` when it is missing or malformed for a share code worker, `rtw_passport_image` or `rtw_document_file` when the upload the document type needs is missing, and the usual type and size errors. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:workers:write`.

201.description: Created. The new worker, in the standard `data` envelope. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

put.description:
Changes who the worker is: name, contact details, date of birth, profession, compliance officer, notes and the surname used for the DBS check. Send only the fields to change; `PUT` and `PATCH` behave the same and a field you leave out keeps its value. The DBS certificate number, the right to work document and the share code are not edited here (a share code has its own endpoint, `PUT /workers/{id}/share-code`), and how often and whether the worker is checked is changed with `PATCH /workers/{id}/monitoring-settings`.

A worker of another client, or a registration worker, is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:workers:write`.

compliance_officer_name.description: The person responsible for the worker's compliance, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

notes.description: Free text notes, at most 5000 characters; send null to clear them.

dbs_surname.description: The surname sent to the DBS Update Service with the certificate number, at most 255 characters. Only for a worker enrolled for DBS; for any other worker the field is refused.

get.summary: List the evidence of a DBS and right to work worker
get.description:
Lists everything Hub holds as evidence for one worker, as one list: a DBS certificate PDF for each DBS check that generated one (`type` `dbs_certificate`), a screenshot for each right to work check that captured one (`rtw_screenshot`), then the uploaded `passport` image and `document` file if the worker has them. The checks come newest first; the uploads have no check and no time. The evidence is what lets you show an auditor what the service said on the day. A worker with no evidence yet (one that has never been checked, for example) gets an empty list.

Each row carries `download_url`, which points to the matching download endpoint; the files are never served from a public address and need your bearer token. `type` keeps one kind of file, `checked_from` and `checked_to` filter by the day of the check (uploads have no date and drop out when either is used), and `sort` orders by `checked_at` or `type`. A worker of another client, or a registration worker, is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is checked, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `checked_at`, `type`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-checked_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: checked_from
parameters.description: Only evidence of checks made on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. The uploaded `passport` and `document` have no date and are left out when this or `checked_to` is used. Must not be after `checked_to`.

parameters.name: checked_to
parameters.description: Only evidence of checks made on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. The uploaded `passport` and `document` have no date and are left out when this or `checked_from` is used. Must not be before `checked_from`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only this kind of evidence: `dbs_certificate`, `rtw_screenshot`, `passport` or `document`.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

get.summary: Download an uploaded passport image or document
get.description: Streams the file uploaded when the worker was added: `passport` is the passport image (`rtw_passport_image`), `document` the document file (`rtw_document_file`). The file is sent with `Content-Disposition: inline`, the media type recorded for its extension (PNG, JPEG or PDF), `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. It is an identity document: store it with the same care as the original. A worker with no such upload, a missing file, or a worker of another client is `404 not_found`; any other `kind` than `passport` or `document` is a `404` too. Nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:evidence:read`.

parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Which uploaded file: `passport` (the passport image sent as `rtw_passport_image`) or `document` (the document file sent as `rtw_document_file`). Any other value is `404 not_found`.

200.description: The uploaded passport image or document. The media type follows the file extension.

patch.summary: Change the monitoring settings of a worker
patch.description:
Changes how often a worker is checked and whether monitoring is on. Send at least one of `check_frequency`, `monitoring_start_date` and `is_active` (and, in DBS & Right To Work, `dbs_check_frequency` and `rtw_check_frequency`); a body with none of them is `422 validation_failed`. In Registration Monitoring `check_frequency` is the schedule of the registration. In DBS & Right To Work `check_frequency` sets every track the worker is enrolled for, and `dbs_check_frequency` or `rtw_check_frequency` sets one track and wins over `check_frequency` for it; a track the worker is not enrolled for is left alone.

Side effects: a changed frequency reschedules the next check of the track while the worker is active, counted from the last check (or the start date when there has been none) for a registration and from now for DBS and right to work, so the new `next_check_due_at` is in the answer. Switching a worker off (`is_active` false) clears every next check date and stops scheduled checks; switching it on again reschedules each track from its frequency. Nothing is checked immediately, no email, alert or webhook is sent, and nothing is charged by this call, but an active worker counts towards the monthly bill (`GET /billing/usage`), so switching a worker off removes it from the bill from then on.

The answer holds `registration` (Registration Monitoring) or `dbs` and `rtw` (DBS & Right To Work, null for a track the worker is not enrolled for). A worker of another client or of the other portal is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write` or `dbs-rtw:workers:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

put.summary: Renew a right to work share code
put.description:
Replaces the share code of a worker that is monitored with a share code (`rtw.document_type` is `share_code`). A share code is valid for 90 days, so renew it when `rtw.share_code_expires_at` is near or `rtw.share_code_stale` is true (the scheduled right to work run skips a worker whose code is stale, and alerts are raised 14 days and 3 days before it expires and when it has expired). The code is stored in upper case; entering it sets `rtw.share_code_provided_at` to today and so restarts the 90 day window at once. The call does not run a check: the next scheduled check, or `POST /workers/{id}/verify` with `track` `rtw`, uses the new code. The call returns the worker.

Errors: `422 not_share_code_worker` when the worker is monitored with another document type (the code only applies to a share code worker; use the other endpoints to change those), `422 validation_failed` on `rtw_share_code` when it is missing or not three groups of three characters like `ABC DEF GHI`, and `404 not_found` for a worker that is not enrolled for right to work, belongs to another client, or is a registration worker. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:workers:write`.

parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

get.summary: List the check history of a worker
get.description:
Lists every check made for one worker on one track, newest first, 25 to a page by default. In Registration Monitoring the track is `registration` and each row is a registration check (`status`, `status_changed`, `previous_status`, `expiry_date`, ...). In DBS & Right To Work send `track` (`dbs` or `rtw`), which is required for a worker enrolled for both tracks (`422 track_required`, and `422 invalid_track` for any other value); a DBS row has the Update Service `status` and `has_evidence_pdf`, a right to work row has `status` (`has_right` or `no_right`), `method`, `expiry_date` and `has_screenshot`. A check that failed to reach a result is in the history with `result` `error` and does not change the worker's status. `checked_from` and `checked_to` filter by the day of the check and `sort` orders by `checked_at` or `id`.

Read only: nothing is changed, checked, sent or billed. A worker of another client or of the other portal is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:read` or `dbs-rtw:verification:read`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `checked_at`, `id`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-checked_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: checked_from
parameters.description: Only checks made whose date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `checked_to`.

parameters.name: checked_to
parameters.description: Only checks made whose date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `checked_from`.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: The track whose history to list: `dbs` or `rtw`. Required when the worker is enrolled for both tracks (`422 track_required`); optional when enrolled for one. Any other value is `422 invalid_track`.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

items.description: A DBS check when `track` is `dbs`, a right to work check when it is `rtw`.

post.description:
Asks for one worker to be checked now instead of waiting for the schedule: a registration against the regulator's register (Registration Monitoring), or the DBS certificate against the DBS Update Service or the right to work against the Home Office service or the passport image (DBS & Right To Work). The call creates a verification job and answers `202` with its `job_id` at once; the check runs in the background. Poll `GET /verify/jobs/{job}` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`, read the result on the worker (`GET /workers/{id}`) and in its history (`GET /workers/{id}/verification`), and the evidence on `GET /workers/{id}/evidence`.

Registration Monitoring has one track (`registration`) and ignores `track`. In DBS & Right To Work send `track` (`dbs` or `rtw`) when the worker is enrolled for both; for a worker enrolled for one track it is optional. A `track` that is not `dbs` or `rtw` is `422 invalid_track`, and omitting it for a worker enrolled for both is `422 track_required`.

The rules are the ones a person pressing Re-check in Hub meets, and a refusal is `422 verification_refused` with the reason in `message`: manual re-checks are not enabled for the account, the worker is not active, the worker is not enrolled for the track, the account may not run checks (the free trial has ended and Direct Debit is not set up, or the regulator's connector is switched off or has used its monthly allowance), or the regulator's connector is paused. When the check ends it can change the worker's status: a change raises an alert and the `registration-monitoring.worker.status_changed`, `dbs-rtw.dbs.status_changed` or `dbs-rtw.rtw.status_changed` webhook, and the first registration result sends `registration-monitoring.worker.initial_verification`. A manual check is not charged separately: monitoring is part of the account's subscription (`GET /billing/usage`). Where the verification engine is switched off the request is only recorded: the job stays `pending` and no regulator is called.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body for the same worker within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same `job_id`) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of queueing a second check; without it every call queues a new job. Another client's worker, or one of the other portal, is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:write` or `dbs-rtw:verification:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

track.description: The track to check: `dbs` (the DBS Update Service) or `rtw` (right to work). Required when the worker is enrolled for both tracks (`422 track_required`); optional when the worker is enrolled for one. Any other value is `422 invalid_track`.

202.description: Accepted. The check is queued: the job id, the track and the job status, in the standard `data` envelope. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

get.description:
Lists the account's candidates who have Online Training (candidates that were archived are left out), ordered by first name, then last name unless you sort. A candidate is identified by `candidate_ref`, the uuid of the Hub core API, where candidates are created and edited; here you only read their training. Each row has identity (read only), `account_status` (`active` once the candidate has activated their login, `pending` before), `training_status`, the counts of courses assigned, completed and expired, who pays (`paid_by`), `renewal_mode`, `completed_at` and `expires_at`. `training_status` is null for a candidate with no course assigned.

Filters: `search` (every word must match the first name, last name or email), `candidate_ref` (one candidate; an unknown or other client's reference gives an empty list, not an error), `status` (`up_to_date`, `expiring_soon`, `expired` or `not_completed`; only candidates with courses are matched), `enrolled` (`true` for candidates with courses, `false` for none), `course_id` (candidates who have that course assigned) and `expires_from` / `expires_to` (on `expires_at`, each bound a whole UTC day). `sort` accepts `first_name`, `last_name`, `email` and `expires_at`; prefix with `-` for descending. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

A candidate who exists in Hub but has never been given online training is not listed (assign a course to start them). The status buckets are the ones Hub stores for its dashboard, so a filtered list matches the dashboard tiles. The key needs the scope `online-training:candidates:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: sort

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Every word must match the candidate name or email (courses: the course name).

parameters.description: Only rows for this candidate: the `candidate_ref` uuid from the Hub core API.

get.description:
Streams a combined training certificate as a PDF (`application/pdf`, shown inline, never cached) for the candidate's completed courses, with a file name such as `training-certificate-000123-261028.pdf`. `type` chooses which completions go on it: `current` (the default: completed, not expired, and still assigned), `assigned` (completed and still assigned, expired ones included), `excl-expired` (completed and not expired, assigned or not), `all` and `incl-expired` (every completion on record), `range` (completed between `date_from` and `date_to`, both required, UK dates, the last day included), `course` (the latest completion of one course, `course_id` required), and `care` or `cstf` (every completion, with the care or CSTF headings when the account uses them, otherwise the standard certificate). There is one line per completion on record, so a course renewed several times appears once per completion except under `course`.

When no completed course matches, the answer is `422` with the code `no_certificates`, not an empty PDF: change the `type` or the dates. A `date_to` before `date_from`, a missing `date_from`, `date_to` or `course_id` for its type, or an unknown `type` is `422 validation_failed` on that field. Another client's candidate, an unknown one and a malformed `candidate_ref` answer `404 not_found`. The certificate is the one Hub produces; the call only reads, nothing is stored or emailed, and the `online-training.certificate.issued` webhook is for certificates staff supply in Hub, not for this call. The key needs the scope `online-training:certificates:read`.

parameters.name: type

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description: With `type=range`: the last day, `YYYY-MM-DD` (UK date), not before `date_from`.

parameters.name: course_id
parameters.description: With `type=course`: the course id.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Download a certificate: GET /api/v2/online-training/candidates/9f1c2d3e-4b5a-4c6d-8e7f-0a1b2c3d4e5f/certificate

{

        CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => $method,
        CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => $headers,
        CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,

{

    $json = ['Accept: application/json', 'Content-Type: application/json'];

put.summary: Set the courses of a candidate
put.description:
Sets the exact list of courses the candidate should have, exactly as the Assign Courses page in Hub does: courses in `course_ids` that the candidate does not have are added, assigned courses that are not in the list are removed (their results and history are kept, and no credits are refunded), courses already assigned are left alone, and `[]` removes every course. Instead of `course_ids` you can send `candidate_group_id`, and the courses of that candidate group (limited to courses the account may assign) are assigned; the group is also saved on the candidate. Settings you leave out (`training_charge`, `renewal_mode`, `renew_training`, `send_reminders`, `framework_id`, `fixed_renewal`) keep the candidate's current values; a candidate who is new to Online Training starts from the account's defaults. `framework_id` and `fixed_renewal` are ignored unless the account lets candidates choose them.

Who can be assigned: a Hub candidate of the account (`candidate_ref` from `POST /hub/candidates`). If the candidate has no Online Training record yet, one is made first, as the Hub pages make it: the account's candidate with the same email is adopted, otherwise a new record and learner login are created, and the candidate keeps the same `candidate_ref`. The activation email is sent for a new login unless `send_activation_email` is false or the account activates candidates by hand. Every course id is checked against the catalogue (`GET /courses`) before anything is written or created: one that is not available is `422 validation_failed` on `course_ids` and nothing changes.

Side effects: the candidate is emailed about the courses added (as in Hub), and the webhook `online-training.course.assigned` is queued for the added courses. Nothing is sent when nothing is added. Repeating the same call changes nothing, so it is safe to retry after a lost answer; the call does not take `Idempotency-Key`.

Credits: by default agency-paid credits are taken when the candidate starts a course group, so `credits_charged` is normally 0. When the account is set to charge at assignment and the credits are not enough, the answer is `402 insufficient_credits` with `needed` and `available` (credits) in `details`, and no course is written (a candidate record made by this same call stays, without courses). Check `GET /credits` first. Other errors: `404 not_found` for an unknown or other client's `candidate_ref`; `422` on `candidate_group_id` for a group that is not one of the account's active groups, and on any field with an invalid value. The key needs the scope `online-training:candidates:write`.

x-credits.description: Agency-paid credits are normally taken when the candidate starts a course group, so credits_charged is usually 0. When the account charges at assignment, an unaffordable assignment answers 402 and writes nothing.

post.summary: Send a reminder email to a candidate
post.description:
Emails the candidate a reminder through Hub's mailer, as the Send Reminder buttons in Hub do. `email_type` is `training_reminder` (their training needs attention; sent with the account's reminder wording and an opt-out link) or `course_completion_reminder` (they have courses not completed yet; the email lists them, and the answer's `incomplete_courses` says how many). The answer is `{ "data": { "email_type", "message" } }`, and for the second type also `incomplete_courses`. It confirms the email was queued, not that it was delivered or read.

Each successful call sends one email, and nothing limits how often you may call, so avoid reminding the same person repeatedly. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters) so a retry after a lost answer does not send it twice: the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`; only a success is remembered.

Errors: `422 validation_failed` on `email_type` when the type is not one of the two, when the candidate has no email address, or (for `course_completion_reminder`) when the candidate has no incomplete courses to remind them about. Another client's candidate and an unknown `candidate_ref` answer `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `online-training:emails:write`.

parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

email_type.description: Which reminder to send: `training_reminder` (the candidate's training needs attention) or `course_completion_reminder` (the candidate has courses not completed yet).

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

Lists the credit ledger, newest first: one row per movement, with its `description` (for example `Credits used`), the credits moved (`amount`, always positive; `is_credit` is true for credits added and false for credits used), the `balance` after it and the candidate it belongs to (`candidate_ref` and `candidate_name`, both null for a movement with no candidate, such as a top-up). When the account shares a credit pool, only the pool's top-ups and the charges of the account's own candidates are listed, so the rows do not add up to the pool's whole history.

Filters: `type` (`all`, the default, `credit` or `debit`) and `created_from` / `created_to` (the first and last day, as `YYYY-MM-DD` UK dates: `2026-10-05` covers 00:00 to 23:59:59 UK time). The list has a fixed order (newest first) and cannot be sorted: a `sort` parameter is `422`. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25). The key needs the scope `online-training:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

get.description:
Returns what the Online Training dashboard in Hub shows, so an integration and the screen always agree: the `tiles` (candidates with training, how many are up to date, expiring soon and expired, and `updated_at`, when the stored statistics were last refreshed), `compliant_pct` (the share that is up to date as a whole percentage, 0 when nobody has training), `needs_attention` (at most five candidates who need action first: expired ones, then those expiring soon, then those who have not completed) and `recent_activity` (the latest five course completions). People are named by `candidate_ref`, so you can open them with `GET /candidates/{candidate_ref}`.

The tiles come from statistics Hub stores per candidate and refreshes in the background, not from a live count of every course, so they can lag a recent change by a short time; `updated_at` says how fresh they are. The expired and expiring buckets can overlap, so the tiles need not add up to `total`. The key needs the scope `online-training:account:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

get.description:
Lists your account's alerts, as the Alerts page does: requests that were `rejected` and need resubmitting, and assessments that ended `not_fit` with a fail letter. Both are `critical`. Each row has a stable `key` (for example `rejected:4821`), the `type`, the `status_label`, the candidate (`candidate_ref`, `candidate_name`), the `clearance`, the `request_id` (null for an older questionnaire with no request), the `submission_id`, a `description` and the time `at`. For a rejection the `description` carries the reviewer's note, which is why the list is health data. `type` filters to one kind and `sort` accepts `at` and `type`.

An alert you dismissed is left out until its request changes status. The call is written to the API log without its bodies. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:alerts:read`. This is health data. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `at`, `type`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Alerts: `rejected` or `not_fit`. Credit transactions: `all`, `credit` or `debit`. One of: `rejected`, `not_fit`.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

// Dismiss all alerts: POST /api/v2/occupational-health/alerts/clear
// Plain PHP 8.1 or newer with ext-curl and ext-json: no packages. Run: php sample.php
// Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.

$baseUrl = rtrim(getenv('HUB_BASE_URL') ?: 'https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk', '/');
$apiKey = getenv('HUB_API_KEY') ?: 'hbk_replace_with_your_api_key';

/**
 * One HTTP call with curl. Returns [status, raw body].
 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body  a JSON string, or an array with CURLFile values for multipart/form-data
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubHttp(string $method, string $url, array $headers, string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    $curl = curl_init($url);
    curl_setopt_array($curl, [
        CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => $method,
        CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => $headers,
        CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
        CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 60,
    ]);

    if ($body !== null) {
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, $body);
    }

    $raw = curl_exec($curl);

    if ($raw === false) {
        throw new RuntimeException('Network error: '.curl_error($curl));
    }

    return [curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE), $raw];
}

/** Prints the standard error body {error, message, details, request_id} and stops. */
function hubFail(int $status, string $raw): never
{
    $error = json_decode($raw, true);
    fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("HTTP %d %s: %s (request_id %s)\n", $status, $error['error'] ?? 'error', $error['message'] ?? $raw, $error['request_id'] ?? '-'));

    if (! empty($error['details'])) {
        fwrite(STDERR, json_encode($error['details'], JSON_PRETTY_PRINT)."\n");
    }

    exit(1);
}

/** The bearer token: exchanged on first use, renewed from the refresh token when asked (a new exchange if it is refused). */
function hubToken(bool $renew = false): string
{
    global $baseUrl, $apiKey;
    static $tokens = null;
    $json = ['Accept: application/json', 'Content-Type: application/json'];

    if ($renew && $tokens !== null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/refresh", $json, json_encode(['refresh_token' => $tokens['refresh_token']]));
        $tokens = $status === 200 ? json_decode($raw, true) : null;
    }

    if ($tokens === null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/token", $json, json_encode(['api_key' => $apiKey]));

        if ($status !== 200) {
            hubFail($status, $raw);
        }

        $tokens = json_decode($raw, true);
    }

    return $tokens['access_token'];
}

/**
 * A call with the bearer token; renews the token once on 401 invalid_token. Returns [status, raw body].
 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubRequest(string $method, string $path, array $headers = [], string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    global $baseUrl;
    $send = fn (string $token): array => hubHttp($method, $baseUrl.$path, ['Accept: application/json', 'Authorization: Bearer '.$token, ...$headers], $body);
    [$status, $raw] = $send(hubToken());

    if ($status === 401 && (json_decode($raw, true)['error'] ?? null) === 'invalid_token') {
        [$status, $raw] = $send(hubToken(renew: true));
    }

    if ($status >= 400) {
        hubFail($status, $raw);
    }

    return [$status, $raw];
}

[$status, $raw] = hubRequest('POST', '/api/v2/occupational-health/alerts/clear');

echo json_encode(json_decode($raw, true), JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE), "\n";

post.description:
Hides one alert from your account's alert list. `key` is the `key` of a row from `GET /alerts`; only an alert that is currently shown can be dismissed, otherwise `404 not_found`, so repeating the call for an alert that is already dismissed answers `404`. The answer is `{ "data": { "dismissed": 1 } }`. A dismissal holds until the request changes status, then a new alert appears if the new status calls for one.

The dismissal is recorded against the API key's owner and is shared with everyone in your account: it also disappears from the Alerts page in Hub. It does not change the request. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:alerts:write`.

key.description: The `key` of the alert to dismiss, from `GET /alerts`. Only an alert that is currently shown can be dismissed.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Dismiss one alert: POST /api/v2/occupational-health/alerts/dismiss
# Needs curl and jq. Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.
set -eu

BASE_URL="${HUB_BASE_URL:-https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk}"
API_KEY="${HUB_API_KEY:-hbk_replace_with_your_api_key}"

# 1. Exchange the API key for a bearer token. It lasts 60 minutes: keep it and reuse it.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o token.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/auth/token" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"api_key\": \"$API_KEY\"}")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' token.json)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(jq -r '.access_token' token.json)

# 2. Dismiss one alert.
BODY='{
    "key": "rejected:4821"
}'
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o response.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/occupational-health/alerts/dismiss" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data "$BODY")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' response.json)" >&2
  jq '.details // empty' response.json >&2
  exit 1
fi
jq . response.json

get.description:
Lists your account's candidates so you can choose who a request is for. Archived and locked candidates are left out. Every word of `search` must match the candidate's name, role or email (so `ann lee` finds Ann Lee), `has_forms=true` keeps only candidates who already have an Occupational Health questionnaire assigned and `false` only those who do not. Rows have the `candidate_ref` (the Hub uuid used by every API), `name`, `email`, `role`, `forms` (the questionnaires assigned) and `has_forms`. `sort` accepts `first_name`, `last_name` and `email`; the default is first name then last name.

A candidate cannot be created here: candidates already exist in Hub, so create one with `POST /api/v2/hub/candidates` and use the same `candidate_ref` in this API. `candidate_ref` is `null` only for a candidate Hub has not synced yet. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:candidates:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-first_name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Every word must match the candidate name, role or email (requests: candidate name or email or reference).

parameters.name: has_forms
parameters.description: `true` returns only candidates with an OH questionnaire assigned, `false` only those without. One of: `true`, `false`, `1`, `0`.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

get.summary: Get a candidate with their request history
get.description:
Returns one candidate (the same row as the list, plus `status`, the candidate's account status) and their `history`: the candidate's requests that have a completed questionnaire, newest first, in the same shape as `GET /requests`. Requests still waiting for the candidate to complete the questionnaire are not in the history: find them with `GET /requests?candidate_ref=`. Archived candidates can be read here even though the list leaves them out.

An unknown, malformed or another account's `candidate_ref` answers `404 not_found`, never `403`. Every view is recorded in the Occupational Health access trail, with the API key as the actor and ids only. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:candidates:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

post.summary: Send the health questionnaire reminder email
post.description:
Emails the candidate a reminder to complete their health questionnaire, exactly as the reminder button in Hub does. The answer `{ "data": { "candidate_ref", "sent": true } }` confirms that the email was queued for the candidate's address. There is no body.

Every call sends one real email, so the call is not idempotent and takes no `Idempotency-Key`: do not retry it blindly after a timeout, and do not call it in a loop (the candidate is also reminded automatically by the chase settings in `GET /settings`). A candidate with no email address answers `422 validation_failed` on `email` and nothing is sent. The call is limited to 20 a minute per key, then `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header. An unknown, malformed or another account's `candidate_ref` answers `404 not_found`.

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:candidates:write`. Side effect: one email to the candidate; nothing is charged.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.
