#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Send the health questionnaire reminder email: POST /api/v2/occupational-health/candidates/9f1c2d3e-4b5a-4c6d-8e7f-0a1b2c3d4e5f/reminder
# Needs curl and jq. Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.
set -eu

BASE_URL="${HUB_BASE_URL:-https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk}"
API_KEY="${HUB_API_KEY:-hbk_replace_with_your_api_key}"

# 1. Exchange the API key for a bearer token. It lasts 60 minutes: keep it and reuse it.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o token.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/auth/token" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"api_key\": \"$API_KEY\"}")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' token.json)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(jq -r '.access_token' token.json)

# 2. Send the health questionnaire reminder email.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o response.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/occupational-health/candidates/9f1c2d3e-4b5a-4c6d-8e7f-0a1b2c3d4e5f/reminder" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' response.json)" >&2
  jq '.details // empty' response.json >&2
  exit 1
fi
jq . response.json

<?php

// Send the health questionnaire reminder email: POST /api/v2/occupational-health/candidates/9f1c2d3e-4b5a-4c6d-8e7f-0a1b2c3d4e5f/reminder
// Plain PHP 8.1 or newer with ext-curl and ext-json: no packages. Run: php sample.php
// Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.

$baseUrl = rtrim(getenv('HUB_BASE_URL') ?: 'https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk', '/');
$apiKey = getenv('HUB_API_KEY') ?: 'hbk_replace_with_your_api_key';

/**
 * One HTTP call with curl. Returns [status, raw body].
 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body  a JSON string, or an array with CURLFile values for multipart/form-data
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubHttp(string $method, string $url, array $headers, string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    $curl = curl_init($url);
    curl_setopt_array($curl, [
        CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => $method,
        CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => $headers,
        CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
        CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 60,
    ]);

    if ($body !== null) {
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, $body);
    }

    $raw = curl_exec($curl);

    if ($raw === false) {
        throw new RuntimeException('Network error: '.curl_error($curl));
    }

    return [curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE), $raw];
}

/** Prints the standard error body {error, message, details, request_id} and stops. */
function hubFail(int $status, string $raw): never
{
    $error = json_decode($raw, true);
    fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("HTTP %d %s: %s (request_id %s)\n", $status, $error['error'] ?? 'error', $error['message'] ?? $raw, $error['request_id'] ?? '-'));

    if (! empty($error['details'])) {
        fwrite(STDERR, json_encode($error['details'], JSON_PRETTY_PRINT)."\n");
    }

    exit(1);
}

/** The bearer token: exchanged on first use, renewed from the refresh token when asked (a new exchange if it is refused). */
function hubToken(bool $renew = false): string
{
    global $baseUrl, $apiKey;
    static $tokens = null;
    $json = ['Accept: application/json', 'Content-Type: application/json'];

    if ($renew && $tokens !== null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/refresh", $json, json_encode(['refresh_token' => $tokens['refresh_token']]));
        $tokens = $status === 200 ? json_decode($raw, true) : null;
    }

    if ($tokens === null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/token", $json, json_encode(['api_key' => $apiKey]));

        if ($status !== 200) {
            hubFail($status, $raw);
        }

        $tokens = json_decode($raw, true);
    }

    return $tokens['access_token'];
}

/**
 * A call with the bearer token; renews the token once on 401 invalid_token. Returns [status, raw body].
 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubRequest(string $method, string $path, array $headers = [], string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    global $baseUrl;
    $send = fn (string $token): array => hubHttp($method, $baseUrl.$path, ['Accept: application/json', 'Authorization: Bearer '.$token, ...$headers], $body);
    [$status, $raw] = $send(hubToken());

    if ($status === 401 && (json_decode($raw, true)['error'] ?? null) === 'invalid_token') {
        [$status, $raw] = $send(hubToken(renew: true));
    }

    if ($status >= 400) {
        hubFail($status, $raw);
    }

    return [$status, $raw];
}

[$status, $raw] = hubRequest('POST', '/api/v2/occupational-health/candidates/9f1c2d3e-4b5a-4c6d-8e7f-0a1b2c3d4e5f/reminder');

echo json_encode(json_decode($raw, true), JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE), "\n";

get.description:
Lists the clearance types your account may choose when it creates a request. Each has an `id` (send it as `clearance_type_id` in `POST /requests`), a `name`, `needs_immunisations` (a new starter's request then needs `imms_method`, and may carry immunisation files), `has_scope_choice` (a new starter may ask for `full` or `temporary` clearance in `scope`) and `has_online_form` (Hub has a health questionnaire the candidate can complete online; otherwise the questionnaire is on paper and goes by email).

The questionnaires of a clearance type are derived from it and never chosen: use `GET /clearance-types/{clearance_type}/questionnaire` to see which forms a request for the type assigns and every question on them, and `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers` to answer them for the candidate. The list is short and fixed, so it is one page that holds every type; `sort` accepts `id` and `name`.

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `name`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

get.summary: Get the questionnaire of a clearance type
get.description:
Returns the health questionnaires that a request for this clearance type assigns to a candidate, with every question and how to answer it, so you know what you will have to send before you create a request. The forms are derived from the clearance type: you never pick a form yourself, and the list follows the clearance type for your account (a list set for your account wins over the standard list of the type). `{clearance_type}` is an `id` from `GET /clearance-types`; a type your account may not use answers `404 not_found`.

Each form has `fieldsets` (headings, in questionnaire order) with `questions`. A question has a `key` (the name you answer it under), its `label`, a `type`, whether it is `required`, its `options` for a choice, a `max_length`, and `show_when` for a question that only appears after another answer (a hidden question is not required and its answer is discarded). `answer_format` says in words what to send for that kind of question. `documents` lists whether supporting documents are needed with the answers, the documents the candidate is normally asked for and the file limits. A clearance type with no online questionnaire returns an empty `forms` list: its request is handled by email and paper and has nothing to answer through the API.

This is the same questionnaire the candidate sees, at the version in use now. `request` is null here; read `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire` once a request exists to see where each form stands. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: clearance_type
parameters.description: The clearance type id (integer), from `GET /clearance-types`.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

questions.label: Do you perform exposure prone procedures?
questions.answer_format: The `value` of one of the options.

questions.label: I consent to my answers being shared with Healthier Business
questions.answer_format: true to tick the box (`true`, `yes`, `1`, `on`), false or empty to leave it clear.

get.description:
Returns the credits your account holds (`balance`, whole credits), how many were used this month (`used_this_month`), whether credits are being taken at all (`deducting`), what a new starter costs (`credits_per_new_starter`) and the price of one credit in pence (`price_per_credit_pence`, with `currency` `GBP`). Credits are read only in the API: they are bought on the billing page in Hub, whose address is `top_up_url`, and there is no top-up call.

A credit is taken when the candidate's questionnaire is submitted (by the candidate, or by you with `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`), only when `deducting` is true, only for a new starter's first submission, and renewals are free. A short balance never blocks a request or a submission: it is simply not charged. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

Lists the health questionnaires in your account's form set: the `shortcode`, the `title` and how many `questions` each has. A `shortcode` is how a questionnaire is named everywhere else: in `GET /forms/{shortcode}`, as the `form` filter of `GET /requests`, as `hq_form` in the answer of `POST /requests` and in the path of `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`. The list is short and fixed, so it is one page that holds every form; `sort` accepts `shortcode` and `title`.

This is the whole form set of the account, not the forms of one request. Which forms a request has follows from its clearance type: read `GET /clearance-types/{clearance_type}/questionnaire` before you create a request, or `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire` afterwards.

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `shortcode`, `title`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-shortcode`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

get.description:
Returns the Occupational Health account the API key belongs to: the client `id` (the same number as the Hub client id) and `name`, who is emailed about requests (`notifications`: `hb` for Healthier Business, `agency` for your own address, or `both`), who may upload documents (`document_upload`: `candidate`, `agency` or `both`) and whether uploads are allowed at all (`allows_uploads`). Call it once at start-up to check that the key reaches the account you expect.

`ftw_routing_configured` says whether a new request has somewhere to be emailed. When it is `false`, `POST /requests` still succeeds but the request has no destination mailbox: it is stored and nobody is emailed, so ask Healthier Business to finish setting the account up before you rely on it. `credit_balance` is the number of credits held and `credits_deducting` says whether credits are taken at all (see `GET /credits`); a short balance never blocks a request.

Everything is scoped to the account of the key and there is no way to read another client's profile. An account without Occupational Health answers `403 portal_unavailable` on every endpoint of this portal. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:account:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

get.description:
Lists the three reports your account can generate: `all_requests` (a spreadsheet of every request), `activity` (a PDF of recent activity) and `expiring` (a spreadsheet of clearances about to expire). Each row has the report's `title`, `subtitle` and `format` (`xlsx` or `pdf`) and the progress of the last run: `status` (`idle`, `processing` or `complete`), `percent`, `count` (the rows in it) and `generated_at` (ISO 8601 UTC, null until it finishes). `sort` accepts `type`, `title` and `generated_at`. The list is short and fixed, so it is one page that holds every report.

Reports are built in the background: start one with `POST /reports/{type}/generate`, poll this list until `status` is `complete`, then download it. The files and their data are kept per account. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:reports:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `type`, `title`, `generated_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-type`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

data.title: All requests
data.description: Every request with its status and outcome.

post.description:
Queues a report to be built in the background, as the Reports page does, and answers `202` at once with `{ "data": { "type", "status": "processing" } }`. The report is not ready yet: poll `GET /reports` until its `status` is `complete`, then download it with `GET /reports/{type}/{format}`. `{type}` is `all_requests`, `activity` or `expiring`; an unknown type answers `404 not_found`. A run that is already processing is left alone (the call still answers `202`), and a new run replaces the previous report's data.

The call is limited to 10 a minute per key, then `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header. The report covers your account only. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:reports:write`. Side effect: one background job; nothing is emailed or charged.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The report type: `all_requests`, `activity` or `expiring`.

202.description: Accepted. The work is queued and continues in the background.

 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}

function hubHttp(string $method, string $url, array $headers, string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    $curl = curl_init($url);
    curl_setopt_array($curl, [
        CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => $method,

get.description:
Lists your account's Occupational Health requests: the same rows, filters and order as the Requests page in Hub. A row is a request that is waiting for the candidate to complete the online questionnaire, or a completed questionnaire with its outcome. Every request has one `id` that never changes (`OH-{id}` is its `reference`), also after the candidate or you complete the questionnaire; an older questionnaire that has no request has `id: null` and is addressed as `form-{submission_id}`. `status` is always one of six client statuses (`submitted`, `awaiting_candidate`, `rejected`, `full_clearance`, `temporary_clearance`, `fail`); staff-only statuses are never returned. Dates are ISO 8601 UTC with a `Z`.

Filters: `status` (send it more than once, as `status[]=fail&status[]=rejected`, for several), `request_type` (`new_starter` or `renewal`), `clearance` (the HB Portal clearance key, for example `epp`), `form` (a questionnaire shortcode), `candidate_ref` (it must be one of your candidates, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`), `reference` (an exact match on `OH-5`, case ignored, or on a questionnaire's own reference; it can be combined with the other filters), `search`, `submitted_from` and `submitted_to`, `completed_from` and `completed_to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`). `sort` accepts `candidate`, `submitted`, `completed` and `status`; prefix with `-` for descending; the default is `-submitted`, newest first. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `candidate`, `submitted`, `completed`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-candidate`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Every word must match the candidate name, role or email (requests: candidate name or email or reference).

parameters.name: submitted_from
parameters.description: Only requests submitted on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `submitted_to`.

parameters.name: submitted_to
parameters.description: Only requests submitted on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `submitted_from`.

parameters.name: completed_from
parameters.description: Only requests whose questionnaire was completed on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `completed_to`.

parameters.name: completed_to
parameters.description: Only requests whose questionnaire was completed on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `completed_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only requests with this client status: `submitted`, `awaiting_candidate`, `rejected`, `full_clearance`, `temporary_clearance` or `fail`. Send it more than once, or comma separated, for several.

parameters.name: request_type
parameters.description: `new_starter` for a first clearance, `renewal` for a renewal.

parameters.name: clearance
parameters.description: The HB Portal clearance key of the clearance type, for example `epp`.

parameters.name: form
parameters.description: The questionnaire shortcode (see `GET /forms`).

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only requests for this candidate: the `candidate_ref` uuid. It must be one of the client's candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Exact match on the request reference, `OH-5`, or on a questionnaire's own reference.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

post.description:
Creates an Occupational Health request for a candidate, exactly as the New Request page does. `candidate_ref` is one of your candidates (otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`, not a 404), `request_type` is `new_starter` or `renewal`, `clearance_type_id` comes from `GET /clearance-types` and `hq_method` says how the health questionnaire is completed. For a new starter whose clearance type needs immunisations, `scope` (`full` or `temporary`) and `imms_method` are required; otherwise `scope` is ignored and treated as `full`. Files (`paper_hq`, `immunisation`, `previous_ftw`) go in a `multipart/form-data` body; their limits are in `GET /request-options`; without files JSON works too.

With an online questionnaire (`hq_method` `online`) and a Hub form for the clearance type, the forms of the clearance type are assigned to the candidate (you cannot choose them: see `GET /clearance-types/{clearance_type}/questionnaire`) and the candidate is emailed to complete them (send `notify_candidate: false` to skip that email when you will answer for the candidate with `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`; everything else is unchanged). The request waits (`status` `awaiting_candidate`) and is emailed to Healthier Business, with its files, once the questionnaire is in. The candidate can complete it, or you can answer it for them with `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`. With a paper questionnaire, or no Hub form, the request is emailed to Healthier Business at once with the uploaded files and its status is `submitted`. The webhooks `occupational-health.request.submitted` and, when it applies, `occupational-health.request.awaiting_candidate` are queued.

The requester Hub needs (the reply-to of the email) is the user who created the API key, else your account's first user; with neither the call answers `422` on `api_key`. This call does not take credits: when credit deduction is switched on (`GET /credits` shows `deducting`), the first completed questionnaire of a new starter costs `credits_per_new_starter` credits and renewals are free; a short balance never blocks. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: repeating the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`, and a repeat that the cache no longer holds answers `200` with `duplicate: true`. Without it every call is its own request. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:write`.

get.summary: Download the requests as a CSV file
get.description:
Streams the requests table as a CSV spreadsheet: UTF-8 with a byte order mark so Excel opens it correctly, one row per request with the columns Candidate, Request type, Form, Clearance, Date, Completed, Status and Outcome, and dates as `dd/mm/yy`. It accepts the same filters as `GET /requests` except `page`, `per_page`, `sort` and `reference`, and returns every matching row (it is not paged). A cell that starts like a spreadsheet formula (`=`, `+`, `-` or `@`) is prefixed with an apostrophe so it is not run.

The file name is `occupational-health-requests-{date}.csv` and the response is `private, no-store`. Each download is recorded in the Occupational Health access trail, with the API key as the actor. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `candidate`, `submitted`, `completed`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-candidate`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Every word must match the candidate name, role or email (requests: candidate name or email or reference).

parameters.name: submitted_from
parameters.description: Only requests submitted on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `submitted_to`.

parameters.name: submitted_to
parameters.description: Only requests submitted on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `submitted_from`.

parameters.name: completed_from
parameters.description: Only requests whose questionnaire was completed on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `completed_to`.

parameters.name: completed_to
parameters.description: Only requests whose questionnaire was completed on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `completed_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only requests with this client status: `submitted`, `awaiting_candidate`, `rejected`, `full_clearance`, `temporary_clearance` or `fail`. Send it more than once, or comma separated, for several.

parameters.name: request_type
parameters.description: `new_starter` for a first clearance, `renewal` for a renewal.

parameters.name: clearance
parameters.description: The HB Portal clearance key of the clearance type, for example `epp`.

parameters.name: form
parameters.description: The questionnaire shortcode (see `GET /forms`).

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only requests for this candidate: the `candidate_ref` uuid. It must be one of the client's candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Exact match on the request reference, `OH-5`, or on a questionnaire's own reference.

200.description: The CSV file: Candidate, Request type, Form, Clearance, Date, Completed, Status, Outcome.

The view is recorded in the Occupational Health access trail, with the API key as the actor and ids only, and the call is written to the API log without its request and response bodies. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:read`. This is health data. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

The request read endpoints (`GET /requests/{id}`, `/answers`, `/documents`, `/ftw`) also accept `form-{submission_id}` for an older questionnaire that has no request; the questionnaire endpoints take a request id only.

get.description:
Returns the answers of the completed questionnaire grouped by fieldset, in the order and with the wording of the questionnaire: each group has a `fieldset` heading and `items`, each with the question `label` and the `value` given. A signature answer also carries `image`, a PNG data URL. A request that is still waiting for the candidate has no answers and returns an empty page; a request with several forms shows the answers of its questionnaire. `sort` accepts `fieldset`.

An unknown request, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`. The request read endpoints (`GET /requests/{id}`, `/answers`, `/documents`, `/ftw`) also accept `form-{submission_id}` for an older questionnaire that has no request; the questionnaire endpoints take a request id only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `fieldset`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-fieldset`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

get.summary: Get the questionnaire of a request
get.description:
Returns the questionnaires of one request, the ones a candidate (or you, on their behalf) has to complete, with every question and how to answer it, and where each form stands. `{id}` is the request `id` from `POST /requests` or `GET /requests`; a request of another client, or an older questionnaire with no request (`form-{id}`), answers `404 not_found`. The forms are the ones the request's clearance type derives; they cannot be chosen.

`request.accepts_answers` says whether answers can be sent now. When it is false, `request.blocked_by` has the reason as an error code: `request_not_online` (the request has a paper questionnaire, or Hub has no form for its clearance type) or `request_closed` (an outcome is already recorded). Each form has a `state`: `due` (not sent), `saved` (the candidate saved it and has to upload documents themselves: it cannot be sent through the API), `submitted`, `resubmit` (rejected, to be sent again) or `more_info` (the reviewer asked for more information), with `can_submit` telling you whether to call `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers` for it. A form that was sent has its `submission_id`, `submission_reference`, `submitted_at` and `submitted_by` (`candidate`, or `client_api` when it was sent through this API). The state is the candidate's: a form the candidate sent within the last 90 days counts for every request that names it.

The answers are not returned here: they are health data, read with `GET /requests/{id}/answers`. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.description: The request id, an integer such as `5`: the same before and after the candidate completes the questionnaire. post.summary: Submit the answers to a questionnaire for a candidate
post.description:
Sends one questionnaire of a request for the candidate, on their behalf, exactly as if the candidate had filled it in and sent it. `{id}` is the request `id` and `{shortcode}` one of its forms (`GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`; the forms follow from the request's clearance type and cannot be chosen). Send the answers as an object of question `key` to answer in `answers`, in the shapes `answer_format` describes, and the supporting documents in `documents` when the questionnaire needs them (`multipart/form-data`; otherwise JSON works). No defaults are filled in: send every question that is shown. A request with several forms has one call per form, in any order.

The answers are validated with the same checks as the candidate's own form: required questions, types, lengths, the options of a choice, date and phone formats, structured answers, and conditional questions (a question that is hidden by another answer is not required and its answer is dropped). Every problem comes back together as `422 validation_failed` with one message per question under `details` as `answers.{key}` (so `answers.is_epp`), and `documents` for a file problem. An answer to a key that is not a question of the form is `422` too, so a mistyped key is never silently lost. Nothing is saved when the call is refused.

A questionnaire that needs documents (`documents_required`) must come with at least one file in this call: the API has no saved-draft step, so a form is either sent whole or not at all. The files are stored with the candidate's submission like the ones a candidate uploads (JPG, PNG or PDF, up to 20 files of 8 MB each, see `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`). An account that does not allow uploads cannot send documents (`422` on `documents`).

On success the state is what the candidate's own submission produces: the candidate's questionnaire is saved with its reference and the status `proc` (the request's client status becomes `submitted`, or stays `awaiting_candidate` while another form of the request has still to be sent), the candidate's last form is updated, credits are taken when credit deduction is switched on (a new starter's first submission; a short balance never blocks it; see `GET /credits`), the Fit to Work request is emailed to Healthier Business with its documents once the request's first form is in (the candidate is not emailed anything), and the webhook `occupational-health.request.questionnaire_completed` is queued with `submitted_by` `client_api` (ids and statuses only, never an answer). Hub records that you, not the candidate, sent it: the API key and the key owner are stored with the submission and appear in the activity trail, and `submitted_by` is `client_api` in this answer and in `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`. Hub also queues the legacy form callback of the account, if it has one, as for any submission. The response holds ids and statuses only; read the answers back with `GET /requests/{id}/answers`.

Conflicts, each with its own code: `409 request_not_online` (the request has a paper questionnaire or no Hub form), `409 request_closed` (an outcome is already recorded), `409 form_not_assigned` (the form is not assigned to the candidate), `409 form_already_submitted` (the candidate, or an earlier call, already sent this form within the last 90 days), `409 form_awaiting_documents` (the candidate saved it and has to upload their documents). A shortcode that is not one of the request's forms is `404 not_found`, and `503 service_unavailable` means the answers could not be saved and nothing was sent: send them again.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters): repeating the call with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and sends nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Only a successful answer is remembered. Without it, repeating a call that succeeded is `409 form_already_submitted`. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:write`. Neither the answers nor the response are written to the API log.

x-credits.description: Not charged by this call as a payment. When credit deduction is on (GET /credits shows deducting), a new starter's first submitted questionnaire costs credits_per_new_starter credits, taken from the balance in the same place the candidate's own submission takes them; renewals are free. A short balance never blocks the call.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The request id, an integer such as `5`: the same before and after the candidate completes the questionnaire. The request read endpoints (`GET /requests/{id}`, `/answers`, `/documents`, `/ftw`) also accept `form-{submission_id}` for an older questionnaire that has no request; the questionnaire endpoints take a request id only.

parameters.name: shortcode
parameters.description: The questionnaire shortcode, from `GET /forms` (or `forms[].shortcode` of a questionnaire answer). A shortcode outside the client's form set is a 404, and so is one that is not a form of the request when you submit answers.

201.description: Created. The submitted questionnaire (ids and statuses only) in the standard `data` envelope. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

get.description:
Streams the PDF report of a completed reference: the candidate, the referee, the answers and, when the account uses scoring, the score. Use it to keep a copy of the reference in your own records. If the stored file is missing (for example for an older imported reference) it is built from the stored answers for this response only and is not saved, so the call changes nothing; the answer is the same file layout either way. Your key needs `references:referees:read` and your account must use the References portal. An unknown referee, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`. Check `has_pdf` on `GET /referees/{uuid}` first if you want to avoid the error. The PDF contains personal data of the candidate and the referee: store it securely.

Sends one referee a reminder email with their link, adds 1 to their `reminder_count` and queues a `references.reference.reminder.sent` webhook. Use it to chase a single referee; use `POST /requests/{uuid}/reminders` to chase everyone who is due. The same rules apply as for the whole request: the referee must have been emailed and not yet completed, declined, expired or bounced, their request must be open, and they must have had fewer reminders than your References settings allow and be due one (the first falls due a set number of days after the request email, each later one a set number of days after the previous; in the standard settings 5 days, then every 3 days, at most 3).

Your key needs `references:requests:write` (the same scope as the other calls that send emails) and your account must use the References portal. When no reminder can be sent the answer is `409 reminder_not_sent`, and the `message` names the referee and the reason (for example that the next reminder is not due until a date, or that the maximum has been reached). An unknown referee, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`. Each successful call sends an email, so do not retry a successful call; a retry after a lost answer is refused until the next reminder is due.

// Remind one referee: POST /api/v2/references/referees/9f1c2d3e-4b5a-4c6d-8e7f-0a1b2c3d4e5f/reminder
// Plain PHP 8.1 or newer with ext-curl and ext-json: no packages. Run: php sample.php
// Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.

$baseUrl = rtrim(getenv('HUB_BASE_URL') ?: 'https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk', '/');
$apiKey = getenv('HUB_API_KEY') ?: 'hbk_replace_with_your_api_key';

/**
 * One HTTP call with curl. Returns [status, raw body].
 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body  a JSON string, or an array with CURLFile values for multipart/form-data
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubHttp(string $method, string $url, array $headers, string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    $curl = curl_init($url);
    curl_setopt_array($curl, [
        CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => $method,
        CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => $headers,
        CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
        CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 60,
    ]);

    if ($body !== null) {
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, $body);
    }

    $raw = curl_exec($curl);

    if ($raw === false) {
        throw new RuntimeException('Network error: '.curl_error($curl));
    }

    return [curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE), $raw];
}

/** Prints the standard error body {error, message, details, request_id} and stops. */
function hubFail(int $status, string $raw): never
{
    $error = json_decode($raw, true);
    fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("HTTP %d %s: %s (request_id %s)\n", $status, $error['error'] ?? 'error', $error['message'] ?? $raw, $error['request_id'] ?? '-'));

    if (! empty($error['details'])) {
        fwrite(STDERR, json_encode($error['details'], JSON_PRETTY_PRINT)."\n");
    }

    exit(1);
}

/** The bearer token: exchanged on first use, renewed from the refresh token when asked (a new exchange if it is refused). */
function hubToken(bool $renew = false): string
{
    global $baseUrl, $apiKey;
    static $tokens = null;
    $json = ['Accept: application/json', 'Content-Type: application/json'];

    if ($renew && $tokens !== null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/refresh", $json, json_encode(['refresh_token' => $tokens['refresh_token']]));
        $tokens = $status === 200 ? json_decode($raw, true) : null;
    }

    if ($tokens === null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/token", $json, json_encode(['api_key' => $apiKey]));

        if ($status !== 200) {
            hubFail($status, $raw);
        }

        $tokens = json_decode($raw, true);
    }

    return $tokens['access_token'];
}

/**
 * A call with the bearer token; renews the token once on 401 invalid_token. Returns [status, raw body].
 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubRequest(string $method, string $path, array $headers = [], string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    global $baseUrl;
    $send = fn (string $token): array => hubHttp($method, $baseUrl.$path, ['Accept: application/json', 'Authorization: Bearer '.$token, ...$headers], $body);
    [$status, $raw] = $send(hubToken());

    if ($status === 401 && (json_decode($raw, true)['error'] ?? null) === 'invalid_token') {
        [$status, $raw] = $send(hubToken(renew: true));
    }

    if ($status >= 400) {
        hubFail($status, $raw);
    }

    return [$status, $raw];
}

[$status, $raw] = hubRequest('POST', '/api/v2/references/referees/9f1c2d3e-4b5a-4c6d-8e7f-0a1b2c3d4e5f/reminder');

echo json_encode(json_decode($raw, true), JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE), "\n";

get.description:
Returns the reference requests of your account, newest first unless you pass `sort`, in the standard list envelope (`data`, `meta`, `links`). Each row is the full request, including its referees, so one call is enough to show progress for many candidates. Use it to find the request of a candidate (`candidate_ref`), to see which requests are still open (`status`), or to find requests that expired or were fully referenced.

Your key needs the `references:requests:read` scope and your account must use the References portal, otherwise the answer is `403 insufficient_scope` or `403 portal_unavailable`. Only requests of your own account are returned; a request of another account never appears. This call is read only: it sends no email and fires no webhook.

`candidate_ref` must be one of your candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref` (not an empty list). `created_from` and `created_to` accept a date (`2026-10-01`) or an ISO 8601 time; a date means the whole day. Without `sort` the order is newest first. The response contains personal data of the candidate (name, email) and of each referee (name, email, phone); handle it accordingly.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `expires_at`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-created_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text, at most 100 characters. It is matched as a part of the text (not word by word) against the request notes, the candidate's first name, last name, name and email, and each referee's name and email.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only rows with this status. One of: `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `expired`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only requests for this candidate: the `candidate_ref` uuid from the Hub core API. It must be one of your candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

parameters.name: collection_mode
parameters.description: Only requests that collect referee details this way: `client_adds` or `candidate_provides`. Any other value, including `both`, is `422 validation_failed`.

parameters.name: is_expired
parameters.description: Send `true` to return only requests that are expired: those with status `expired` and those whose `expires_at` has passed. Send `false` to return only requests that are not (status other than `expired` and no `expires_at` in the past). Leave it out for both. Accepts `true`, `false`, `1` or `0`; anything else is `422 validation_failed`.

parameters.name: is_fully_referenced
parameters.description: Send `true` to return only requests whose references are all in (status `completed`), `false` to return only the others. Leave it out for both. Accepts `true`, `false`, `1` or `0`; anything else is `422 validation_failed`.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

data.notes: Care assistant post, start date 2 November.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# List reference requests: GET /api/v2/references/requests
# Needs curl and jq. Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.
set -eu

BASE_URL="${HUB_BASE_URL:-https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk}"
API_KEY="${HUB_API_KEY:-hbk_replace_with_your_api_key}"

# 1. Exchange the API key for a bearer token. It lasts 60 minutes: keep it and reuse it.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o token.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/auth/token" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"api_key\": \"$API_KEY\"}")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' token.json)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(jq -r '.access_token' token.json)

# 2. List reference requests.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o response.json -w '%{http_code}' -X GET "$BASE_URL/api/v2/references/requests?page=1&per_page=25&status=pending" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' response.json)" >&2
  jq '.details // empty' response.json >&2
  exit 1
fi
jq . response.json

post.description:
Asks for references for one candidate. Choose who gives the referee details with `collection_mode`. With `client_adds` you send the `referees` in the same call: each referee is emailed at once with their private link to the form, and the request becomes `in_progress`. With `candidate_provides` you send no referees: the candidate is emailed a link to a page (the `submission_url` in the answer) where they enter up to the number of referees required; each is then emailed automatically. If the candidate has no email address no email is sent and the call still succeeds; give the candidate the `submission_url` yourself. Referees then answer in their browser: they submit the form or decline. You are told by webhook, and you can read the outcome from the request, the referee and the referee's PDF.

Your key needs `references:requests:write` (add `references:requests:read` to read it back) and your account must use the References portal. The `candidate_ref` must be one of your candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref` (not a 404). Numbers outside the limits, and a `collection_mode` that is not `client_adds` or `candidate_provides` (`both` included), are `422 validation_failed` on the field. A request the references engine refuses answers `422 reference_request_refused` with the reason in `message`: the form is not available to you, `collection_mode` is not one your References settings allow, a `client_adds` request has no referee or has two with the same email address, and so on. A duplicate request for the same candidate is not refused: check `GET /requests?candidate_ref=` first if you want to avoid it.

Side effects: the referee emails above; an activity log entry; and the webhook `references.reference.request.created` is queued once the request exists (the referee emails are queued before it). No credits are charged. The request expires `expiry_days` days from now; nothing happens to it at that moment except that referees can no longer answer and the status becomes `expired`. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and creates and emails nothing again; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without the header every call creates a new request and emails the referees again. The referee details are personal data of third parties: Hub stores them to send the request and to show you the outcome, and they are never put in a webhook.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate the references are for: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). It must be one of your candidates, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

collection_mode.description: Who gives the referee details: `client_adds` (you send them in `referees`) or `candidate_provides` (the candidate is emailed a link to enter them). The value `both` is not accepted: it is `422 validation_failed` on `collection_mode`, so choose one. A way your References settings do not allow is refused with `422 reference_request_refused`.

template_id.description: The form the referees complete: an `id` from `GET /templates`. When omitted, the request takes your default form (set in References settings). An id that is not available to your account is refused with `422 reference_request_refused`.

references_required.description: How many completed references the request needs. At least your References settings' minimum (and never less than 1) and at most their maximum; the standard settings are 2 and 5. When omitted it is your minimum. A value outside your limits is `422 validation_failed`.

expiry_days.description: Days from now until the request expires: 1 to 365. When omitted it is your References settings' default (14 days in the standard settings).

notes.description: A note stored with the request and shown to your staff, at most 1000 characters. It is not sent to referees by the API call. When omitted there is no note.
examples: Care assistant post, start date 2 November.

referees.description: The referees to ask, 1 to 10. Required when `collection_mode` is `client_adds`: every referee is emailed at once. For `candidate_provides` the list is ignored (the candidate gives the referees); you may omit it. Each item has `referee_name`, `referee_email`, `referee_organisation` and `referee_position` (all required) and `referee_phone` and `relationship_to_candidate` (optional). Two referees must not share an email address (compared without regard to case), otherwise `422 reference_request_refused`.

referee_name.description: The referee's full name, at most 255 characters. It appears in the request email and on the reference PDF.

referee_email.description: The referee's email address, a valid address of at most 255 characters. The request and any reminders are sent here. It must differ from the address of every other referee of the request who has not declined, expired or bounced (compared without regard to case).

referee_organisation.description: The organisation the referee works for, at most 255 characters.

referee_position.description: The referee's job title or position, at most 255 characters.

referee_phone.description: The referee's telephone number, at most 50 characters. Optional; when omitted it is stored as null.

relationship_to_candidate.description: How the referee knows the candidate, at most 255 characters (for example "Line manager"). Optional; when omitted it is stored as null.

example.notes: Care assistant post, start date 2 November.

201.description: Created. The new request, in the standard `data` envelope, with its referees (empty for `candidate_provides`). A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Create a reference request: POST /api/v2/references/requests
# Needs curl and jq. Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.
set -eu

BASE_URL="${HUB_BASE_URL:-https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk}"
API_KEY="${HUB_API_KEY:-hbk_replace_with_your_api_key}"

# 1. Exchange the API key for a bearer token. It lasts 60 minutes: keep it and reuse it.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o token.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/auth/token" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"api_key\": \"$API_KEY\"}")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' token.json)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(jq -r '.access_token' token.json)

# 2. Create a reference request.
BODY='{
    "candidate_ref": "9f1c2d3e-4b5a-4c6d-8e7f-0a1b2c3d4e5f",
    "collection_mode": "client_adds",
    "template_id": 1,
    "references_required": 2,
    "expiry_days": 14,
    "notes": "Care assistant post, start date 2 November.",
    "referees": [
        {
            "referee_name": "Dr Helen Carter",
            "referee_email": "helen.carter@riverside-surgery.example",
            "referee_organisation": "Riverside Surgery",
            "referee_position": "Practice Manager",
            "referee_phone": "01632 960123",
            "relationship_to_candidate": "Line manager"
        }
    ]
}'
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o response.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/references/requests" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: ec1d738d-6e57-4038-a19e-0c7df519f856" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data "$BODY")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' response.json)" >&2
  jq '.details // empty' response.json >&2
  exit 1
fi
jq . response.json

Repeating the call on a cancelled request is the `409 request_not_cancellable` above, not a success.

Gives referees more time. The new expiry is `days` days after the current `expires_at` when that is still in the future, otherwise `days` days from now. The request goes back to `pending` and its status is recalculated, so an `expired` request becomes live again. Every referee who has not completed, declined or bounced gets the new expiry, and a referee who had expired is reopened (back to `sent`, or `pending` if they were never emailed) and can use the same link again. Your key needs `references:requests:write` and your account must use the References portal. `days` is required, 1 to 365, otherwise `422 validation_failed`. A `completed` or `cancelled` request cannot be extended (`409 request_not_extendable`), nor can an imported legacy request that nobody answered and that has no expiry date (`409 legacy_request_unanswered`; contact support). An unknown request, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`. The answer is the updated request.

post.summary: Add a referee to a request
post.description:
Adds one more referee to an open request and emails them straight away with their private link. Use it when a referee declined, expired or bounced and you want to replace them, when you need more referees than you first gave, or to add referees to a `candidate_provides` request yourself. The referee's status becomes `sent` and the request's status is recalculated (a `pending` request becomes `in_progress`). The referee will submit or decline in their browser, and you are told by the `references.reference.submitted` and `references.reference.declined` webhooks. Adding a referee does not itself fire a webhook.

Your key needs `references:requests:write` and your account must use the References portal. The request must be open: a `completed`, `cancelled` or `expired` request, or one past its `expires_at`, answers `409 request_not_open` (extend an expired one first). The email address of a referee of the request who has not declined, expired or bounced (compared without regard to case) is `409 referee_already_added`; a request that already has 10 referees who have not declined, expired or bounced is `409 referee_limit_reached`; an imported legacy request that nobody answered is `409 legacy_request_unanswered`. An unknown request, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`; a field that fails validation is `422 validation_failed`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and adds and emails nothing again; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without it, repeating a call whose answer you lost is refused as a duplicate referee (`409 referee_already_added`), so keep the header. The answer is the new referee row; their answers and PDF are read later from `GET /referees/{uuid}`.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The uuid of the record.

referee_name.description: The referee's full name, at most 255 characters. It appears in the request email and on the reference PDF.

referee_email.description: The referee's email address, a valid address of at most 255 characters. The request and any reminders are sent here. It must differ from the address of every other referee of the request who has not declined, expired or bounced (compared without regard to case).

referee_organisation.description: The organisation the referee works for, at most 255 characters.

referee_position.description: The referee's job title or position, at most 255 characters.

referee_phone.description: The referee's telephone number, at most 50 characters. Optional; when omitted it is stored as null.

relationship_to_candidate.description: How the referee knows the candidate, at most 255 characters (for example "Line manager"). Optional; when omitted it is stored as null.

201.description: Created. The new referee, in the standard `data` envelope. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

post.summary: Remind the referees of a request
post.description:
Chases every referee of the request who is due a reminder, and tells you why the others were not. A referee is due when they have been emailed and not yet completed, declined, expired or bounced, the request is open, they have had fewer reminders than your References settings allow, and the waiting time has passed: the first reminder falls due a set number of days after the request email and each later one a set number of days after the previous (in the standard settings 5 days, then every 3 days, at most 3 reminders); a chase window in your settings can also close. The call does not override these rules, so calling it twice in a row sends nothing the second time. Each reminder is an email to the referee with their link, adds 1 to their `reminder_count`, and queues a `references.reference.reminder.sent` webhook.

Your key needs `references:requests:write` and your account must use the References portal. The answer is `200` even when no reminder is sent: `reminders_sent` is then 0 and `skipped` lists each waiting referee by name with the reason (for example that the next reminder is not due until a date). Referees who have finished are not listed. An unknown request, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`. Use `POST /referees/{uuid}/reminder` to chase one referee. The scheduled automatic reminders, where they are switched on, count towards the same maximum.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The uuid of the record.

200.description: How many reminders were sent and the referees who were not reminded, with the reason for each.

skipped.reason: is not due a reminder until 02 Nov 2026

get.description:
Returns the reference forms (templates) you can ask referees to complete: the active forms that belong to Healthier Business and are open to every client, and the active forms your own organisation created. Use an `id` from this list as `template_id` when you create a request (`POST /requests`); without it the request uses your default form, which is the one marked `is_default`. The list gives a summary of each form (name, description, number of questions); the questions themselves are not returned.

Your key needs the `references:templates:read` scope and your account must use the References portal. The list is short, so it is normally one page; it is returned in the standard list envelope and sorted by `name` unless you pass `sort` (`name` or `updated_at`, with `-` for descending). It has no filters or search. Read only: no email, no webhook.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `name`, `updated_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

get.description:
Lists the Virtual BLS Training bookings of the account, newest session first by default. Each row carries the `candidate_ref` of the Hub candidate the booking belongs to (null when your account has no Hub candidate that matches the booking), the name on the booking, the course, the session start and end in UTC, the booking and payment status, the way it was paid, the price, attendance, the Zoom details and what you can still do with it (`can_reschedule`, `can_cancel`, `certificate_available`). The candidate's email address, phone number and job role are not returned: read them from the Hub candidate. Bookings that were abandoned (a pending booking that was never paid and was cleaned up) are never listed.

Filter by `status` (one or several of `pending`, `booked`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled`, `refunded`), `course_id`, `candidate_ref`, session date with `start_date_from` and `start_date_to`, booking date with `created_from` and `created_to`, `upcoming` and `past`, and `search`. Sort by `start_date`, `created_at` or `status` (prefix with `-` for descending). The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25). A `candidate_ref` that is not a candidate of your account is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`, not an empty list. A `status` value that is not one of the known statuses is ignored.

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `start_date`, `created_at`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-start_date`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text, at most 100 characters. A booking matches when the text is part of the first name, the last name or the email address on the booking. The text is not split into words, so a full name such as `Jo Smith` matches nothing; search for one name.

parameters.name: start_date_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `start_date` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `start_date_to`.

parameters.name: start_date_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `start_date` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `start_date_from`.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only bookings with this booking status: `pending`, `booked`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled` or `refunded`. Send the parameter several times (`status[]=booked&status[]=rescheduled`) to match any of them. A value that is not a booking status is ignored, not an error.

parameters.name: course_id
parameters.description: Only bookings for this course: an `id` from `GET /courses`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only bookings of this candidate: their `candidate_ref` uuid from the Hub core API. A booking matches when its HB Portal candidate id or its email address is that of the Hub candidate. A uuid that is not a candidate of your account is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

parameters.description: Send `true` to return only bookings whose session has not started yet.

parameters.name: past
parameters.description: Send `true` to return only bookings whose session has already started.

post.description:
Books the slot you are holding for a candidate. This is the third step of a booking, after `GET /timeslots` and `POST /timeslots/hold`. Send the `hold_hash` of a live hold of your account, the `candidate_ref` of a Hub candidate of your account, the address the training kit is posted to, how the booking is paid for, and the agency contact. The attendee's first name, last name, email address, phone number and job role are not sent: they are taken from the Hub candidate (the job role is the candidate's first role). The booking is made exactly as the Bookings page of Hub makes it, for the course and the date and time of the hold, and the hold is used up.

What `pay_option` does. With `credits` one booking credit of the held course is taken from the account, with `balance` the price in pence is taken from the money balance (at your own rate if the account has one, otherwise the list price), and with `invoice` (or its older spelling `inv`) the booking is charged to the account by invoice at your own rate or the list price. In these three cases the booking is created `booked` with `pay_status` `completed` at once, and the response is the finished booking. With `candidate_pays` the candidate pays by card: the booking is created `pending`, the candidate is emailed a payment link, and the response carries the same link as `payment_url`. The booking becomes `booked` when the candidate pays. The link stops taking payment three days before the session, and an unpaid booking of this kind is never abandoned after an hour (which is what happens to an unpaid pending booking made on the Bookings page), but it is cancelled automatically when the session is five days away or less. Paying by card as the agency is not available through the API.

Side effects. A booking made with credits, balance or invoice sends the booking confirmation email and text message, exactly as the Bookings page does. The webhook event `virtual-bls-training.booking.created` is sent to your endpoints for every booking, and `virtual-bls-training.booking.confirmed` is sent when the booking is confirmed: at once for credits, balance and invoice, and after payment for `candidate_pays`. A trainer is assigned afterwards by the platform, the Zoom meeting details appear on the booking once the meeting exists (`virtual` is null until then), the training kit is sent to `address`, `city` and `postcode`, and the candidate's e-learning account is provisioned afterwards by a background job. The booking is not linked to the Hub candidate record itself: it matches the candidate by their HB Portal candidate id or email address.

Errors. `422 validation_failed` names the field in `details`: `hold_hash` when the hold does not exist, belongs to another account or has expired (hold the slot again); `candidate_ref` when it is not a candidate of your account or the candidate has no first name, no email address or no phone number, or a name the booking rules refuse (letters and spaces only), in which case fix the candidate with `PATCH /api/v2/hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}`; `pay_option`, `address`, `city`, `postcode`, `agency_contact_name` or `agency_contact_email` when missing or invalid; and `booking_fields.field_<id>` when an answer to a booking question is missing or not one of the allowed options. `422 booking_rejected` means the booking rules refused it, most often `That way of paying is not available for this booking.`: the account has no credit for the course, the balance is below the price, or invoicing is not open to the account or its credit limit is too low. Check `GET /credits` and choose another `pay_option`. When the hold's course can no longer be found the answer is also `422 booking_rejected`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and books nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:bookings:write`.

x-credits.description: Charged by this call, before it answers, when pay_option is credits (one credit of the held course) or balance (the price in pence from the money balance). Nothing is taken from either wallet for invoice or candidate_pays. A way of paying the account cannot cover is refused with 422 booking_rejected, not 402.

201.description: Created. The new booking in the standard `data` envelope, with `payment_url` added when `pay_option` was `candidate_pays`. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

post.description:
Cancels a paid booking that has not started. The booking changes to `cancelled`, the trainer, the trainer's calendar entry and the Zoom meeting are released, the candidate is emailed, and the webhook event `virtual-bls-training.booking.cancelled` is sent to your endpoints (with `status` `cancelled`, sent before any refund is made).

Refunds. When the session is more than 120 hours (five days) away the booking is refund eligible (`refund_eligible` is `true`) and is refunded automatically: a booking paid with a credit gets the credit back as a deposit in `GET /credits/transactions`, a booking paid from the balance gets the money back onto the balance, and a booking paid by card is refunded to the card. A booking paid by invoice has nothing to refund. When the refund is made the booking changes on to `refunded`, so the response can show `booking_status` `refunded` rather than `cancelled`. A refund that fails does not fail this call: the booking stays `cancelled` with `refund_eligible` `true` and is refunded by hand. Inside the 120 hours nothing is refunded and `refund_eligible` is `false`. A cancelled booking cannot be reinstated; make a new booking.

Errors. `409 conflict` when the booking cannot be cancelled: it is not paid yet (a `pending` booking for which a candidate has not paid cannot be cancelled here), it is already cancelled or refunded, or its session has already started. A booking of another account is `404 not_found`. This call does not take an `Idempotency-Key`; a repeat after the first succeeded answers `409 conflict`.

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:bookings:write`.

post.description:
Moves a paid booking to another free timeslot of the same course. Send the new `date` and `time` in UK local time; the slot must be one that `GET /timeslots` lists as free (a slot has to be at least five days ahead and is not held, so you do not hold it first). The booking changes to `rescheduled`, keeps its price and way of paying, and the session start and end change. The trainer is released and a new one is assigned afterwards by the platform, the Zoom meeting is moved, the old calendar entry of the trainer is cancelled, and the candidate is emailed the new time. The webhook event `virtual-bls-training.booking.rescheduled` is sent to your endpoints. Nothing is charged by a reschedule made outside the late-change window.

The late-change window. Within 120 hours (five days) before the session a reschedule needs a flat fee to be paid first, which the platform sets (its default is 20 pounds). Until it is paid this call answers `402 payment_required` with a `payment_url` in the body: the candidate pays the fee by card on that signed page, and you then call this endpoint again, which then succeeds. This is a fee for the change; it does not take credits or balance. Outside the window there is no fee.

Errors. `422 booking_rejected` when the booking cannot be rescheduled: it is not paid yet (`pending`), it is cancelled or refunded, its session has already started, or the new slot is not free. The message says which. `422 validation_failed` when `date` or `time` is missing or malformed. A booking of another account is `404 not_found`. This call does not take an `Idempotency-Key`.

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:bookings:write`.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

200.description: The rescheduled booking in the standard `data` envelope, with `booking_status` `rescheduled` and the new `start_date` and `end_date`.

402.description: The session is inside the 120 hour late-change window and the late-change fee has not been paid. Error code: `payment_required`. `payment_url` is a signed page where the candidate pays the fee by card; once it is paid, call the endpoint again.

example.message: This training is within 5 days. A reschedule fee applies.

get.description:
Lists the Virtual BLS Training courses that can be booked: each course with its list price, the price your account pays under its own agreement and the length of the session. Only active courses are listed, in name order by default. The list is short and fixed, so one page holds every course.

`cost_inc_vat_pence` is the list price including VAT, in pence. `client_rate_pence` is your account's own rate in pence, or 0 when the account has none. The own rate is charged only when a booking is paid by invoice (`invoice`) or from the money balance (`balance`); a booking paid with a credit or by the candidate is charged at the list price. Take the course `id` from here for `GET /timeslots` and `POST /timeslots/hold`.

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page

get.description:
Lists the movements of the account's wallets, newest first by default: the booking balance (money, in pence) and one credit wallet per course (whole credits). Each row says whether it was a `deposit` or a `withdraw`, which wallet it touched, the amount (always positive; `type` tells added from taken out), whether it is confirmed, a description and, when the movement paid for a booking, the `booking_id`. A booking paid with a credit or from the balance takes one `withdraw` at the moment the booking is made, and a refund puts the credit or the money back as a `deposit`.

Filter by `wallet` (`booking_balance` or a course id such as `12`), by `type`, and by date with `created_from` and `created_to` (a date such as `2026-10-01`; the range runs from the start of the first day to the end of the last day in UTC). Sort by `id` or `created_at` (prefix with `-` for descending). A wallet value that matches none of the account's wallets returns an empty page, not an error. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Only movements of this wallet: `booking_balance` for the money balance, or a course id (for example `12`) for that course's credits. At most 100 characters. A value that matches none of the account's wallets returns an empty page.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only movements of this type: `deposit` (money or credits added) or `withdraw` (money or credits taken out).

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

get.description:
Lists the start times that are free for one course, so that you can choose one to hold. This is the first step of a booking. Each row is a `date` and a `time` in UK local time (not UTC) and the course. Slots start every 15 minutes between 07:00 and 22:00 UK time. The first bookable day is five days from today, and the search looks `months_ahead` months beyond that (2 when you leave it out, up to 12). A slot is free when at least one trainer is free for the whole session and the slot is not already promised to another booking or held by another client.

Send `course_id` (required): an id from `GET /courses`; an unknown course is `422 validation_failed` on `course_id`. Send `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) to see only one day. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25) and can be sorted by `date` or `time`. The list is a snapshot: a slot you see can be taken before you hold it, in which case `POST /timeslots/hold` answers `422 booking_rejected`. An empty list means that nothing is free in the window.

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, held, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `date`, `time`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-date`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: course_id
parameters.description: The course to list free slots for: an `id` from `GET /courses`. Required. An id that does not exist is `422 validation_failed` on `course_id`.

parameters.name: months_ahead
parameters.description: How many months ahead of the first bookable day (five days from today) to search, 1 to 12. When omitted the search covers 2 months. A value outside 1 to 12 is a `422`.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Only slots on this date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, as a UK local date. A date outside the searched window returns an empty list, not an error.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.
