post.description:
Reserves one free timeslot for 30 minutes so that nobody else can book it while you complete the booking. This is the second step: pass the returned `hold_hash` to `POST /bookings` before `expires_at`. The `date` and `time` you send are UK local time and must be a slot that `GET /timeslots` lists as free. The course must be active.

An account may hold one slot at a time. A second hold while one is still live is refused with `409 conflict`, and the error body carries the live hold in a top-level `hold` field (with its `hold_hash`), so you can either book it or release it with `DELETE /timeslots/hold/{hash}` and hold another. A slot that is not free, or a course that is not available, is `422 booking_rejected`. A hold that is not booked simply expires after 30 minutes and no longer blocks the slot. Nothing is charged, sent or emailed, and no webhook event is fired by a hold.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the original hold with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:holds:write`.

201.description: Created. The held slot, in the standard `data` envelope: its `hold_hash`, when it expires and the slot. A repeat of an earlier Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

409.description: Two cases. `conflict`: your account already holds a slot; the body carries the live hold in `hold` (with its `hold_hash`), so book it or release it with `DELETE /timeslots/hold/{hash}` first. `idempotency_conflict`: the `Idempotency-Key` was used before with a different body.

hold.description: On `409 conflict`: the hold your account already has.

example.message: You already have an active slot hold. Release it before requesting a new one.

delete.description:
Releases a hold that you made with `POST /timeslots/hold`, so that the slot becomes free again at once. Use it when the candidate changes their mind before you book, or to replace a hold with another slot (an account may hold one slot at a time). Only a hold of your own account can be released; the hash of a hold that does not exist, has expired and been removed, belongs to another account or has already been booked is `404 not_found`. A booking that was made from the hold is not affected, and nothing is charged or sent.

The answer is `{ "data": { "hold_hash": "...", "released": true } }`. The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:holds:write`.

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

hold_hash.description: The `hold_hash` that was released, as sent in the path.

released.description: Always `true`: the hold was found and removed, and the slot is free again.

get.description:
Lists the account's interview bookings, by default the latest interview first. Each row is a booking as `GET /bookings/{id}` returns it. Abandoned bookings (a card payment that was never completed) are not listed.

Filters: `status` (`pending`, `booked`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled` or `refunded`; send the parameter more than once, as `status[]=booked&status[]=pending`, for several; a value that is not a status is ignored), `interview_status` (one or several of `scheduled`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `no_show`, `incomplete`), `interview_type_id`, `candidate_ref` (must be one of your Hub candidates, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`; a booking matches by the candidate it belongs to, or, when it has no candidate link, by the candidate's email address), `start_date_from` and `start_date_to` (the day of the interview), `created_from` and `created_to` (the day the booking was made; each is a UK calendar day when it is a date alone, an exact instant when it has a time with `Z` or an offset, and UTC when it has a time with no offset), `upcoming=true` (confirmed bookings that have not started yet), `past=true` (bookings whose start has passed) and `search` (part of the candidate's first name, last name or email, at most 100 characters). `sort` accepts `start_date` (the default, latest first), `created_at` and `status`; prefix it with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

Use it to reconcile your own records, and use the webhook events (`clinical-interviews.booking.*`) to hear about changes as they happen. The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. The rows carry the candidate's name, email and phone as entered on the booking: personal data.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `start_date`, `created_at`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-start_date`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text, at most 100 characters: part of the candidate's first name, last name or email address on the booking.

parameters.name: start_date_from
parameters.description: Only interviews on or after this date or time. A date (`2026-10-01`) is a UK calendar day and means the start of that day in UK time; a date and time with a `Z` or an offset (`2026-10-01T09:00:00Z`) is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be after `start_date_to`.

parameters.name: start_date_to
parameters.description: Only interviews on or before this date or time. A date (`2026-10-31`) is a UK calendar day and includes all of it, to the end of that day in UK time; a date and time with a `Z` or an offset is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be before `start_date_from`.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only bookings made on or after this date or time. A date (`2026-10-01`) is a UK calendar day and means the start of that day in UK time (an hour before midnight UTC in summer); a date and time with a `Z` or an offset is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only bookings made on or before this date or time. A date (`2026-10-31`) is a UK calendar day and includes all of it; a date and time with a `Z` or an offset is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only bookings with this status: `pending`, `booked`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled` or `refunded`. Send the parameter more than once (`status[]=booked&status[]=pending`) to match several. Values that are not a status are ignored.

parameters.name: interview_status
parameters.description: Only bookings whose interview is in this state: `scheduled`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `no_show` or `incomplete`. Send the parameter more than once to match several.

parameters.name: interview_type_id
parameters.description: Only bookings of this interview type: an `id` from `GET /interview-types`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only bookings of this candidate: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API. It must be one of your candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`. A booking with no candidate link is matched by the candidate's email address.

parameters.name: upcoming
parameters.description: `true` returns only confirmed bookings (`booked` or `rescheduled`) whose interview has not started yet.

parameters.name: past
parameters.description: `true` returns only bookings whose interview start time has passed, whatever their status.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

// Plain PHP 8.1 or newer with ext-curl and ext-json: no packages. Run: php sample.php
// Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.

/**
 * One HTTP call with curl. Returns [status, raw body].
 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body  a JSON string, or an array with CURLFile values for multipart/form-data
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubHttp(string $method, string $url, array $headers, string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    $curl = curl_init($url);
    curl_setopt_array($curl, [
        CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => $method,
        CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => $headers,
        CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
        CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 60,
    ]);

    if ($body !== null) {
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, $body);
    }

    $raw = curl_exec($curl);

    if ($raw === false) {
        throw new RuntimeException('Network error: '.curl_error($curl));
    }

    return [curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE), $raw];
}

/** Prints the standard error body {error, message, details, request_id} and stops. */
function hubFail(int $status, string $raw): never
{
    $error = json_decode($raw, true);
    fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("HTTP %d %s: %s (request_id %s)\n", $status, $error['error'] ?? 'error', $error['message'] ?? $raw, $error['request_id'] ?? '-'));

    if (! empty($error['details'])) {
        fwrite(STDERR, json_encode($error['details'], JSON_PRETTY_PRINT)."\n");
    }

    exit(1);
}

/** The bearer token: exchanged on first use, renewed from the refresh token when asked (a new exchange if it is refused). */
function hubToken(bool $renew = false): string
{
    global $baseUrl, $apiKey;
    static $tokens = null;
    $json = ['Accept: application/json', 'Content-Type: application/json'];

    if ($renew && $tokens !== null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/refresh", $json, json_encode(['refresh_token' => $tokens['refresh_token']]));
        $tokens = $status === 200 ? json_decode($raw, true) : null;
    }

    if ($tokens === null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/token", $json, json_encode(['api_key' => $apiKey]));

        if ($status !== 200) {
            hubFail($status, $raw);
        }

        $tokens = json_decode($raw, true);
    }

    return $tokens['access_token'];
}

/**

 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}

function hubRequest(string $method, string $path, array $headers = [], string|array|null $body = null): array
{

    }

    return [$status, $raw];

post.description:
Books the interview of a Hub candidate in the slot you hold with `POST /timeslots/hold`. Send the `hold_hash`, the `candidate_ref`, how you pay (`pay_option`) and the agency contact; the candidate's name, email and phone come from the Hub candidate, so create the person first with `POST /api/v2/hub/candidates`. A candidate with no name, email or phone number in Hub is a `422` on `candidate_ref` unless you send `phone`. The interview type and the time are those of the hold.

The booking is confirmed and paid at once (`booking_status` `booked`, `pay_status` `completed`) and the answer is `201` with the booking. With `pay_option` `credits` one credit is taken now, with `balance` the interview's price is taken from the booking money balance now, and with `invoice` nothing is taken now and the interview is invoiced by Healthier Business. The hold is used up. The candidate and the agency contact are emailed a confirmation (the candidate's text message is sent as well), Healthier Business's bookings mailbox is notified, the webhook event `clinical-interviews.booking.created` is sent, and an interviewer is assigned afterwards, so `interviewer` is null in the answer until then.

Send an `Idempotency-Key`. A retry with the same key and the same body within 24 hours returns the original booking with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and books nothing twice; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without a key a retry would find the hold already used and answer `422 booking_refused`.

Refusals. `422 validation_failed` names the field in `details` (for example `candidate_ref`, `agency_contact_email`, or `booking_fields.field_9` for an unanswered booking question). `422 booking_refused` is a business refusal with a message: the hold is unknown or has expired, the way of paying is not available to your account (no credit for the type, a balance that does not cover the price, no invoice terms), or the interview type cannot be found. A short balance is therefore refused, never answered with `402`. `403 client_restricted` means the account is restricted and cannot book.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:bookings:write`; because a `:write` scope does not include its `:read` scope, also give it `clinical-interviews:bookings:read` to read the booking afterwards. The booking holds the candidate's personal data (name, email and phone), which later answers return.

x-credits.description: With pay_option `credits` one credit is taken from this call (the credits of the interview type first, then a pool that covers it, then the all-types credits); with `balance` the interview price is taken from the booking money balance; with `invoice` nothing is taken now. A way of paying the account cannot afford is refused with `422 booking_refused`, never `402`, and nothing is charged.

201.description: The new booking, confirmed and paid. `interviewer` is null until an interviewer is assigned.

Cancels a confirmed interview. The answer is the booking (`booking_status` `cancelled`) plus two fields: `refund_eligible` and `late_cancellation`, which tell you what the cancellation cost. With 24 hours' notice or more the cancellation is free (`late_cancellation` false, `refund_eligible` true): a credit or booking money taken for the interview is given back, a card payment is refunded and an invoiced interview is left off the invoice. post.description:
Moves a confirmed interview to another free slot, given as UK local `date` and `time` (take them from `GET /timeslots` for the booking's interview type). You do not hold the new slot first: it is checked again and taken in one step, so two callers cannot get the same slot. The answer is the booking, with `booking_status` `rescheduled`.

A reschedule clears the interviewer and queues a new assignment (so `interviewer` is null until one is assigned), sets the interview back to `scheduled` and clears `attendance`. It removes the interview from the old interviewer's calendar and tells them, emails the candidate and the agency contact the new time, and sends the webhook event `clinical-interviews.booking.rescheduled` with `previous_start_date`. Only a booking that is paid, confirmed (`booked` or `rescheduled`), not yet started and in the future can be moved.

Notice and cost. With 24 hours' notice or more a move is free. Under 24 hours' notice a move counts as a late cancellation plus a new booking: a booking paid with credits has one free late reschedule (a new credit is taken now and given back when the new interview is completed within 4 weeks of the original date; a second late move stays charged), a booking paid from the money balance is charged again, and an invoiced booking is invoiced again. The charge is taken after the interview has moved and never undoes the move. A card booking (made in Hub, not through the API) cannot be moved under 24 hours' notice: the answer is `422 late_reschedule_not_allowed` and the booking has to be cancelled and booked again.

Errors. `409 slot_taken` means the new slot cannot be booked (it has just been taken, including in the moment of the move, is before the interview type's minimum notice, or no interviewer is free). `422 reschedule_refused` carries the reason in `message` when the booking cannot be moved (it is unpaid, closed, already started or finished, or in the past). `422 late_reschedule_not_allowed` is described above. `404 not_found` is a booking that is not yours. A `date` and `time` that do not exist in UK local time (the hour that is skipped when the clocks go forward) are a `422` on `time`.

Repeating the call is safe. Send an `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key and the same body within 24 hours returns the original answer with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and moves, charges and sends nothing again; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without a key it is safe as well: when the booking is already in the slot you ask for, the answer is `200` with the booking as it is (its status stays as it was), the interviewer is not cleared, no email or webhook event is sent, and nothing is charged. A call that is repeated at the same moment as the first is held back until the first has finished and then finds the booking in the slot.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:bookings:write`.

x-credits.description: Free with 24 hours' notice or more. Under 24 hours' notice a late reschedule is charged as a new booking: a credit booking has one free late reschedule (a new credit is taken now and returned when the new interview is completed within 4 weeks of the original date), later late moves keep the new credit, a balance booking is charged the interview price again and an invoice booking is invoiced again. The charge never blocks the move and never answers `402`: a balance booking is charged the interview price even when the booking money balance is short, so the balance can go below zero, and a credit booking takes a credit even when none is left (as in the Clinical Interviews portal). A repeated call that finds the booking already in the slot charges nothing.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

200.description: Success. The record, in the standard `data` envelope.

get.description:
Returns what the account can pay for interviews with, in the order a booking spends it. `booking_credits` lists the credits held for one interview type each; `interview_type_group_credits` lists the credit pools, which are credits that pay for any of several interview types; `all_interview_types_credits` is the number of credits that pay for any type; and `booking_money_balance_pence` is the booking money balance in pence. A type or pool that holds no credits is not listed. When you book with `pay_option` `credits`, one credit is taken from the narrowest credits that have one: those of the interview type, then a pool that covers it, then the all-types credits.

An account that uses another client's credits sees that client's credit balances here. Credits and money cannot be bought through the API: the answer only reports the balances. get.description:
Lists the movements of the account's credit wallets and of its booking money balance, newest first by default: each deposit (credits or money added) and each withdrawal (an interview paid for, or a charge). A credit movement has `amount` (a number of credits); a money movement has `amount_pence` and `currency` and `amount` is null. `type` says the direction, and `booking_id` names the booking the movement was made for when there is one.

Filters: `wallet` is an interview type id, `all` (the credits that pay for any type), a credit pool key (see `interview_type_group_credits` in `GET /credits`) or `booking_balance`; `type` is `deposit` or `withdraw`; `created_from` and `created_to` bound the date of the movement (a date alone is a UK calendar day; a time with `Z` or an offset is an exact instant; a time with no offset is UTC). `sort` accepts `created_at` (the default, newest first) and `id`; prefix it with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25). An account that uses another client's credits sees that client's credit movements made for its own bookings, plus its own money movements.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only movements made on or after this date or time. A date (`2026-10-01`) is a UK calendar day and means the start of that day in UK time (an hour before midnight UTC in summer); a date and time with a `Z` or an offset is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only movements made on or before this date or time. A date (`2026-10-31`) is a UK calendar day and includes all of it; a date and time with a `Z` or an offset is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Only movements of this wallet: an interview type id (`3`), `all` for the credits that pay for any type, the key of a credit pool (`non_doctor`), or `booking_balance` for the money balance.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only deposits (`deposit`, a wallet grew) or only withdrawals (`withdraw`, a wallet shrank).

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

get.description:
Lists the free start times of one interview type as UK local `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and `time` (`HH:MM`) pairs, earliest first by default (`sort` accepts `date` and `time`; prefix it with `-` for descending). `interview_type_id` is required. By default the slots of the next 2 months are returned; `months_ahead` (1 to 12) widens or narrows that, and `date` limits the answer to one day. Pass the `date` and `time` of a row to `POST /timeslots/hold` to keep the slot while you book it.

A listed slot is not reserved: another booking, or another hold, can take it before you hold it, in which case the hold answers `422 hold_refused`. A slot is listed when an interviewer is free for the whole interview, and no slot is listed that starts sooner than the interview type's minimum notice from now. The list is computed on every call and is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25); a 2 month window holds many rows, so page through it or ask for one `date`. An unknown `interview_type_id` is a `422` on that field.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is held, changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `date`, `time`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-date`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: interview_type_id
parameters.description: The interview type to list slots for: an `id` from `GET /interview-types`. Required. An id that does not exist is a `422` on this field.

parameters.name: months_ahead
parameters.description: How many months ahead to look, 1 to 12. Default 2.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Only slots on this day, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in UK local time.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

post.description:
Keeps one free slot for your account for a few minutes (5 by default; the answer states `expires_in_seconds` and `expires_at`) so that nobody else can book it while you complete the booking. The answer is `201` with the `hold_hash`, which `POST /bookings` takes to book the slot. Nothing is booked, charged, emailed or sent as a webhook by a hold. When the hold runs out it is dropped and the slot is free again; a hold that has run out cannot be booked.

An account holds one slot at a time. While a hold is open, a second hold answers `409 hold_exists` and puts the existing hold (`hold_hash`, `expires_at`, `slot`) in `details`, so you can carry on with it or release it with `DELETE /timeslots/hold/{hash}`. Holds are also limited per account and per internet address: too many open holds answer `429 client_limit` or `429 ip_limit`, opening slots too quickly answers `429 too_fast`, and an address that Healthier Business has blocked answers `403 blocked`. A slot that is no longer free, an interview type that is not available and any other refusal answer `422 hold_refused`. A restricted account answers `403 client_restricted`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key and the same body within 24 hours returns the original hold with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of answering `409 hold_exists` against its own hold. The key and the body must match exactly; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:holds:write`. Because a `:write` scope does not include its `:read` scope, also give the key `clinical-interviews:catalogue:read` to find slots.

201.description: The hold, with the `hold_hash` that books it. The slot stays held until `expires_at`.

delete.description:
Gives a held slot back before it runs out, for example when the candidate changes their mind. `{hash}` is the `hold_hash` of `POST /timeslots/hold`. The slot is free again at once. The answer is `{ "data": { "hold_hash", "released": true } }`. A hold is also released by booking it and by running out, so you only need this call to free a slot you will not book. Nothing is charged, emailed or sent as a webhook.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:holds:write`.

# Needs curl and jq. Set HUB_API_KEY (and HUB_BASE_URL for a sandbox) or replace the placeholders below.
set -eu

BASE_URL="${HUB_BASE_URL:-https://hub.hbcompliance.co.uk}"
API_KEY="${HUB_API_KEY:-hbk_replace_with_your_api_key}"

# 1. Exchange the API key for a bearer token. It lasts 60 minutes: keep it and reuse it.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o token.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE_URL/api/v2/auth/token" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"api_key\": \"$API_KEY\"}")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' token.json)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(jq -r '.access_token' token.json)

# 2. List appraisal types.
STATUS=$(curl -sS -o response.json -w '%{http_code}' -X GET "$BASE_URL/api/v2/clinical-appraisals/appraisal-types?page=1&per_page=25" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json")
if [ "$STATUS" -ge 400 ]; then
  echo "HTTP $STATUS: $(jq -r '[.error, .message, .request_id] | join(" | ")' response.json)" >&2
  jq '.details // empty' response.json >&2
  exit 1
fi
jq . response.json

/**
 * One HTTP call with curl. Returns [status, raw body].
 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body  a JSON string, or an array with CURLFile values for multipart/form-data
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubHttp(string $method, string $url, array $headers, string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    $curl = curl_init($url);
    curl_setopt_array($curl, [
        CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => $method,
        CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => $headers,
        CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
        CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 60,
    ]);

    if ($body !== null) {
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, $body);
    }

    $raw = curl_exec($curl);

    if ($raw === false) {
        throw new RuntimeException('Network error: '.curl_error($curl));
    }

    return [curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE), $raw];
}

/** Prints the standard error body {error, message, details, request_id} and stops. */
function hubFail(int $status, string $raw): never
{
    $error = json_decode($raw, true);
    fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("HTTP %d %s: %s (request_id %s)\n", $status, $error['error'] ?? 'error', $error['message'] ?? $raw, $error['request_id'] ?? '-'));

    if (! empty($error['details'])) {
        fwrite(STDERR, json_encode($error['details'], JSON_PRETTY_PRINT)."\n");
    }

    exit(1);
}

/** The bearer token: exchanged on first use, renewed from the refresh token when asked (a new exchange if it is refused). */
function hubToken(bool $renew = false): string
{
    global $baseUrl, $apiKey;
    static $tokens = null;
    $json = ['Accept: application/json', 'Content-Type: application/json'];

    if ($renew && $tokens !== null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/refresh", $json, json_encode(['refresh_token' => $tokens['refresh_token']]));
        $tokens = $status === 200 ? json_decode($raw, true) : null;
    }

    if ($tokens === null) {
        [$status, $raw] = hubHttp('POST', "{$baseUrl}/api/v2/auth/token", $json, json_encode(['api_key' => $apiKey]));

        if ($status !== 200) {
            hubFail($status, $raw);
        }

        $tokens = json_decode($raw, true);
    }

    return $tokens['access_token'];
}

/**
 * A call with the bearer token; renews the token once on 401 invalid_token. Returns [status, raw body].
 *
 * @param  list<string>  $headers
 * @param  string|array<string, mixed>|null  $body
 * @return array{0: int, 1: string}
 */
function hubRequest(string $method, string $path, array $headers = [], string|array|null $body = null): array
{
    global $baseUrl;
    $send = fn (string $token): array => hubHttp($method, $baseUrl.$path, ['Accept: application/json', 'Authorization: Bearer '.$token, ...$headers], $body);

get.description:
Lists the account's appraisal bookings, by default the newest first. Each row is a booking as `GET /bookings/{id}` returns it. Abandoned bookings (a card payment that was never completed) are not listed.

Filters: `status` (the booking's state, such as `pending`, `booked` or `cancelled`; send the parameter more than once, as `status[]=booked&status[]=pending`, for several; a value that matches no booking returns an empty page), `appraisal_status` (one or several of `pending_docs`, `docs_submitted`, `slot_booked`, `in_progress`, `evaluation_submitted`, `report_ready`, `completed`, `cancelled`; values that are not an appraisal status are ignored), `appraisal_type_id`, `candidate_ref` (must be one of your Hub candidates, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`; a booking matches by the candidate it belongs to, or, when it has no candidate link, by the candidate's email address), `created_from` and `created_to` (the day the booking was made) and `search` (part of the candidate's first name, last name or email, at most 100 characters). `sort` accepts `created_at` (the default, newest first), `start_date` and `status`; prefix it with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

Use it to follow each appraisal through its stages and to find those whose `evaluation_report_available` is true. The key needs the scope `clinical-appraisals:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. The rows carry the candidate's name, email and phone as entered on the booking: personal data.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `created_at`, `start_date`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-created_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text, at most 100 characters: part of the candidate's first name, last name or email address on the booking.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only bookings made on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only bookings made on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only bookings in this state: `pending`, `booked` or `cancelled`. Send the parameter more than once (`status[]=booked&status[]=pending`) to match several. A value that matches no booking gives an empty page.

parameters.name: appraisal_status
parameters.description: Only bookings at this stage: `pending_docs`, `docs_submitted`, `slot_booked`, `in_progress`, `evaluation_submitted`, `report_ready`, `completed` or `cancelled`. Send the parameter more than once to match several. Values that are not a stage are ignored.

parameters.name: appraisal_type_id
parameters.description: Only bookings of this appraisal type: an `id` from `GET /appraisal-types`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only bookings of this candidate: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API. It must be one of your candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`. A booking with no candidate link is matched by the candidate's email address.

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

post.description:
Books an appraisal for a Hub candidate. Send the `appraisal_type_id` (from `GET /appraisal-types`), the `candidate_ref`, who pays and how (`pay_option`), the agency contact and your confirmation that the candidate knows about the video call and the photo ID requirement. The candidate's name, email and phone come from the Hub candidate, so create the person first with `POST /api/v2/hub/candidates`; a candidate with no name, email or phone number in Hub is a `422` on `candidate_ref` unless you send `phone`. There is no slot to hold or choose: the booking starts at `appraisal_status` `pending_docs`, the candidate completes the documentation and then books a slot themselves, and `start_date` stays null until they do.

With `credits`, `balance` or `invoice` the booking is confirmed and paid at once (`booking_status` `booked`): one credit of the type is taken, or the appraisal's price is taken from the booking money balance, or nothing is taken now and the appraisal is invoiced by Healthier Business. The candidate is emailed a request to complete the documentation, the agency contact is told the booking is awaiting the candidate, and Healthier Business's bookings mailbox is notified. With `candidate_pays` the booking stays `pending` and `paid_by` is `candidate`: the candidate is emailed a payment link, the answer carries the same link as `payment_url`, and nothing is taken from your account. In every case the webhook event `clinical-appraisals.booking.created` is sent when the booking is made, and `clinical-appraisals.booking.confirmed` follows when a card payment is received later. A login on the appraisals portal is created for the candidate's email and for the agency's email when they do not have one, with a random password nobody knows; the person gets in through the signed links in the booking emails or the portal's password reset.

Send an `Idempotency-Key`. A retry with the same key and the same body within 24 hours returns the original booking with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and books and charges nothing twice; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without a key a retry books again, and charges again.

Refusals. `422 validation_failed` names the field in `details` (for example `candidate_ref`, `agency_contact_email`, or `video_call_awareness`). `422 booking_refused` is a business refusal with a message: the appraisal type cannot be found or is not active, or the way of paying is not available to your account (no credit for the type, a balance that does not cover the price, no invoice terms). A short balance is therefore refused, never answered with `402`.

The key needs the scope `clinical-appraisals:bookings:write`; because a `:write` scope does not include its `:read` scope, also give it `clinical-appraisals:bookings:read` to read the booking afterwards. The booking holds the candidate's personal data (name, email and phone), which later answers return.

x-credits.description: With pay_option `credits` one credit of the appraisal type is taken by this call; with `balance` the appraisal price is taken from the booking money balance; with `invoice` nothing is taken now; with `candidate_pays` nothing is taken from the account. A way of paying the account cannot afford is refused with `422 booking_refused`, never `402`, and nothing is charged.

201.description: The new booking. With `pay_option` `candidate_pays` it is `pending` and also carries `payment_url`.

get.description:
Returns one booking in full: the candidate (`candidate_ref`, and the name, email and phone entered on the booking), the appraisal type, the appraiser when one has been assigned, the start and end time (null until the candidate has booked a slot), the appraisal stage and its label, the booking and payment statuses, who pays, and whether the evaluation report can be downloaded. `{booking}` is the booking id. A booking that does not exist, that is abandoned, or that belongs to another client answers `404 not_found`. The payment link of a `candidate_pays` booking is only in the answer of `POST /bookings`.

get.description:
Lists the movements of the account's credit wallets and of its booking money balance, newest first by default: each deposit (credits or money added) and each withdrawal (an appraisal paid for). A credit movement has `amount` (a number of credits); a money movement has `amount_pence` and `currency` and `amount` is null. `type` says the direction.

Filters: `wallet` is an appraisal type id or `booking_balance`; `type` is `deposit` or `withdraw`; `created_from` and `created_to` bound the date of the movement. `sort` accepts `created_at` (the default, newest first) and `id`; prefix it with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `clinical-appraisals:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only movements made on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only movements made on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Only movements of this wallet: an appraisal type id (`2`) for the credits of that type, or `booking_balance` for the money balance.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only deposits (`deposit`, a wallet grew) or only withdrawals (`withdraw`, a wallet shrank).

200.description: One page of results in the standard list envelope: `data`, `meta` and `links`.

<?php

// Verify and receive virtual-bls-training.booking.rescheduled. Plain PHP 8.1 or newer, no packages: serve this file as your endpoint.
// Set HUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET (the signing secret shown once when the endpoint was created or rotated).

const REPLAY_WINDOW_SECONDS = 300;

/**
 * The signature is `sha256=` and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of "{X-Hub-Timestamp}.{raw body}" keyed with the secret.
 * Sign the exact bytes received, never a re-encoded array. Returns null when the delivery is genuine, else the reason.
 *
 * @param  array<string, string>  $headers
 */
function verifyHubWebhook(string $rawBody, array $headers, string $secret, ?int $now = null): ?string
{
    $now ??= time();
    $headers = array_change_key_case($headers, CASE_LOWER);
    $timestamp = $headers['x-hub-timestamp'] ?? '';
    $signature = $headers['x-hub-signature'] ?? '';

    if (! ctype_digit($timestamp)) {
        return 'missing or invalid X-Hub-Timestamp';
    }

    if (abs($now - (int) $timestamp) > REPLAY_WINDOW_SECONDS) {
        return 'outside the replay window';
    }

    $expected = 'sha256='.hash_hmac('sha256', $timestamp.'.'.$rawBody, $secret);

    return hash_equals($expected, $signature) ? null : 'signature mismatch';
}

// Your endpoint: reads the raw body, verifies it, then acknowledges with any 2xx status.
$headers = [];

foreach ($_SERVER as $name => $value) {
    if (str_starts_with($name, 'HTTP_X_HUB_')) {
        $headers[strtolower(str_replace('_', '-', substr($name, 5)))] = $value;
    }
}

$rawBody = file_get_contents('php://input');
$problem = verifyHubWebhook($rawBody, $headers, getenv('HUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET') ?: 'replace_with_your_endpoint_signing_secret');

if ($problem !== null) {
    http_response_code(401);
    exit($problem);
}

if (($headers['x-hub-event'] ?? '') !== 'virtual-bls-training.booking.rescheduled') {
    http_response_code(400);
    exit('unexpected event');
}

// A redelivery keeps its X-Hub-Event-Id: store the ids you have handled and skip a repeat.
$envelope = json_decode($rawBody, true, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR); // event_id, event_type, occurred_at, data
error_log($envelope['event_type'].' '.$envelope['event_id']);

http_response_code(200);
echo 'ok';

"""Verify and receive virtual-bls-training.booking.rescheduled. Python 3.9 or newer, standard library only: python webhook.py

Set HUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET (the signing secret shown once when the endpoint was created or rotated).
"""
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import os
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

SECRET = os.environ.get("HUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET", "replace_with_your_endpoint_signing_secret")
REPLAY_WINDOW_SECONDS = 300


def verify_hub_webhook(raw_body, headers, secret=SECRET, now=None):
    """The signature is sha256= and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of "{X-Hub-Timestamp}.{raw body}" keyed with the secret.

    Sign the exact bytes received (never a re-serialised dict). Returns None when genuine, else the reason.
    """
    now = int(time.time()) if now is None else now
    headers = {name.lower(): value for name, value in headers.items()}
    timestamp = headers.get("x-hub-timestamp", "")
    signature = headers.get("x-hub-signature", "")

    if not (timestamp.isascii() and timestamp.isdigit()):
        return "missing or invalid X-Hub-Timestamp"

    if abs(now - int(timestamp)) > REPLAY_WINDOW_SECONDS:
        return "outside the replay window"

    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), timestamp.encode() + b"." + raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

    return None if hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature) else "signature mismatch"


# Your endpoint: reads the raw body, verifies it, then acknowledges with any 2xx status.
seen_event_ids = set()  # use a database in production: a redelivery keeps its X-Hub-Event-Id


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        raw_body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
        problem = verify_hub_webhook(raw_body, dict(self.headers.items()))

        if problem is None and self.headers.get("X-Hub-Event") != "virtual-bls-training.booking.rescheduled":
            problem = "unexpected event"

        if problem is not None:
            self.send_response(401 if problem != "unexpected event" else 400)
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(problem.encode())
            return

        event_id = self.headers.get("X-Hub-Event-Id")

        if event_id not in seen_event_ids:
            seen_event_ids.add(event_id)
            envelope = json.loads(raw_body)  # event_id, event_type, occurred_at, data
            print(envelope["event_type"], envelope["data"])

        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b"ok")


HTTPServer(("", 3000), Handler).serve_forever()

ApiKeyInfo.description: The API key behind the access token you sent: which client it belongs to and what it may do. The secret part of the key is never returned.

client_id.description: The id of the Hub client the key belongs to (the account that is billed and whose data the key can read). The same id is in every portal for the same client.

key.description: The key itself. The secret is never returned: only enough to recognise it.

name.description: The name given to the key on the Developer page of Hub, to tell your keys apart.

prefix.description: The first eight characters of the key (`hbk_` and four more), enough to recognise it on the Developer page. It cannot be used to call the API.

scopes.description: The scopes the key holds, as saved: `{portal}:{resource}:{read|write}` (for example `hub:candidates:read`), `{portal}:*` for a whole portal, or `*` for everything. A `:write` scope also grants the matching `:read` scope. A call that needs a scope the key lacks is `403 insufficient_scope`.

expires_at.description: When the key expires (ISO 8601 UTC), or null if it never does. This is the expiry of the key, not of the token. After it every call and every exchange is `403 key_inactive`.

id.description: The appraisal type id: an integer. Use it as `appraisal_type_id` in `POST /bookings`.

description.description: A short description of the appraisal type: the headline Hub shows for it. Null when none is set.
examples: Annual clinical appraisal for registered nurses, held as a video call.

price_inc_vat_pence.description: The list price of one appraisal including VAT, in pence.

client_rate_pence.description:
The price your account pays for one appraisal, in pence, which can differ from the list price when the account has
its own rate. The account's own rate applies to bookings paid with `balance` or `invoice`; it is not what a credit
is worth.

id.description:
The booking id: an integer that never changes. Use it in `GET /bookings/{id}`, in the report download and as
`booking_id` in webhook events.

candidate_ref.description:
The candidate the appraisal is for: their `candidate_ref` in the Hub core API (`/api/v2/hub/candidates`). A booking
made through this API always belongs to the candidate named in the request. A booking that was made without that
link (an older booking, for example) is matched to your Hub candidate with the same email address; when there is
none, `candidate_ref` is null.

candidate_name.description:
The candidate's full name as entered on the booking (first name and last name joined by a space). This is
personal data: use `candidate_ref` to identify the person in your own system.

candidate_email.description:
The candidate's email address as entered on the booking. The appraisal's emails to the candidate go to this
address.

candidate_phone.description: The candidate's phone number as entered on the booking.

job_role.description: The candidate's job role as entered on the booking; null when none was sent.

nmc_number.description: The candidate's NMC registration number as entered on the booking; null when none was sent.

id.description: The appraisal type id.

appraiser.description: The appraiser who has been given the appraisal; null until one is assigned.

id.description: The appraiser id: an integer.

start_date.description: When the appraisal starts, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z`. It is null until the candidate has booked a slot.

end_date.description: When the appraisal is due to end, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z`. It is null until the candidate has booked a slot.

appraisal_status.description:
Where the appraisal is in its process: `pending_docs` (awaiting the candidate's documents), `docs_submitted`,
`slot_booked`, `in_progress`, `evaluation_submitted` (the appraiser has submitted the evaluation),
`report_ready`, `completed` or `cancelled`. A new booking is `pending_docs`. The evaluation report exists from
`evaluation_submitted` onwards. There is no outcome or pass mark.

appraisal_status_label.description:
The words Hub shows for `appraisal_status`, for example `Awaiting documents` or `Slot booked`. Use
`appraisal_status` in code: the label is for people and can be reworded.

booking_status.description:
The booking's state as recorded: `booked` once it is paid for or arranged, `pending` while a payment is awaited
(a booking the candidate has to pay for), and `cancelled` for a booking that was cancelled. Bookings made through
this API are `booked`, or `pending` with `pay_option` `candidate_pays`. Abandoned bookings are never returned by the
API.

pay_status.description:
The payment state recorded on the booking: `completed` when it is paid for or arranged (credit, balance and
invoice are settled when the booking is made), `pending` while a payment is awaited.

pay_option.description:
How the booking is paid for: `credits`, `balance` (the booking money balance), `inv` (invoice) or `cc` (card).
A booking made with `candidate_pays` has `cc` and `paid_by` `candidate`.

booked_by.description: Who made the booking, as recorded on it. A booking made through this API is `Agency`.

evaluation_report_available.description:
True when the evaluation report exists: `appraisal_status` is `evaluation_submitted`, `report_ready` or
`completed`. Then `GET /bookings/{id}/evaluation-report` returns the PDF.

created_at.description: When the booking was created, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z`.

payment_url.description:
The page where the candidate pays, on the Healthier Business appraisals portal. Present only in the answer of
`POST /bookings` with `pay_option` `candidate_pays`, and not in any later answer: keep it if you need it (the
candidate is also emailed the link).

id.description: The transaction id: an integer that never changes.

type.description:
`deposit` when the wallet grew, `withdraw` when it shrank. The amount is always positive: use `type` for the
direction.

wallet.description:
The wallet the movement belongs to: `bls_{appraisal type id}` for the credits of one appraisal type, or
`booking_balance` for money. It is null when the wallet is not known. To filter, pass the appraisal type id or
`booking_balance` as `wallet`.

is_money.description: True for a movement of the booking money balance, false for credits.

amount.description: The number of credits moved. Null for a money movement.

amount_pence.description: The money moved, in pence. Null for a credit movement.

currency.description: `GBP` for a money movement; null for a credit movement.

created_at.description: When the movement was made, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z`.

booking_credits.description:
The credits held for one appraisal type each. A type with no credits is not listed, so an empty list means the
account holds no credits. Credits of one type pay only for that type.

appraisal_type_id.description: The appraisal type the credits pay for (an `id` of `GET /appraisal-types`).

credits.description: The credits held for that type.

booking_money_balance_pence.description:
The booking money balance in pence. A booking paid with `pay_option` `balance` takes the appraisal's price from
it.

id.description: The Hub client id of the account: the same client id as in the rest of Hub. It is an integer.

name.description: The account name, as it appears on bookings, invoices and emails.

contact_name.description: The name of the account's main contact.

email.description: The account's main email address.

notify_email.description:
The address that receives the account's booking notifications. It is the default `agency_email` of a booking when
none is sent. Null when none is set.

CaStoreBookingBody.description:
`POST /bookings`: books an appraisal for a Hub candidate. There is no slot to hold or choose: the candidate completes
the documentation and books a slot afterwards. The candidate's name, email and phone come from the Hub candidate, not
from this body (`phone` can fill a missing phone number). The service that creates the booking validates the details
again after these rules.

appraisal_type_id.description:
The appraisal type to book: an `id` from `GET /appraisal-types`. A type that does not exist or is not active is
`422 booking_refused`.

candidate_ref.description:
The candidate to book: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API (`/api/v2/hub/candidates`). It must be one of
your candidates, otherwise `422` on `candidate_ref` (never a 404). The candidate needs a name, an email address
and a phone number in Hub (the phone can be sent in `phone` instead), otherwise `422` on `candidate_ref`.

phone.description:
The phone number to put on the booking. Needed only when the Hub candidate has no phone number; when it is sent it
is used instead of the number held in Hub. At most 50 characters.

job_role.description: The candidate's job role, kept on the booking. At most 255 characters. Optional.

nmc_number.description: The candidate's NMC registration number, kept on the booking. At most 50 characters. Optional.

pay_option.description:
Who pays and how. `credits` takes one credit of the appraisal type now; `balance` takes the appraisal's price from
the booking money balance now; `invoice` (or `inv`) adds it to your invoice and takes nothing now;
`candidate_pays` leaves the payment to the candidate, who is emailed a payment link (the booking stays `pending`
until they pay, and the answer carries `payment_url`). A way of paying that is not available to your account (no
credit, balance too low, no invoice terms) is `422 booking_refused`. Card payment by the agency is not offered
through the API.

agency_contact_name.description: The name of the person at your agency who made the booking. At most 255 characters.

agency_contact_email.description:
The email address of that person. The agency's emails about the booking (it is awaiting the candidate's
documentation, and the later steps) go to this address.

agency_email.description:
The agency's own email address kept on the booking. Optional; when it is left out the account's notification email
(`notify_email` in `GET /profile`) is used, and when that is empty the account's main email.

video_call_awareness.description:
Your confirmation that the candidate knows the appraisal is held as a video call. It must be `true`; anything else
is a `422` on this field.

photo_id_awareness.description:
Your confirmation that the candidate knows they must show photo ID at the appraisal. It must be `true`; anything
else is a `422` on this field.

CaStoreBookingBody.title: CaStoreBookingBody

id.description:
The booking id: an integer that never changes. Use it in `GET /bookings/{id}`, in the reschedule and cancel calls and
as `booking_id` in webhook events.

candidate_ref.description:
The candidate the interview is for: their `candidate_ref` in the Hub core API (`/api/v2/hub/candidates`). A booking made
through this API always belongs to the candidate named in the request. A booking that was made without that link
(an older booking, for example) is matched to your Hub candidate with the same email address; when there is none,
`candidate_ref` is null.

candidate_name.description:
The candidate's full name as it was entered on the booking (first name and last name joined by a space).
This is personal data: use `candidate_ref` to identify the person in your own system.

candidate_email.description:
The candidate's email address as entered on the booking. Interview emails (confirmation, reminders, the link to join)
are sent to this address.

candidate_phone.description: The candidate's phone number as entered on the booking.

job_role.description: The candidate's job role as entered on the booking; null when none was sent.

nmc_number.description: The candidate's NMC registration number as entered on the booking; null when none was sent.

id.description: The interview type id.

interviewer.description:
The interviewer who has been given the interview. It is null until one is assigned, and again after a reschedule
(a rescheduled booking is cleared of its interviewer and given a new one for the new time).

id.description: The interviewer id: an integer.

start_date.description:
When the interview starts, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z`. The interview is booked in UK time, so an interview at 11:00
in UK summer time is `10:00:00Z`.

end_date.description: When the interview is due to end, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z`: the start plus the length of the interview type.

booking_status.description:
The booking's state. `pending` is a booking that is waiting for a card payment; `booked` is confirmed and paid for
or arranged; `rescheduled` is confirmed and has been moved at least once; `cancelled` and `refunded` are closed.
Bookings made through this API are `booked` at once. Abandoned bookings are never returned by the API.

interview_status.description:
How the interview itself stands: `scheduled` (not started), `in_progress`, `completed`, `no_show` (the candidate did
not attend) or `incomplete` (the candidate attended but the interview could not go ahead, see `incomplete_reason`).
It can be null for an older booking that has no interview status.

attendance.description:
Whether the candidate attended, recorded by the interviewer: `attended` or `no_show`. It is null until it has been
recorded, and is cleared when the booking is rescheduled.

incomplete_reason.description:
Why an interview ended as incomplete, in the words the interviewer chose from the portal's list of reasons. It is
only set when `interview_status` is `incomplete`; otherwise null.
examples: Candidate had no valid photo ID

video_provider.description:
The video platform the interview is held on, as recorded on the booking (for example `hbmeet`). Null when none is
recorded.

cancelled.description: True when the booking is closed: its `booking_status` is `cancelled`, `abandoned` or `refunded`.

can_reschedule.description:
True when the booking could be moved now: it is `booked` or `rescheduled`, its interview has not started
(`interview_status` is `scheduled` or null) and its start time is in the future. It does not look at the notice
rules of the payment method: a card booking under 24 hours away still answers `422 late_reschedule_not_allowed`.

can_cancel.description:
True when the booking could be cancelled now. It has exactly the same conditions as `can_reschedule`. Whether the
cancellation is free or late depends on the notice given: see `POST /bookings/{id}/cancel`.

pay_status.description:
The payment state of the booking, as recorded on it: `completed` once the booking is paid for or arranged (credit,
balance or invoice are settled when the booking is made), `pending` while a card payment is awaited, and
`refunded` after a card payment has been refunded. A credit or balance charge that is given back on cancellation
does not change it.

pay_option.description:
How the booking is paid for: `credits`, `balance` (the booking money balance), `inv` (invoice) or `cc` (card).
Bookings made through this API use `credits`, `balance` or `inv`.

booked_by.description: Who made the booking, as recorded on it. A booking made through this API is `Agency`.

zoom.description:
The Zoom meeting details stored on the booking, for a booking that was held on Zoom. Every field is null for a
booking that has no Zoom meeting. The join link and the password are sensitive: do not log them.

meeting_id.description: The Zoom meeting id; null when the booking has no Zoom meeting.

join_link.description: The link a participant joins the Zoom meeting with; null when the booking has no Zoom meeting. Sensitive: do not log it.

password.description: The Zoom meeting password; null when the booking has no Zoom meeting. Sensitive: do not log it.

interview_report_available.description:
True when `interview_status` is `completed`, which is when `GET /bookings/{id}/interview-report` normally has a PDF
to return. It does not take the retention period into account: an old report can still answer `410 report_expired`.

created_at.description: When the booking was created, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z`.

refund_eligible.description:
Present only in the answer of `POST /bookings/{id}/cancel` that cancelled the booking, and in no other answer. True
when the cancellation was made with 24 hours' notice or more, so the charge for the interview is given back: a
credit or booking money is returned, a card payment is refunded, and an invoiced interview is left off the
invoice. False for a late cancellation.

late_cancellation.description:
Present only in the answer of `POST /bookings/{id}/cancel` that cancelled the booking, and in no other answer. True
when the interview was cancelled under 24 hours before it started: nothing is given back and an invoiced
interview is still invoiced. False when the notice was 24 hours or more.

id.description: The transaction id: an integer that never changes.

type.description:
`deposit` when the wallet grew, `withdraw` when it shrank. The amount is always positive: use `type` for the
direction.

wallet.description:
The wallet the movement belongs to: `bls_{interview type id}` for the credits of one interview type, `bls_any` for
the all-types credits, `bls_{pool key}` for a pool, or `booking_balance` for money. It is null when the wallet is
not known. To filter, pass the interview type id, `all`, the pool key or `booking_balance` as `wallet`.

is_money.description: True for a movement of the booking money balance, false for credits.

amount.description: The number of credits moved. Null for a money movement.

amount_pence.description: The money moved, in pence. Null for a credit movement.

currency.description: `GBP` for a money movement; null for a credit movement.

booking_id.description: The booking the movement was made for, when it was made for one; otherwise null.

created_at.description: When the movement was made, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z`.

booking_credits.description:
The credits held for one interview type each. A type with no credits is not listed, so an empty list means the
account holds no type-specific credits. Credits that pay for any type are in `all_interview_types_credits`.

interview_type_id.description: The interview type the credits pay for (an `id` of `GET /interview-types`).

credits.description: The credits held for that type.

interview_type_group_credits.description:
The credit pools: credits that pay for an interview of any of several interview types. Only pools that hold
credits are listed. A booking spends the narrowest credits first: those of its own type, then a pool that covers
it, then the all-types credits.

pool.description: The pool's key. It is the value `wallet` takes in `GET /credits/transactions` to list the pool's movements.

interview_type_ids.description: The interview types the pool's credits can pay for.

all_interview_types_credits.description:
The credits that pay for an interview of any type. They are spent after the credits of the type and of its
pools.

booking_money_balance_pence.description:
The booking money balance in pence. A booking paid with `pay_option` `balance` takes the interview's price from
it.

hold_hash.description:
The hold's token: a string of 32 characters. Send it as `hold_hash` to `POST /bookings`, or in the path of
`DELETE /timeslots/hold/{hash}` to release the slot.

expires_at.description:
When the hold runs out, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z`. After that the slot is free for anyone and booking with the
hold answers `422 booking_refused`.

date.description: The day of the slot as `YYYY-MM-DD`, in UK local time.

time.description: The start time as `HH:MM`, in UK local time.

id.description: The interview type id.

interview_type.description: The interview type of the slot.

expires_in_seconds.description:
How long a hold lasts, in seconds, counted from when it was made. Present in the answer that creates a hold
(five minutes unless Healthier Business has set another time), and not in the hold of `hold_exists`.

hold_hash.description: The hash of the hold that was released.

released.description: Always `true`: a hold that does not exist or is not yours answers `404 not_found` instead.

CiHoldTimeslotBody.description: `POST /timeslots/hold`: the slot to hold. Take `date` and `time` from a row of `GET /timeslots`; both are UK local time.

interview_type_id.description:
The interview type to hold a slot for: an `id` from `GET /interview-types`. An id that does not exist is a `422` on
this field.

date.description: The day of the slot, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in UK local time: the `date` of a row of `GET /timeslots`.

time.description: The start time of the slot, `HH:MM` (24 hour clock), in UK local time: the `time` of a row of `GET /timeslots`.

id.description: The interview type id: an integer. Use it as `interview_type_id` in `GET /timeslots` and `POST /timeslots/hold`.

price_inc_vat_pence.description: The list price of one interview including VAT, in pence.

client_rate_pence.description:
The price your account pays for one interview, in pence, which can differ from the list price when the account has
its own rate. The account's own rate applies to bookings paid with `balance` or `invoice`; it is not what a credit
is worth.

duration_hours.description:
How long one interview of this type lasts, in hours (decimals are possible: `1.5` is an hour and a half). It
decides the interview's `end_date`.

id.description: The Hub client id of the account: the same client id as in the rest of Hub. It is an integer.

name.description: The account name, as it appears on bookings, invoices and emails.

contact_name.description: The name of the account's main contact.

email.description: The account's main email address.

notify_email.description:
The address that receives the account's booking notifications. It is the default `agency_email` of a booking
when none is sent. Null when none is set.

CiRescheduleBookingBody.description:
`POST /bookings/{id}/reschedule`: the new slot. Take `date` and `time` from a row of `GET /timeslots` for the booking's
interview type; both are UK local time. A reschedule does not take a hold: the slot is checked and taken in one step.

date.description: The new day, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in UK local time: the `date` of a free slot from `GET /timeslots`.

time.description: The new start time, `HH:MM` (24 hour clock), in UK local time: the `time` of a free slot from `GET /timeslots`.
