CiStoreBookingBody.description:
`POST /bookings`: books a held slot for a Hub candidate. The candidate's name, email and phone come from the Hub
candidate, not from this body (`phone` can fill a missing phone number). The booking questions the client or Healthier
Business has set up for the interview type are answered in `booking_fields`; the service that creates the booking
validates those answers after these rules.

hold_hash.description:
The hold to book: the `hold_hash` returned by `POST /timeslots/hold`. It must be a hold of your account that has not
run out; a hold that is unknown or expired is `422 booking_refused`. The hold is used up by the booking.

candidate_ref.description:
The candidate to book: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API (`/api/v2/hub/candidates`). It must be one of
your candidates, otherwise `422` on `candidate_ref` (never a 404). The candidate needs a name, an email address
and a phone number in Hub (the phone can be sent in `phone` instead), otherwise `422` on `candidate_ref`.

phone.description:
The phone number to put on the booking. Needed only when the Hub candidate has no phone number; when it is sent it
is used instead of the number held in Hub. At most 50 characters.

job_role.description: The candidate's job role, kept on the booking and shown in the report. At most 255 characters. Optional.

nmc_number.description: The candidate's NMC registration number, kept on the booking. At most 50 characters. Optional.

nursing_band.description: The candidate's nursing band, kept on the booking. At most 50 characters. Optional.

pay_option.description:
How you pay for the interview. `credits` takes one credit now (the credits of the interview type first, then a
pool that covers it, then the all-types credits); `balance` takes the interview's price from the booking money
balance now; `invoice` (or `inv`) adds it to your invoice and takes nothing now. A way of paying that is not
available to your account (no credit, balance too low, no invoice terms) is `422 booking_refused`. Card payment
is not offered through the API.

agency_contact_name.description:
The name of the person at your agency who made the booking. At most 255 characters. The interview emails to the
agency are addressed to this contact.

agency_contact_email.description:
The email address of that person. The agency's booking confirmation and its later emails (reschedule, cancellation,
outcome) go to this address.

agency_email.description:
The agency's own email address kept on the booking. Optional; when it is left out the account's notification email
(`notify_email` in `GET /profile`) is used.

agency_contact_cc.description:
Extra addresses that receive a copy of the agency's emails, separated by single commas: at most 10 distinct, valid
addresses and 500 characters. A stray comma or an invalid address is a `422` on this field. Optional.

booking_fields.description:
Answers to the booking questions set up for the interview type, as an object keyed `field_{question id}` (for
example `{"field_9": "Yes"}`). A question that is required (or required because of another answer) and is not
answered is a `422` on `booking_fields.field_{id}`. An answer to a radio or select question must be one of its
options. The questions are the ones shown on the Hub booking page; the API does not list them. Leave it out when
the interview type has no required questions.

CiStoreBookingBody.title: CiStoreBookingBody

date.description: The day of the slot as `YYYY-MM-DD`, in UK local time. Send it as `date` to hold the slot.

time.description: The start time as `HH:MM`, in UK local time (not UTC). Send it as `time` to hold the slot.

interview_type.description: The interview type the slot is free for.

id.description: The interview type id.

DrCreateWorkerBody.description: The worker to monitor: who they are and what to check. Send JSON, or `multipart/form-data` (`DrCreateWorkerUploadBody`) when you upload a passport image or a document. `first_name`, `last_name`, `email` and `consent_given` are required, and at least one of `dbs_certificate_number` and `rtw_document_type`. A field that is not listed is ignored.

first_name.description: The worker's first name, at most 255 characters.

last_name.description: The worker's last name, at most 255 characters.

email.description: The worker's email address, at most 255 characters. Required.

phone.description: The worker's telephone number, free text, at most 255 characters.

date_of_birth.description: The worker's date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`, before today. Required when `dbs_certificate_number` is sent (the DBS check needs it, otherwise `422` on this field). Also send it for a share code worker: the Home Office check needs it, and a check without it ends with an error.

profession.description: The worker's profession in your own words, at most 255 characters.

compliance_officer_name.description: The person in your organisation responsible for the worker's compliance, at most 255 characters.

monitoring_start_date.description: The date monitoring starts, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Left out, it is today.

consent_given.description: Must be true: the worker has agreed to be monitored. The call is refused with `422` on this field otherwise. Hub records the moment you made the call as the time consent was given.

notes.description: Free text notes about the worker, at most 5000 characters.

dbs_certificate_number.description: The 12 digit DBS certificate number, to enrol the worker for the DBS Update Service. It must not already be monitored for your account. Send this, `rtw_document_type`, or both: sending neither is `422` on this field.

dbs_surname.description: The surname the DBS Update Service is asked about, at most 255 characters. Required when `dbs_certificate_number` is sent.

dbs_check_frequency.description: How often the DBS status is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Left out, the account's default for DBS applies (`monthly` when the account has none).

rtw_document_type.description: The document the right to work check is based on, to enrol the worker for right to work. One of: `uk_passport`, `irish_passport`, `irish_passport_card`, `share_code`, `uk_birth_certificate`, `irish_birth_certificate`, `uk_adoption_certificate`, `british_citizenship_certificate`, `immigration_status_document`, `passport_with_endorsement`. A passport type (`uk_passport`, `irish_passport`, `irish_passport_card`) needs `rtw_passport_image` and is read from the image; `share_code` needs `rtw_share_code` and is checked against the Home Office service; every other type needs `rtw_document_file` and is stored for manual handling (it is not verified automatically).

rtw_share_code.description: The Home Office right to work share code: three groups of three letters or digits separated by single spaces, like `ABC DEF GHI`. Required when `rtw_document_type` is `share_code`; it is stored in upper case. A share code is assumed valid for 90 days from the day it is entered.

rtw_check_frequency.description: How often the right to work status is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Left out, the account's default for right to work applies (`monthly` when the account has none).

allOf.description: The files that go with the form fields.

rtw_passport_image.description: An image of the passport, required when `rtw_document_type` is `uk_passport`, `irish_passport` or `irish_passport_card`. An image file, at most 10 MB. Hub reads the passport from the image when the right to work check runs.

rtw_document_file.description: The document, required when `rtw_document_type` is a type other than a passport or `share_code`. `jpg`, `jpeg`, `png` or `pdf`, at most 10 MB. It is stored for manual handling and not verified automatically.

id.description: The check id. Use it with `GET /evidence/dbs/{check}` and `GET /dbs-checks/{check}/raw-data`.

status.description: The status the Update Service returned: `BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO`, `NON_BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO`, `NEW_INFO` or `NO_MATCH_FOUND`. Null when the check did not get a status (see `result`).

result.description: Whether the check itself worked: `success`, `rejected` (the service answered with a result other than success) or `error` (the number was malformed or the service could not be reached). Only a `success` check changes the worker's DBS status.

has_evidence_pdf.description: True when a certificate PDF was generated for this check: download it with `GET /evidence/dbs/{check}`.

type.description: What the file is: `dbs_certificate` (the PDF generated by a DBS check), `rtw_screenshot` (the screenshot of a right to work check), `passport` (the passport image uploaded when the worker was added) or `document` (the document file uploaded when the worker was added). The first two exist once per check; the last two once per worker.

check_id.description: The id of the DBS or right to work check that produced the file; null for the uploaded `passport` and `document`.

checked_at.description: When the check ran; null for the uploaded `passport` and `document`.

download_url.description: The absolute address that downloads the file: `GET /evidence/dbs/{check}`, `GET /evidence/rtw/{check}` or `GET /workers/{id}/evidence/{passport|document}`. It needs the same bearer token as every other call: it is not a public link.

worker_ids.description: The ids of the workers to change, 1 to 500 (repeated ids count once). Every id must be a worker of your account in this portal, otherwise nothing is changed and the call is `422 workers_not_found`.

DrMonitoringSettingsBody.description: The monitoring settings to change. Send at least one field; a field you leave out keeps its value.

check_frequency.description: How often the worker is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. In DBS & Right To Work it sets every track the worker is enrolled for, unless `dbs_check_frequency` or `rtw_check_frequency` names that track.

monitoring_start_date.description: The date monitoring starts, `YYYY-MM-DD`; send null to clear it.

is_active.description: Whether the worker is monitored. False stops scheduled checks and clears every next check date; true again reschedules each track from its frequency.

dbs_check_frequency.description: How often the DBS status is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Only applies to a worker enrolled for DBS; wins over `check_frequency` for the DBS track.

rtw_check_frequency.description: How often the right to work status is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Only applies to a worker enrolled for right to work; wins over `check_frequency` for the right to work track.

id.description: The check id. Use it with `GET /evidence/rtw/{check}` and `GET /rtw-checks/{check}/raw-data`.

status.description: What the check found: `has_right` or `no_right`. Null when the check did not reach a result (see `result`).

method.description: How the check was made: `playwright` (the Home Office share code service was opened and read), `openai` (a passport image was read) or `manual` (the document type is not verified automatically).

result.description: Whether the check itself worked: `success` or `error`. A document type that is not verified automatically always gives `error`. Only a `success` check changes the worker's right to work status.

expiry_date.description: The date the right to work ends, `YYYY-MM-DD`, as this check found it; null for a permanent right or when none was found.

has_screenshot.description: True when a screenshot of the result was captured: download it with `GET /evidence/rtw/{check}`.

rtw_share_code.description: The new Home Office right to work share code: three groups of three letters or digits separated by single spaces, like `ABC DEF GHI`. Stored in upper case. Required.

id.description: The worker id: an integer that never changes. Use it in every `/workers/{id}` path and as `worker_id` in alerts and webhooks.

candidate_ref.description: The `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid) of the Hub candidate this worker was linked to. It is null for every worker created through this API, an import or the Hub pages; it is filled only when Hub staff linked the worker. It is read only.

last_name.description: The worker's last name. It is the surname the DBS Update Service is asked about unless `dbs.surname` is set.

email.description: The worker's email address; null when none was given.

phone.description: The worker's telephone number, free text; null when none was given.

date_of_birth.description: The worker's date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`. The DBS Update Service check needs it, so it is required for a worker enrolled with a DBS certificate; null when none was given.

profession.description: The worker's profession in your own words, free text; null when none was given.

is_active.description: True while the worker is monitored. An inactive worker is not checked on schedule, has no next check date and a manual check on it is refused (`verification_refused`).

consent_given.description: True when the worker has agreed to be monitored. A worker created through this API always has it true; a worker brought in by an import can have it false.

monitoring_start_date.description: The date monitoring starts, `YYYY-MM-DD`. A worker created without one starts on the day it was created.

notes.description: Free text notes you keep about the worker, at most 5000 characters; null when there are none.

compliant.description: True when every track the worker is enrolled for is in good standing: the DBS status is `BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO` (if enrolled for DBS) and the right to work status is `has_right` (if enrolled for right to work). A track that has not been checked yet is not in good standing, so a new worker is false until its first checks complete.

dbs.description: The DBS track; null when the worker is not enrolled for the DBS Update Service.

certificate_number.description: The DBS certificate number with all but the last four digits replaced by `*`. The full number is never returned by the worker endpoints.

surname.description: The surname sent to the DBS Update Service with the certificate number; null when none was stored (the worker's last name is used then).

status.description: The status the Update Service returned at the last check: `BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO` (clear), `NON_BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO` (the certificate held information, no new information since), `NEW_INFO` (new information is available) or `NO_MATCH_FOUND`. Null until a check has completed.

check_frequency.description: How often the DBS status is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Change it with `PATCH /workers/{id}/monitoring-settings`.

last_checked_at.description: When the DBS status was last checked; null until the first check.

next_check_due_at.description: When the next DBS check is due; null for an inactive worker and for a worker not yet scheduled.

rtw.description: The right to work track; null when the worker is not enrolled for right to work.

document_type.description: The document the right to work check is based on: `uk_passport`, `irish_passport`, `irish_passport_card`, `share_code`, `uk_birth_certificate`, `irish_birth_certificate`, `uk_adoption_certificate`, `british_citizenship_certificate`, `immigration_status_document` or `passport_with_endorsement`. status_label.description: The status as a person reads it: `Has right to work`, `No right to work`, or `Not checked` while `status` is null.

expiry_date.description: The date the right to work ends, `YYYY-MM-DD`, as the last check found it; null for a permanent right or when none was found.

share_code_provided_at.description: The date the current share code was entered, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null when the worker has no share code. Entering a new code (`PUT /workers/{id}/share-code`) sets it to today.

share_code_expires_at.description: The date the share code is assumed to stop working, `YYYY-MM-DD`: 90 days after `share_code_provided_at`. The Home Office service never reports a share code's expiry, so this is an assumption. Null unless `document_type` is `share_code`.

share_code_stale.description: True for a share code worker whose code is older than 90 days: checks have stopped until a new code is entered with `PUT /workers/{id}/share-code`.

check_frequency.description: How often the right to work status is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`.

last_checked_at.description: When the right to work status was last checked; null until the first check.

next_check_due_at.description: When the next right to work check is due; null for an inactive worker and for a worker not yet scheduled.

recent_rtw_checks.description: The ten latest right to work checks, newest first; empty when the worker is not enrolled for right to work. The full history is `GET /workers/{id}/verification?track=rtw`.

recent_alerts.description: The ten latest DBS and right to work alerts of the worker (types starting `dbs_` or `rtw_`), newest first, acknowledged or not.

Error.description: The one error body of the v2 API.

error.description: A stable snake_case code to program against, for example `not_found` or `insufficient_scope`.

message.description: A sentence for a person. It never contains an exception text, class name, file or query.

details.description: Only present when there is something to point at: on a 422, each field mapped to its messages.

request_id.description: The id of this request, the same as the `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it to support.

required.description: On `402 insufficient_credits` where the portal reports it at top level: the credits the action needs.

available.description: On `402 insufficient_credits` where the portal reports it at top level: the credits the account has.

payment_url.description: On `402 payment_required`: where the candidate pays.

candidate_ref.description: The uuid that identifies this person in every portal API. Use it in paths and filters of the other APIs.

name.description: The candidate's full name as Hub shows it.

email.description: The candidate's email address. It is unique within the client.

phone.description: The candidate's phone number.

roles.description: The roles the candidate holds (up to 10).

candidate_reference.description: The client's own reference for the candidate (the Candidate reference field of the Hub form).

compliance_officer.description: The name of the client's compliance officer for this candidate.

is_active.description: True when the candidate is active; false when they were made inactive.

compliance_status.description: The candidate's overall compliance: `compliant`, `expiring_soon`, `expired`, `pending` (something is still outstanding) or `na` (nothing applies).

next_expiry_date.description: The date the earliest expiring item runs out (`YYYY-MM-DD`); null when nothing expires.

added_at.description: When the candidate was added to Hub.

updated_at.description: When the candidate was last changed.

added_at.description: When the candidate was added to Hub.

updated_at.description: When the candidate was last changed.

compliance.description: How many of the candidate's items are in each state.

services.description: The candidate's service with each portal: one entry per Hub service. A service the candidate does not have is `not_required`.

management.description: Who manages the service: Healthier Business (`hb`), the client (`client`) or nobody (`not_required`).

status.description: The service's compliance status; `na` when the service is not required.

completed_at.description: The date the service was completed (`YYYY-MM-DD`), or null.

next_expiry_date.description: The date the service next expires (`YYYY-MM-DD`), or null.

portal_id.description: The id the portal itself uses for the candidate's record (the booking, request, worker or reference request last synced; for Online Training the HB Portal candidate id), or null.

key.description: The alert's id. Send it as `key` to `POST /alerts/dismiss` to dismiss it. It stays the same while the request keeps its outcome.

type.description: Which outcome raised the alert: `rejected` (the request was rejected and must be resubmitted) or `not_fit` (the assessment returned a fail letter).

severity.description: How serious the alert is. Both alert types are `critical`.

status_label.description: The outcome as a person reads it, for example `Rejected`.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid); null only until Hub has synced the candidate.

candidate_name.description: The candidate's full name, or `Unknown candidate`.

description.description: What happened. For a rejection it is the reviewer's note, or `Request rejected: resubmission needed.` when there is none. For not fit it says the assessment returned a fail letter.

clearance.description: The name of the clearance type of the request.

request_id.description: The request id (see `GET /requests/{id}`); null for a questionnaire that has no request.

submission_id.description: The id of the completed questionnaire the outcome belongs to.

at.description: When the outcome was recorded (the questionnaire's completion time).

fieldset.description: The heading of the group of questions, as on the questionnaire.

items.description: The answers in this group, in questionnaire order. Each has the question `label` and the `value` given. A signature answer also has `image`, a PNG data URL. This is health data.

request_id.description: The request the answers were sent for. It does not change.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate the answers are for.

form.description: The shortcode of the questionnaire that was submitted.

submission_id.description: The id of the submitted questionnaire (the candidate's submission). It is the `submission_id` of the request in `GET /requests/{id}` once the first form of the request is in.

status.description: The client status of the request after this call: `submitted` once the request's questionnaire is in, `awaiting_candidate` while another form of the request still has to be sent.

status_label.description: The status as a person reads it.

forms_remaining.description: Shortcodes of the request's forms that still have to be sent; empty when every form has been sent.

request_complete.description: True when every form of the request has been sent (`forms_remaining` is empty).

documents.description: How many supporting documents were stored with the questionnaire.

submitted_by.description: Who sent the questionnaire: always `client_api` here, a client sending it through the API on the candidate's behalf. The same value is `submitted_by` in the `request.questionnaire_completed` webhook and in `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's Hub uuid, the same value as `candidate_ref` in the Hub core API; null only for a candidate Hub has not synced yet.

email.description: The candidate's email address.

role.description: The candidate's job role, else their position.

forms.description: How many Occupational Health questionnaires are assigned to the candidate.

has_forms.description: True when at least one questionnaire is assigned, so an online request can be made for them.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's Hub uuid, the same value as `candidate_ref` in the Hub core API; null only for a candidate Hub has not synced yet.

role.description: The candidate's job role, else their position.

has_forms.description: True when at least one questionnaire is assigned, so an online request can be made for them.

status.description: The candidate's account status in Occupational Health as stored (`activated` once they have activated their account).

history.description: The candidate's requests that have a questionnaire submission, newest first, as request rows (the same fields as `GET /requests`). Requests still waiting for the candidate are found with `GET /requests?candidate_ref=`.

id.description: The clearance type id. Send it as `clearance_type_id` to `POST /requests`.

name.description: The name of the clearance type.

needs_immunisations.description: True when a new starter's request for this type needs immunisation evidence, so `imms_method` is required.

has_scope_choice.description: True when a new starter may choose full or temporary clearance (`scope`).

has_online_form.description: True when Hub has a questionnaire the candidate can complete online for this type; otherwise the questionnaire is on paper.

credits.description: How many whole credits the package adds.

price_pence.description: The price before VAT, in pence.

vat_pence.description: The VAT in pence. Occupational Health is not charged VAT, so this is 0.

per_credit_pence.description: The price of one credit, in pence.

id.description: The id of the ledger entry.

description.description: What the movement was, for example `Credits purchased` or `New starter request`.

note.description: An extra note on the movement, if any.

amount.description: The credits moved, always positive. `is_credit` tells added from used.

OhSubmitAnswersBody.description: The fields of `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`: the answers to one questionnaire, and its supporting documents when it needs them. Send `multipart/form-data` (needed for files; write the answers as `answers[key]=value`, and a list as `answers[key][]=value`); a JSON body `{ "answers": { "key": value } }` also works when no files are sent, and is the easier way to send structured answers. The keys and the shape of each answer come from `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`.

answers.description: The answers, an object of question `key` to answer. Required (send an empty object when every question is optional and you have no answers). Take the keys and the shape of each answer from `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire` (`answer_format`): a text or a choice is a string, a tick box is true or false, a multiple choice is a list of option values, a date range is two dates, a rating grid is an object of row to column, a repeating group is a list of rows and a signature is a PNG data URL. Send every question that is shown; a question left out counts as unanswered, and a required one then fails with `422` on `answers.{key}`. A key that is not a question of the questionnaire is `422` as well. No defaults are filled in for you. With `multipart/form-data` send `answers[key]=value` and `answers[key][]=value` for a list.

documents.description: Supporting documents for the questionnaire, up to 20 files. Needed (at least one) when the questionnaire says `documents_required` in `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`; not accepted when the account does not allow uploads (`422` on `documents`). Send as `multipart/form-data` (`documents[]`). Allowed types are JPG, PNG and PDF, up to 8 MB each: the limits are in `documents.upload` of the questionnaire answer. The files are stored with the candidate's submission exactly like the ones a candidate uploads.

Only `booked` and `rescheduled` hold a seat.

address.description: The venue address as one text.

training_event_id.description: The id of the session (training event) the booking is on. It changes when the booking is rescheduled. Use it with `GET /training-events/{event}`.

start_date.description: When the session starts. An instant in UTC with a `Z`: the session's UK local time converted to UTC. In British Summer Time that is an hour earlier than the clock in the UK (a 09:00 session on 7 July is `2026-07-07T08:00:00Z`), in winter it is the same (a 09:00 session on 7 November is `2026-11-07T09:00:00Z`).

end_date.description: When the session ends. An instant in UTC with a `Z`: the session's UK local time converted to UTC. In British Summer Time that is an hour earlier than the clock in the UK (a 09:00 session on 7 July is `2026-07-07T08:00:00Z`), in winter it is the same (a 09:00 session on 7 November is `2026-11-07T09:00:00Z`).

booking_status.description: The state of the booking: `pending` (created but not yet paid or confirmed, for example a candidate-pays booking waiting for the candidate), `booked` (confirmed and holding a seat), `rescheduled` (moved to another session; it still holds a seat), `cancelled` (cancelled, nothing was refunded to the payer), `refunded` (cancelled and a refund was made to the original payment method: booking credit or balance returned to the account, or a card refund; see `refund` on `GET /bookings/{booking}`), or `abandoned` (a `pending` booking that was never paid and was closed by the scheduled housekeeping). Only `booked` and `rescheduled` hold a seat.

pay_status.description: The payment state recorded on the booking. `completed` once payment is complete (credits, balance and invoice bookings are completed when they are created), `refunded` after a refund, and null while payment is outstanding. Other values can occur for bookings paid through other flows.

pay_option.description: How the booking is paid for: `credits` (one booking credit), `balance` (the booking balance), `inv` (invoiced), `cc` (by card, including a candidate-pays booking) or `free` (a free booking granted to the account).

booked_by.description: Who made the booking, as recorded on it: `Agency` for a booking made by the account (including through this API). Bookings made another way can carry another value.

cost_pence.description: The price recorded on the booking, in integer pence, including VAT. It is the price at booking time; it does not show what was actually charged to credits, balance or a card.

attendance.description: The attendance result recorded for the booking's first training day: `passed`, `present` or `absent`. Null when none is recorded yet. Use `certificate_available` to see whether any day was attended.

certificate_available.description: True when any recorded training day is `passed` or `present`: the certificate can then be downloaded with `GET /bookings/{booking}/certificate`. The webhook event `practical-training.booking.certificate_available` is sent when this becomes true.

created_at.description: When the booking was made: an instant in UTC with a `Z`.

trainer.description: The trainer assigned to the session, or null when none is assigned.

id.description: The trainer id.

refund.description: What was paid back when the booking was cancelled, or null when nothing was (a booking that is not cancelled or refunded, an invoice or free booking, a cancellation inside 48 hours of the session, or a card payment that was not refundable). A refunded booking always has it. It goes back to the original payment method and never shows card details.

method.description: Where the money went: `credits` (booking credit returned to the account's credits for the course), `balance` (the price returned to the booking balance) or `card` (refunded to the card that paid).

amount_pence.description: The amount refunded in integer pence, for `balance` and `card`. Null for `credits`.

credits.description: The credits returned, for `credits` (for example `1`); null for `balance` and `card`.

partial.description: True when a card was refunded only part of what it paid (20% when the candidate had already used the online training).

payment_url.description: The link the candidate pays through: a signed address that opens the payment page for this booking. Present only in the answer of `POST /bookings` when `pay_option` is `candidate_pays`; it is not returned by `GET /bookings/{booking}` or in lists.

id.description: The invitation id. Use it with `GET /booking-invites/{invite}` and `DELETE /booking-invites/{invite}`.

candidate_ref.description: The Hub `candidate_ref` of the Hub candidate of this account who has the invited email address. Null when the account has no such Hub candidate.

candidate_name.description: The invited candidate's name as it was saved on the invitation (the Hub candidate's name at the time).

status.description: The state of the invitation: `unsent` (made but not sent), `waiting` (sent, not yet used) or `used` (the candidate booked).

course_id.description: The course the invitation is for: the course set for the account. The candidate chooses a session of this course.

contact_name.description: The contact at the account who is copied in on the invitation email. Null when none was given.

contact_email.description: The email address of that contact. Null when none was given.

url.description: The candidate's one-time booking link. Present only while the link still works (it has not been used and has not expired); otherwise null. Treat it as a secret: whoever has it can book the place.

expires_at.description: When the link stops working: an instant in UTC with a `Z`. Null while the invitation has not been sent. After a withdrawal the invitation is no longer returned.

booking_id.description: The booking the candidate made with the link, once the invitation is `used`; otherwise null.

created_at.description: When the invitation was made: an instant in UTC with a `Z`.

booking_url.description: The public booking page address to give to candidates so they book on this account. Null when the account has no Sage contact id.

sage_contact_id.description: The account's Sage contact id, from which the booking address is built. Null when the account has none.

id.description: The course id. Use it as `course_id` when you filter sessions and bookings.

client_rate_pence.description: The price this account pays for one place on the course, in integer pence. `0` when the account has no rate of its own for the course (the session's own price then applies; see `cost_inc_vat_pence` on a session).

duration_hours.description: The length of the course in hours: the number of days multiplied by the hours per day. It can be fractional.

id.description: The movement id.

type.description: `deposit` when money or credits were added, `withdraw` when they were taken out.

wallet.description: Which wallet moved: `booking_balance` for the booking money balance, or the course id as text (for example `1`) for that course's credits.

amount_pence.description: The amount in integer pence, always positive, for a `booking_balance` movement; null for a credits movement.

currency.description: `GBP` for a money movement; null for a credits movement.

credits.description: The number of credits, always positive, for a course movement (it can be fractional such as `0.2`); null for a money movement.

description.description: The text recorded with the movement, for example the booking it paid for. Null when none was recorded.

booking_id.description: The booking the movement belongs to, when it was made for one; otherwise null.

created_at.description: When the movement was recorded: an instant in UTC with a `Z`.

booking_credits.description: The booking credits left, one entry per course that still has some. Courses with none are left out. Each entry has `course_id`, `course_name` and `credits` (the number of credits: one credit pays for one place on that course; it can be fractional such as `4.5`).

course_id.description: The id of the course the credits are for (see `GET /courses`).

credits.description: The credits left for the course: one credit pays for one place on it. It can be fractional, such as `4.5`.

booking_balance_pence.description: The booking money balance in integer pence. It can be zero or negative (a fee can take it below zero).

hold_hash.description: The token that identifies the hold (32 characters). Send it as `hold_hash` to `POST /bookings`, or as `{hash}` to `DELETE /training-events/hold/{hash}`. Treat it as opaque.

expires_at.description: When the hold ends: an instant in UTC with a `Z`. A hold is created for 30 minutes. After this time the hold can no longer be used to book.

expires_in_seconds.description: The seconds left until `expires_at` at the time of the answer, never below 0.

training_event.description: The held session in brief. Use `GET /training-events/{event}` for the full session.

id.description: The session id.

start_date.description: When the session starts. An instant in UTC with a `Z`: the session's UK local time converted to UTC. In British Summer Time that is an hour earlier than the clock in the UK (a 09:00 session on 7 July is `2026-07-07T08:00:00Z`), in winter it is the same (a 09:00 session on 7 November is `2026-11-07T09:00:00Z`).

id.description: The location id. Use it as `location_id` when you filter sessions and bookings.

address.description: The address of the venue as one text. Null when none is held.

id.description: The Hub client id of the account: the same id the Hub core API and the other portals use for this client. It is not a Practical Training internal id.

contact_name.description: The name of the main contact held on the account.

email.description: The email address of the account.

notify_email.description: The address that receives the account's booking notifications and agency confirmations unless a booking names another `agency_email`.

PtStoreBookingBody.description:
`POST /bookings`: books a held place for a Hub candidate. The attendee's name, email, phone and job role come from the Hub
candidate and are not sent; the session is the one the hold was made on; the key's scope is the permission.

hold_hash.description: The `hold_hash` returned by `POST /training-events/{event}/hold`. Required. It must be a live hold of your own account: a hold that does not exist, has expired, belongs to another account or has already been used is `422 validation_failed` on `hold_hash`. The booking is made on the session the hold was made on. A successful booking removes the hold; a rejected booking keeps it.

candidate_ref.description: The `candidate_ref` (uuid) of the person to book: a candidate of your account in the Hub core API (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Required. The attendee's first name, last name, email, phone and job role (the candidate's first role) are taken from this candidate. An unknown candidate, or one without a first name, an email address or a phone number, is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`; add the missing detail with `PATCH /api/v2/hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}`.

pay_option.description: How the place is paid for. Required. `credits`: one booking credit for the course is taken now. `balance`: the session price is taken from the booking balance now. `invoice` (or its alias `inv`): the booking is confirmed and invoiced, if invoicing is switched on for your account and the price is within its credit limit. `candidate_pays`: the booking stays `pending` and the candidate is emailed a payment link, which is also returned as `payment_url`. Too few credits or too little balance is `402 insufficient_credits`; invoicing that is not allowed is `422 booking_rejected`. Check `GET /credits` first.

agency_contact_name.description: The name of the person at your account who is responsible for the booking (the agency contact). Required, at most 150 characters. Stored on the booking.

agency_contact_email.description: The email address of the agency contact. Required, a valid email address, at most 255 characters. Stored on the booking; for some accounts it is the address that receives the agency emails.

agency_email.description: The address that receives the agency's confirmation email for the booking. Optional, a valid email address, at most 255 characters. When left out, the account's notification address is used.

PtStoreBookingBody.title: PtStoreBookingBody

PtStoreBookingInviteBody.description:
`POST /booking-invites`: invites a Hub candidate (the email comes from the candidate). The contact is the person at the
client who is copied in, as on the Invites page.

candidate_ref.description: The `candidate_ref` (uuid) of the person to invite: a candidate of your account in the Hub core API (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Required. The invited name and email address are taken from this candidate. An unknown candidate, or one without an email address, is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`; add the address with `PATCH /api/v2/hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}`.

contact_name.description: The name of the person at your account who is copied in on the invitation email. Optional, at most 150 characters. When left out, nobody is named.

contact_email.description: The email address of that contact, who is copied in on the invitation email. Optional, a valid email address, at most 255 characters. When left out, nobody is copied in.

course.description: The course taught at the session.

location.description: Where the session takes place. Null when the session has no location.

remaining_slots.description: The number of places still free on the session at the time of the call. A place is taken only when a booking is made (a hold does not take one), so the number can fall before you book.

cost_inc_vat_pence.description: The price this account pays for one place, in integer pence, including VAT: the account's own rate for the course when it has one, otherwise the session's price.

remaining_slots.description: The number of places still free on the session at the time of the call. A place is taken only when a booking is made (a hold does not take one), so the number can fall before you book.

cost_inc_vat_pence.description: The price this account pays for one place, in integer pence, including VAT: the account's own rate for the course when it has one, otherwise the session's price.

trainer.description: The trainer assigned to the session, or null when none is assigned yet.

id.description: The trainer id.
The alert id, for `GET /alerts/{id}` and `POST /alerts/{id}/acknowledge`.

type.description: What raised the alert. Registration Monitoring: `registration_expired`, `registration_suspended`, `conditions_added`, `conditions_cleared`, `removed_from_register`, `registration_not_found`, `manual_review_required`, `registration_restored`, `invalid_pin` or `status_changed`. DBS & Right To Work: `dbs_new_info`, `dbs_non_blank`, `rtw_issue`, `rtw_expired`, `rtw_expiry_3_days`, `rtw_expiry_1_month`, `rtw_expiry_3_months`, `rtw_share_code_expired`, `rtw_share_code_expiry_3_days` or `rtw_share_code_expiry_14_days`. A value that is not in these lists can appear if a new type is added later.

type_label.description: The type as a person reads it, for example `Registration expired` or `Share code expires in 14 days`.

severity.description: How serious the alert is: `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`. A registration alert takes its severity from the new status (removed, suspended or not found are `critical`; lapsed, conditions, caution and invalid PIN `high`; manual review `medium`; restored `low`); DBS and right to work alerts are set when they are raised (new DBS information is `critical`).

title.description: The alert's headline. It usually begins with the worker's full name, so treat it as personal data.

description.description: What happened, as a sentence. It can contain the registration number and, for the DBS alerts, the DBS certificate number masked to its last four characters (`********7890`), so treat it as personal data.
examples: NMC registration 12A3456E status changed from active to lapsed.

previous_status.description: The worker's status before the change (registration alerts and DBS status alerts); null when the alert is not about a status change.

new_status.description: The worker's status after the change; null when the alert is not about a status change.

acknowledged.description: True once the alert has been acknowledged (through the API, or in Hub).

acknowledged_at.description: When the alert was acknowledged; null while it is open.

registration_check_id.description: The check that raised the alert (`GET /registration-checks/{check}/raw-data`); null for DBS and right to work alerts and for the expiry reminders, which are not raised by a registration check.

worker.description: The worker the alert is about.

id.description: The worker id; null when the worker no longer exists.

name.description: The worker's full name (first and last name), or `Unknown worker` when the worker no longer exists.

regulator.description: The regulator's abbreviation in upper case, for example `NMC` (the worker's `regulator` field is the lower case key). Null for a DBS or right to work worker, which has no professional registration.

registration_number.description: The registration number; null for a DBS or right to work worker.

id.description: The alert id, for `GET /alerts/{id}` and `POST /alerts/{id}/acknowledge`.

type.description: The alert type, for example `registration_expired` or `rtw_issue`: see `type` of the full alert for the list.

severity.description: How serious the alert is: `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`.

title.description: The alert's headline. It begins with the worker's full name, so it is personal data.

acknowledged.description: True once the alert has been acknowledged.

acknowledged_count.description: How many alerts this call acknowledged. Alerts that were already acknowledged, and ids that are not open alerts of this portal, are not counted, so the number can be lower than the number of ids sent; 0 is a normal answer.

id.description: The bill id, for `GET /billing/bills/{id}/invoice`.

bill_number.description: The bill number printed on the invoice.

period.description: The month the bill covers, as text.

active_workers.description: How many active workers the bill counted: registrations, DBS-only and right-to-work-only workers all count once.

billing_type.description: The billing type the bill was made under: `per_candidate` or `fixed_monthly`.

tier_label.description: The name of the pricing tier that applied; null when none did.

base_amount_pence.description: The price before adjustments and VAT, in pence.

adjustments_total_pence.description: The total of manual adjustments (credits are negative), in pence; 0 when there are none.

vat_amount_pence.description: The VAT on the bill, in pence.

total_amount_pence.description: The amount due including adjustments and VAT, in pence.

currency.description: The currency of every amount: always `GBP`.

status.description: Where the bill is: `generated`, `amended`, `ready_for_collection`, `submitted_to_gocardless`, `paid`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

status_label.description: The status as a person reads it, for example `Paid` or `Submitted for collection`.

status_tone.description: A colour hint for the status: `success`, `danger`, `warning`, `info` or `neutral`.

due_at.description: The date payment is due, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null when none is set.

paid_at.description: The date the bill was paid, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null until it is.

generated_at.description: The date the bill was generated, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null when not recorded.

label.description: The name of the billing type, for example `Per candidate`.

tier_label.description: The name of the pricing tier that applies at today's worker count; null when no tier applies (for example when there are no active workers).

base_amount_pence.description: The price before VAT, in pence; 0 when no tier applies.

vat_amount_pence.description: The VAT on the base price, in pence.

total_amount_pence.description: The base price plus VAT, in pence.

label.description: The band of worker counts the tier covers, as text: `26 – 50` or `1,001 – +` for a per candidate tier, `Up to 50` or `1,001+` for a fixed monthly tier.

price_pence.description: The price in pence: per worker per month for a per candidate tier, per month for a fixed monthly tier. Before VAT.

currency.description: The currency of every amount: always `GBP`.

trial.description: The free trial. It starts when the account's first worker was created and lasts one month.

starts_at.description: The day the trial started (the day the first worker was created), `YYYY-MM-DD`; null while the account has no workers.

expires_at.description: The day the trial ends, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null while the account has no workers.

days_left.description: Whole days left of the trial, rounded up; null when the trial is over or has not started.

on_trial.description: True while the trial is running.

expired.description: True once the trial has ended.

restricted.description: True when checks have stopped: the trial is over and the account has neither Direct Debit set up with billing allowed nor a manual access override.

eligible.description: True when the account may run checks now: the trial is running, Direct Debit is set up with billing allowed, or a manual access override is running. When false, `POST /workers/{id}/verify` answers `422 verification_refused`.

manual_access_ends_at.description: The day a manual access override granted by Hub staff ends, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null when none is running.

billing_type.description: The billing type the account chose: `per_candidate` or `fixed_monthly`. Null until it has been chosen in Hub; once chosen it can only be changed by the account team.

billing_types.description: The billing types that exist, each with its label.

value.description: The value to compare with `billing_type`: `per_candidate` or `fixed_monthly`.

label.description: The name of the billing type, for example `Per candidate`.

allow_billing.description: True when HB staff have allowed billing for the account (one of the two conditions, with Direct Debit, for checks to continue after the trial).

direct_debit.description: The state of the account's Direct Debit. The set-up link is not returned.

gc_created.description: True when Direct Debit is set up.

mandate_status.description: The state of the Direct Debit mandate as the payment provider reports it; null when there is none.

invite_status.description: The state of the invitation to set Direct Debit up (`invited`, `failed`, ...); null when none was sent.

invited_at.description: When the invitation was sent, an ISO 8601 time with its offset; null when none was sent.

has_invitation_sent.description: True when an invitation has been sent.

can_resend_invitation.description: True when the invitation can be sent again from Hub.

available.description: True when Direct Debit is available on this installation.

estimate.description: What this month would cost at today's number of active workers.

month.description: The month the estimate is for, as text.

active_workers.description: How many active workers the estimate counts: registrations, DBS-only and right-to-work-only workers each count once.

vat_rate_percent.description: The VAT rate in percent that applies; 0 when VAT is switched off.

selected.description: The billing type the account chose (`per_candidate` or `fixed_monthly`), the same as the top level `billing_type`; null until chosen.

options.description: The estimate under each billing type, as an object with the keys `per_candidate` and `fixed_monthly`, so the two can be compared before choosing.

per_candidate.description: The estimate under per candidate billing.

fixed_monthly.description: The estimate under fixed monthly billing.

tiers.description: The pricing tiers in force today.

per_candidate.description: The per candidate tiers: the price of one worker in each band of worker counts.

fixed_monthly.description: The fixed monthly tiers: the monthly price of each band of worker counts.

id.description: The import id, for `GET /worker-imports/{id}`.

status.description: Where the import is: `pending` (queued), `processing` (rows are being read), `completed` (every row was handled; some can still have failed, see `failed_count`) or `failed` (the file could not be processed at all, see `errors`).

file_name.description: The name the uploaded file had.

total_rows.description: How many data rows the file has (blank rows are not counted). 0 until the job has counted them.

imported_count.description: How many rows were turned into workers (created, or updated when the row names a worker that already exists). While the import runs the figure is refreshed every ten rows.

failed_count.description: How many rows were rejected. Each has an entry in `errors`.

progress.description: The percentage of rows handled, 0 to 100 (`imported_count` plus `failed_count`, out of `total_rows`). A completed file with no rows is 100.

errors.description: The rows that failed, each with the line number in the file (the header is line 1) and the first message for that row, at most 1000 of them; null when there are none. When the whole import fails the list has one entry with a `message` and no `line`.

examples.message: The registration number field is required unless regulator is in dbs, rtw.

processed_at.description: When the import finished (completed or failed); null while it is pending or processing.

headers.description: The column headers of the file, trimmed and in lower case.

expected_fields.description: The fields the import understands for this portal, the same list as `GET /worker-imports/template`.

suggested_mapping.description: The column mapping used: for each expected field, the file header it reads, or null when it is not mapped. It is the `column_mapping` you sent, or, when you sent none, a guess made by matching header names (ignoring case, spaces and underscores). The import itself never guesses: send this object as `column_mapping` to `POST /worker-imports` to import with it.

sample_rows.description: The first five data rows after the mapping is applied: the mapped fields and, as `line`, the line number in the file. Rows are not validated here.

total_rows.description: How many data rows the file has (blank rows are not counted).

rows_checked.description: How many rows were validated: at most the first 1000. When `total_rows` is higher, `truncated` is true and the real import still handles every row.

valid_count.description: How many of the validated rows have no errors and would be imported.

invalid_count.description: How many of the validated rows have errors and would be rejected.

truncated.description: True when the file has more rows than were validated.

errors.description: The first error of each invalid row, at most 200 rows: the line number in the file (the header is line 1) and a message.

examples.message: The registration number field is required unless regulator is in dbs, rtw.

columns.description: The column names to use as the header row of the CSV, in the order of the Hub template. Registration Monitoring: first_name, last_name, regulator, registration_number, date_of_birth, email, phone, profession, check_frequency, monitoring_start_date, consent_given, is_active, notes. DBS & Right To Work: first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, email, phone, dbs_certificate_number, dbs_surname, dbs_check_frequency, rtw_document_type, rtw_share_code, rtw_check_frequency, consent_given, is_active, notes.

updated_count.description: How many workers were changed: the number of distinct ids sent. A call that names an id that is not one of the portal's workers changes nothing and answers `422 workers_not_found` instead.

id.description: The worker id.

is_active.description: True while the worker is monitored. Switching a worker off clears every next check date; switching it on again reschedules each track from its frequency.

monitoring_start_date.description: The date monitoring starts, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null when none is set.

registration.description: The registration schedule (Registration Monitoring only); null in DBS & Right To Work.

check_frequency.description: How often the registration is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`.

next_check_due_at.description: When the next check is due; null while the worker is inactive.

dbs.description: The DBS schedule (DBS & Right To Work only); null in Registration Monitoring and when the worker is not enrolled for DBS.

check_frequency.description: How often the DBS status is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`.

next_check_due_at.description: When the next DBS check is due; null while the worker is inactive.

rtw.description: The right to work schedule (DBS & Right To Work only); null in Registration Monitoring and when the worker is not enrolled for right to work.

check_frequency.description: How often the right to work status is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`.

next_check_due_at.description: When the next right to work check is due; null while the worker is inactive.

format.description: The format of `content`: `json` (a registration check, a right to work check) or `xml` (a DBS Update Service answer, returned as text).

content.description: The stored answer. For `json` it is the decoded structure (an object or array whose fields depend on the regulator or service and can change without notice; if the stored text is not valid JSON it is returned as that text); for `xml` it is the XML as a string. Null when nothing was stored. It can contain personal data.

roles.description: The roles an Owner can give a team member: `client-admin`, `client-manager`, `client-officer` and `client-viewer`, each with the permissions it holds for this account (the Owner's changes on the My Team page are included). The Owner role, which always holds every permission, and the Developer role are not listed.

permissions.description: The names of the permissions the role holds, from `permissions[].permissions[].name`, for example `registration-monitoring.view`.
Every permission that exists, grouped by area of Hub (the Hub core and each service).

key.description: The area: `hub` or the portal key, for example `registration-monitoring` or `dbs-rtw`.

jobs.description: The jobs that were queued, one per worker and track. A DBS & Right To Work worker enrolled for both tracks has two jobs unless `track` was sent. Never empty: when nothing could be queued the call answers `422 verification_refused` instead.

track.description: The track that is being checked: `registration`, `dbs` or `rtw`.

job_id.description: The id of the verification job. Poll `GET /verify/jobs/{job}` with it.

refused.description: The worker and track pairs that were not queued, each with the reason. Empty when everything was queued.

track.description: The track that was refused: `registration`, `dbs` or `rtw`.

reason.description: Why the check was refused, for a person to read, for example `Manual re-check is not enabled for this account.`

job_id.description: The job id, as returned when the check was queued.

track.description: The track the job checks: `registration`, `dbs` or `rtw`.

regulator.description: The regulator key of a registration job (`nmc`, `gmc`, ...), or `dbs` or `rtw` for those tracks.

status.description: Where the job is: `pending` (queued, or recorded and waiting because the engine is switched off), `processing`, `completed` or `failed`. A job can be `completed` with `failed_count` above 0 when a check could not be read.

total_workers.description: How many workers the job checks, set when the job starts: 0 or null before that.

processed_count.description: How many workers the job has handled so far, successfully or not.

success_count.description: How many checks worked (the register or service was read).

failed_count.description: How many checks failed (the register or service could not be read). The worker stays as it was and is retried later.

status_changes_found.description: How many workers this job found with a different status from before. Each raises an alert and a webhook.

started_at.description: When the job started; null while it is `pending`.

completed_at.description: When the job ended; null until it is `completed` or `failed`.

error_message.description: Why the job failed, for a person to read; null while it has not failed.

job_id.description: The id of the verification job. Poll `GET /verify/jobs/{job}` with it.

track.description: The track that is being checked: `registration` (Registration Monitoring), `dbs` or `rtw` (DBS & Right To Work).

status.description: The state of the job when it was created: `pending`. It becomes `processing` when the check starts and `completed` or `failed` when it ends.

id.description: The id of the worker that was removed. It no longer answers on `/workers/{id}`.

uuid.description: The referee's uuid (the `uuid` of the referee row in the request, and `reference_uuid` in webhooks).

reference_request_uuid.description: The uuid of the request this reference belongs to (`GET /requests/{uuid}`).

candidate_ref.description: The candidate the reference is about: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API. Null only for a candidate Hub has not yet synced.

candidate_name.description: The candidate's display name, or null when the candidate cannot be found.

candidate_email.description: The candidate's email address, or null when there is none.

referee.description: Who the referee is, as `name`, `email`, `organisation`, `position`, `phone` (or null) and `relationship_to_candidate` (or null). Personal data of a third party.

email.description: The referee's email address.

organisation.description: The organisation the referee works for.

position.description: The referee's job title or position.

phone.description: The referee's telephone number, or null when none was given.

relationship_to_candidate.description: How the referee knows the candidate, or null when none was given.

status.description: Where the reference is in its life: `pending`, `sent`, `opened`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `declined`, `expired` or `bounced`. `completed`, `declined`, `expired` and `bounced` are final.

display_status.description: The simpler status the Hub screens show a client: `received`, `rejected`, `expired`, `overdue`, `legacy` or `requested`.

score.description: The score of the reference: the weighted average of the scored questions, rounded to two decimals. Null when the client does not use scoring, when the form has no scoring criteria, or when the answers did not match any criterion. It is also null until the reference is completed.

score_breakdown.description: How the score was reached: one item per scored question with its `label`, the `value` answered, the `raw_score`, the `weight` and the `weighted_score`. Empty when the client does not use scoring or the reference is not scored.

decline_reason.description: The reason the referee gave for declining, in their own words. It is set only when `status` is `declined` and the referee wrote one; null otherwise. It is free text from a third party: show it as plain text. It is never in a webhook (`has_decline_reason` tells you whether one exists).

answers.description: The answers the referee gave, in the order recorded. Each has the question's `field_code` (the question id on the form), its `label` (the question text; the `field_code` again when the form no longer has that question) and the `value` (the answer in readable form for a question the form still has, otherwise as stored). The referee's own contact details are not repeated here: they are in `referee`. Empty until the reference is completed.

has_pdf.description: True when the reference is `completed`, which is when `GET /referees/{uuid}/pdf` returns a PDF.

sent_at.description: When the request email was sent to the referee (ISO 8601, UTC), or null if it has not been sent.

opened_at.description: When the referee first opened the form (ISO 8601, UTC), or null if they have not.

submitted_at.description: When the referee submitted the reference (ISO 8601, UTC), or null until then.

expires_at.description: When this reference expires (ISO 8601, UTC); it follows the request's `expires_at` and moves when the request is extended. Null for an older imported record with no expiry date.

reminder_count.description: How many reminders the referee has been sent.

last_reminder_at.description: When the last reminder was sent (ISO 8601, UTC), or null if none has been sent.

uuid.description: The referee's uuid. It never changes and is what you pass to `GET /referees/{uuid}`, `GET /referees/{uuid}/pdf` and `POST /referees/{uuid}/reminder`. A `reference_uuid` in a webhook is this value.

name.description: The referee's full name, as given when the referee was added.

email.description: The email address the request and any reminders are sent to.

organisation.description: The organisation the referee works for.

position.description: The referee's job title or position.

phone.description: The referee's telephone number, or null when none was given.

relationship_to_candidate.description: How the referee knows the candidate, in the words given when the referee was added (for example "Line manager"), or null when none was given.

status.description: Where the reference is in its life: `pending` (added, not yet emailed), `sent` (emailed), `opened` (the referee opened the form), `in_progress` (the referee started the form), `completed` (submitted), `declined`, `expired` (not answered in time, or the request was cancelled) or `bounced` (the email could not be delivered). `completed`, `declined`, `expired` and `bounced` are final.

status_label.description: The text of `status` for display: `Pending`, `Sent`, `Opened`, `In progress`, `Completed`, `Declined`, `Expired` or `Bounced`.

display_status.description: The simpler status the Hub screens show a client: `received` (completed), `rejected` (declined), `expired` (expired or bounced), `overdue` (still waiting and past its expiry time), `legacy` (an imported older record that nobody answered and that has no expiry date) or `requested` (anything else).

sent_at.description: When the request email was sent to the referee (ISO 8601, UTC), or null while the referee has not been emailed.

submitted_at.description: When the referee submitted the reference (ISO 8601, UTC), or null until then.

reminder_count.description: How many reminders have been sent to this referee, by the automatic reminders and by `POST /requests/{uuid}/reminders` or `POST /referees/{uuid}/reminder` together.

uuid.description: The request's uuid. It never changes and is what you pass to every `/requests/{uuid}` call. It is `uuid` in the `reference.request.created` webhook and `reference_request_uuid` in the other reference webhooks.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate the references are about: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). It is null only for a candidate that Hub has not yet synced and that has no reference yet; use `candidate_name` and `candidate_email` to recognise the person in that case.

candidate_name.description: The candidate's display name. Null when the candidate record cannot be found.

candidate_email.description: The candidate's email address. For a request with `collection_mode` `candidate_provides` this is where the invitation to give referees is sent. Null when the candidate has no email address or cannot be found.

template.description: The form the referees complete, as `id` (an `id` from `GET /templates`) and `name`. On creation the request takes the `template_id` you sent, else the client's default form; it is null when neither exists, and the form in force then falls back to the system default form.

id.description: The template id (an `id` from `GET /templates`).

name.description: The template's name; null if the template can no longer be found.

collection_mode.description: Who gives the referee details: `client_adds` (you gave the referees when you created the request, or add them with `POST /requests/{uuid}/referees`) or `candidate_provides` (the candidate is emailed a link to a page where they enter their referees).

status.description: The state of the request: `pending` (no referee has been emailed yet), `in_progress` (at least one referee has been emailed and not all references are in), `completed` (enough references are in), `cancelled` or `expired`. `completed` and `cancelled` are final; an `expired` request can be extended with `POST /requests/{uuid}/extend`.

status_label.description: The text of `status` for display: `Pending`, `In progress`, `Completed`, `Cancelled` or `Expired`.

references_required.description: How many completed references the request needs. When you do not send `references_required` on creation it is the client's minimum.

references_completed.description: How many referees have submitted their reference so far.

notes.description: The free-text note stored with the request when it was created, or null when none was given.
examples: Care assistant post, start date 2 November.

expires_at.description: When the request expires (ISO 8601, UTC). After this time referees can no longer submit and the request becomes `expired`. Null for an older imported request that has no expiry date.

is_expired.description: True when `expires_at` has passed. It can be true a short while before `status` changes to `expired`, because the status is updated by a scheduled job.

submission_url.description: For a `candidate_provides` request: the public page where the candidate enters their referees (it needs no login). Null for a `client_adds` request.

referees.description: The referees added to the request. Empty for a `candidate_provides` request until the candidate has given their referees.

created_at.description: When the request was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

reminders_sent.description: How many reminder emails were sent by this call. 0 when no referee was due.

skipped.description: The referees who are still expected to answer but were not reminded, each with the `referee` name and the `reason` in words (for example that the next reminder is not due until a date, or that the maximum number of reminders has been reached). Referees who have finished (completed, declined, expired or bounced) are not listed.

examples.reason: is not due a reminder until 02 Nov 2026

sent.description: Always true: when no reminder can be sent the call answers `422 reminder_not_sent` instead.

reminder_count.description: The number of reminders the referee has had, including this one.

id.description: The template id. Pass it as `template_id` to `POST /requests` to ask the referees to complete this form. It never changes.

description.description: What the form is for, or null when no description was written.

is_system.description: True for a form that belongs to Healthier Business and is available to every client; false for a form the client created.

is_default.description: True for the form used when a request names no `template_id`: the client's default form, or the system default when the client has not set one. At most one template in the list is the default, and none is when no default can be found.

questions.description: How many questions the form asks the referee. Headings and other items that take no answer are not counted.

updated_at.description: When the template was last changed (ISO 8601, UTC), or null when that is not recorded.

id.description: The check id. Use it with `GET /registration-checks/{check}/raw-data` and to match the `registration_check_id` of alerts, evidence files and webhooks.

status.description: The status the register showed: `active`, `lapsed`, `suspended`, `conditions`, `caution`, `removed`, `erased`, `registered_no_licence`, `not_found`, `manual_review`, `invalid_pin` or `error`. Null when the check produced no status.

status_label.description: The status as a person reads it, for example `Active`. `Awaiting Initial Check` when `status` is null.

status_changed.description: True when this check found a different status from the check before it. A status change raises an alert and sends the `registration-monitoring.worker.status_changed` webhook.

previous_status.description: The status the worker had before this check; null for the first check of a worker.

expiry_date.description: The registration end date the regulator reported at this check, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null when it gave none.

method.description: How the register was read, for example `browser` (the regulator's public register was opened and read). Null when not recorded.

result.description: Whether the check itself worked: `success` when the register was read, `error` when it could not be (the regulator's site was unavailable, for example). An `error` check does not change the worker's status. Null when not recorded.

RmCreateWorkerBody.description: The worker to monitor: who they are and the registration to check. Send JSON. `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `regulator`, `registration_number` and `consent_given` are required, and `date_of_birth` is required when `regulator` is `nmc`. A field that is not listed is ignored.

first_name.description: The worker's first name, at most 255 characters.

last_name.description: The worker's last name, at most 255 characters.

email.description: The worker's email address, at most 255 characters. Required.

phone.description: The worker's telephone number, free text, at most 255 characters.

date_of_birth.description: The worker's date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`, before today. Required when `regulator` is `nmc` (the NMC check needs it, otherwise `422` on this field); optional for the other regulators.

regulator.description: The regulator whose register is checked, as a lower case key. Required. One of: `nmc`, `gmc`, `hcpc`, `gdc`, `goc`, `gphc`, `ahcs`, `swe`, `sssc`, `scw`, `niscc`, `psni`, `gosc`, `gcc`.

registration_number.description: The registration number (PIN) the regulator issued, at most 255 characters. Required. The same regulator and number cannot be monitored twice for one account (`422` on this field); a number that was removed earlier is restored.

profession.description: The worker's profession in your own words, at most 255 characters.

compliance_officer_name.description: The person in your organisation responsible for the worker's compliance, at most 255 characters.

monitoring_start_date.description: The date monitoring starts, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Left out, it is today.

consent_given.description: Must be true: the worker has agreed to be monitored. The call is refused with `422` on this field otherwise. Hub records the moment you made the call as the time consent was given.

notes.description: Free text notes about the worker, at most 5000 characters.

check_frequency.description: How often the registration is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Left out, the account's default frequency for registrations applies (`monthly` when the account has none).

id.description: The evidence file id, for `GET /evidence/{file}` and `GET /evidence/{file}/download`.

registration_check_id.description: The id of the check that captured the file (see `GET /workers/{id}/verification`); null when the file is not tied to a check.

worker_id.description: The id of the worker the file belongs to.

type.description: What the file is: `screenshot` (an image of the register page), `html_snapshot` (the page's saved HTML), `sanction_pdf` (an NMC sanction document) or `determination_pdf` (a GDC determination notice for conditions or a caution).

mime_type.description: The file's media type, for example `image/png`, `text/html` or `application/pdf`.

file_size.description: The size of the file in bytes.

download_url.description: The absolute address of `GET /evidence/{file}/download` for this file. It needs the same bearer token as every other call: it is not a public link.

worker_ids.description: The ids of the workers to change, 1 to 500 (repeated ids count once). Every id must be a worker of your account in this portal, otherwise nothing is changed and the call is `422 workers_not_found`.

RmMonitoringSettingsBody.description: The monitoring settings to change. Send at least one field; a field you leave out keeps its value.

check_frequency.description: How often the registration is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. The next check is rescheduled from the last check (or from the start date when there has been none).

monitoring_start_date.description: The date monitoring starts, `YYYY-MM-DD`; send null to clear it.

is_active.description: Whether the worker is monitored. False stops scheduled checks and clears every next check date; true again reschedules each track from its frequency.

id.description: The worker id: an integer that never changes. Use it in every `/workers/{id}` path and as `worker_id` in alerts and webhooks.

candidate_ref.description: The `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid) of the Hub candidate this worker was linked to, the same value the Hub core API gives the candidate. It is null for every worker created through this API, an import or the Hub pages, because those do not link a worker to a candidate; it is filled only when Hub staff linked the worker. It is read only.

first_name.description: The worker's first name, as stored. It is also the name used to look the registration up where the regulator needs one.

email.description: The worker's email address; null when none was given (an import row may leave it out).

phone.description: The worker's telephone number, free text; null when none was given.

date_of_birth.description: The worker's date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`. It is required for an NMC registration (the NMC check needs it) and optional for the other regulators; null when none was given.

profession.description: The worker's profession in your own words, free text; null when none was given. It is not read from the regulator.

regulator.description: The regulator whose register is checked, as a lower case key: `nmc`, `gmc`, `hcpc`, `gdc`, `goc`, `gphc`, `ahcs`, `swe`, `sssc`, `scw`, `niscc`, `psni`, `gosc` or `gcc`.

registration_number.description: The registration number (PIN) the regulator issued, as entered. Together with the regulator it identifies the registration: the same pair cannot be monitored twice for one client.

status.description: The status the last successful check found: `active`, `lapsed`, `suspended`, `conditions`, `caution`, `removed`, `erased`, `registered_no_licence`, `not_found`, `manual_review`, `invalid_pin` or `error`. It is null until the first check has completed (`status_label` then reads `Awaiting Initial Check`).

status_label.description: The status as a person reads it, for example `Active`, `Lapsed` or `Registered (no licence)`. An `active` registration that carries a regulator warning or condition reads `Active with warning`, `Active with condition` or `Active with warning and condition`. `Awaiting Initial Check` while `status` is null.

restrictions.description: The restrictions or entitlements the regulator reported at the last successful check, joined with commas; null when none were reported or no check has completed.

has_warning.description: True when the regulator reported a warning on the registration at the last check (an NMC or GMC warning flag).

has_condition.description: True when the regulator reported a condition on the registration at the last check: an NMC undertaking or fitness to practise issue, or a GMC undertaking or condition.

expiry_date.description: The end date of the registration as the regulator reported it at the last successful check, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null when the regulator gave none or no check has completed.

check_frequency.description: How often the registration is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. A worker created without one gets the account's default for registrations (`monthly` when the account has none). Change it with `PATCH /workers/{id}/monitoring-settings`.
