is_active.description: True while the worker is monitored. An inactive worker is not checked on schedule, has no next check date, and a manual check on it is refused (`verification_refused`).

compliance_officer_name.description: The name of the person in your organisation responsible for this worker's compliance, free text; null when none was given.

notes.description: Free text notes you keep about the worker, at most 5000 characters; null when there are none.

last_checked_at.description: When the registration was last checked successfully. A check that failed (an error from the regulator's site, for example) does not move it. Null until the first successful check.

next_check_due_at.description: When the next scheduled check is due. It is null for an inactive worker and for a worker that has not been scheduled yet (a worker created through the API is first picked up by the next monitoring run). After a failed check it is moved on by a few hours so the worker is retried later.

TokenPair.description: The answer of the token exchange and of the refresh: a short-lived access token for calling the API and a longer-lived refresh token to get the next pair without the API key. Both tokens are opaque random strings of 80 characters; Hub stores only a hash of them, so a lost token cannot be shown again. Store the refresh token as carefully as the API key itself.

token_type.description: Always `Bearer`: send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

access_token.description: The access token, 80 random characters. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every call. Valid for `expires_in` seconds; after that, or after revoke or refresh, a call with it is `401 invalid_token`.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token, 80 random characters. Exchange it at `POST /api/v2/auth/refresh` for a new pair. Valid for `refresh_expires_in` seconds and usable once: the refresh revokes it and the access token that came with it.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires: always 3600 (one hour). Renew shortly before, or on the first `401 invalid_token`.

refresh_expires_in.description: Seconds until the refresh token expires: always 604800 (seven days). Every refresh gives a new refresh token with a fresh seven days.

TokenRevoked.description: Confirmation that the token pair was revoked. The API key itself is unaffected.

status.description: Always `revoked`: the access token and its refresh token no longer work.

ValidationError.description: The error body of a 422 `validation_failed`: an `Error` whose `details` maps each invalid field to its messages.

details.description: Each invalid field (dot notation for nested fields) mapped to its messages.

id.description:
The booking id: an integer that never changes. It is the id in the paths `/bookings/{booking}`, the
`booking_id` of the webhook events and the `booking_id` of credit transactions.

candidate_ref.description:
The `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid) of the candidate the booking belongs to, the same value the Hub core API uses.
A booking stores the attendee's name and email address, not a Hub candidate, so the ref is that of your
account's Hub candidate with the booking's HB Portal candidate id or, failing that, the same email address.
It is null when your account has no such Hub candidate.

candidate_name.description:
The attendee's first and last name as recorded on the booking. The email address, phone number and job role
are not returned: read them from the Hub candidate.

course.description: The course the booking is for.

id.description: The course id, as in `GET /courses`.

start_date.description:
When the session starts, ISO 8601 in UTC. The booking stores the start as UK local time and the API converts
it, so a session at 11:00 in summer is `10:00:00Z`.

end_date.description: When the session ends, ISO 8601 in UTC; the start plus the length of the course.

booking_status.description:
Where the booking stands: `pending` (created, waiting for the candidate to pay), `booked` (confirmed),
`rescheduled` (confirmed and moved to another slot), `cancelled`, or `refunded` (cancelled and refunded).
`pending` is followed by `booked` when the payment arrives. Abandoned bookings are never returned.

pay_status.description:
The payment status recorded on the booking: `pending` until it is paid, `completed` once it is paid (a
booking made with credits, balance or invoice is `completed` at once) and `refunded` after a refund.

pay_option.description:
How the booking is paid for: `credits` (one booking credit), `balance` (the money balance), `inv` (invoice) or
`cc` (card, paid by the candidate through the payment link: a booking made with `pay_option`
`candidate_pays`).

booked_by.description:
Who made the booking: `Agency` for a booking made by an account (every booking made through this API) and
`Candidate` for a candidate who booked on the public booking page.

cost_pence.description:
The price recorded on the booking, in pence, VAT included. It is your account's own rate for `inv` and
`balance` bookings that have one and the list price otherwise; a booking made through a free booking link
costs 0.

attendance.description:
The attendance recorded after the session: `attended` (the candidate passed or was present), `no_show` (the
candidate was absent), or null until attendance has been recorded. (The webhook event
`booking.attendance_marked` carries the recorded value `passed`, `present` or `absent` instead.)

virtual.description:
The online session details. The values are null until the Zoom meeting has been created, and a rescheduled
booking keeps its meeting, moved to the new time.

zoom_link.description: The link the candidate joins the Zoom meeting with.

zoom_password.description: The password of the Zoom meeting.

can_reschedule.description:
True when `POST /bookings/{booking}/reschedule` can be called: the booking is paid, is not cancelled or
refunded and its session has not started. It stays true inside the 120 hour late-change window, where the
reschedule call answers `402 payment_required` until the fee is paid. Always equal to `can_cancel`.

can_cancel.description:
True when `POST /bookings/{booking}/cancel` can be called: the booking is paid, is not cancelled or refunded
and its session has not started. Whether the cancellation is refunded depends on the time left (see
`refund_eligible`). Always equal to `can_reschedule`.

certificate_available.description:
True once the candidate has attended and the training kit has been returned, from which point
`GET /bookings/{booking}/certificate` returns the certificate.

created_at.description: When the booking was created, ISO 8601 in UTC.

trainer.description:
The trainer assigned to the session; null until the platform has assigned one. A reschedule releases the
trainer, so a rescheduled booking has none until a new one is assigned.

id.description: The trainer id.

payment_url.description:
Only present in the answer of `POST /bookings` when `pay_option` was `candidate_pays`: the signed link where the
candidate pays for the booking by card, the same link that is emailed to them. The link stops taking payment
three days before the session. It is not repeated by the other calls.

refund_eligible.description:
Whether the booking is refunded when cancelled: true when it was cancelled more than 120 hours before the
session, false when it was cancelled inside that window, and null while the booking has not been cancelled.
The refund itself is made automatically for credit, balance and card bookings; a failed refund leaves the
booking `cancelled` with this flag true so that it can be refunded by hand.

booking_url.description:
The public link you give to candidates so that they can book and pay for a session themselves on your
account. Null when the account has no such link.

id.description:
The course id: an integer that never changes. Use it as `course_id` in `GET /timeslots` and
`POST /timeslots/hold`.

cost_inc_vat_pence.description:
The list price of a place, in pence, VAT included. A booking paid with a credit or by the candidate is
charged at this price.

client_rate_pence.description:
Your account's own price of a place, in pence, or 0 when the account has no own rate for the course. It is
charged instead of the list price on bookings paid by invoice or from the money balance.

currency.description: The currency of the prices: always `GBP`.

duration_hours.description:
The length of the session, as the course records it: hours with the minutes as decimals, so `0.3` is 30
minutes and `1.45` is 1 hour 45 minutes (it is not a decimal fraction of an hour).

id.description: The id of the movement.

type.description:
`deposit` when money or credits were added, `withdraw` when they were taken out. The amount is always
positive; this says which way it moved.

wallet.description:
The wallet that moved: `booking_balance` for the money balance, or the id of a course, as a string, for that
course's credits.

amount_pence.description: The money moved, in pence, for the `booking_balance` wallet; null for a credit wallet.

currency.description: The currency of `amount_pence`: `GBP` for the `booking_balance` wallet, null for a credit wallet.

credits.description: The whole credits moved, for a course credit wallet; null for the `booking_balance` wallet.

description.description:
A sentence describing the movement, for example `Debited for booking #77 - Jo Smith` or
`Refund for booking #77 - Jo Smith`; null when the movement has none.

booking_id.description: The booking the movement paid for or refunded; null when it belongs to no booking (a purchase).

created_at.description: When the movement was recorded, ISO 8601 in UTC.

booking_credits.description:
The booking credits left, one entry per course that still has credits (a course with none is not listed, so
an empty list means no credits). Each entry has the `course_id`, the `course_name` and the whole `credits`
left; one credit pays for one place on that course.

booking_balance_pence.description: The pay-as-you-go money balance, in pence (integer). 12550 is 125.50 pounds.

hold_hash.description:
The identifier of the hold: a string, not an integer. Send it as `hold_hash` to `POST /bookings`, or in the
path of `DELETE /timeslots/hold/{hash}` to release the slot.

expires_at.description:
When the hold ends, ISO 8601 in UTC: 30 minutes after it was made. After this time the slot is free again and
the `hold_hash` can no longer be booked.

expires_in_seconds.description: The seconds left before the hold ends, counted when the response was made; 0 once it has ended.

slot.description: The held slot, in UK local time.

date.description: The date of the slot, `YYYY-MM-DD`, UK local date.

time.description: The start time of the slot, `HH:MM` in 24 hour UK local time (not UTC).

course.description: The course the slot is held for.

id.description: The course id.

VblsHoldTimeslotBody.description:
The slot to hold with `POST /timeslots/hold`: a course, a date and a start time. `date` and `time` are UK local time, and the
slot must be one that `GET /timeslots` lists as free. The hold lasts 30 minutes and an account holds one slot at a time.

course_id.description:
The course to hold a slot for: an `id` from `GET /courses`. Required. An id that does not exist is
`422 validation_failed` on `course_id`, and a course that is not active is `422 booking_rejected`.

date.description:
The date of the slot, `YYYY-MM-DD`, as a UK local date. Required. It must be a date on which
`GET /timeslots` lists the time as free, otherwise the call is `422 booking_rejected`.

time.description:
The start time of the slot, `HH:MM` in 24 hour UK local time (not UTC), exactly as `GET /timeslots` lists
it (slots start every 15 minutes between 07:00 and 22:00). Required.

id.description:
The Hub client id of the account: the same id that the Hub core API and the other portals use for your
organisation.

contact_name.description: The name of the account's main contact.

email.description: The account's contact email address.

notify_email.description:
The email address that receives booking notifications for the account. It is also the address used as the
agency email of a booking when `agency_email` is not sent.

client_active.description: Whether the account is active on Virtual BLS Training.

VblsRescheduleBookingBody.description:
The new slot for `POST /bookings/{booking}/reschedule`: a date and a start time in UK local time. The slot must be one that
`GET /timeslots` lists as free for the booking's course and at least five days ahead. No hold is needed.

date.description:
The new date of the session, `YYYY-MM-DD`, as a UK local date. Required. It must be a date on which the
time is free for the booking's course, otherwise the call is `422 booking_rejected`.

time.description:
The new start time, `HH:MM` in 24 hour UK local time (not UTC), exactly as `GET /timeslots` lists it.
Required.

VblsStoreBookingBody.description:
The booking made with `POST /bookings`: a held slot booked for a Hub candidate. The attendee's first name, last name, email
address, phone number and job role are not part of the body: they are read from the Hub candidate named by `candidate_ref`
(the job role is the candidate's first role). The postal address is where the training kit is sent and is kept on the
booking. The key's scope is the permission.

hold_hash.description:
The hold to book: the `hold_hash` returned by `POST /timeslots/hold`. Required, at most 64 characters. The
hold must belong to your account and must not have expired (holds last 30 minutes), otherwise the call is
`422 validation_failed` on `hold_hash`. The course, date and time of the booking are those of the hold, and the
hold is used up by the booking.

candidate_ref.description:
The candidate the booking is for: their `candidate_ref` (a uuid) from the Hub core API, `GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`.
Required. It must be a candidate of your account that has a first name, an email address and a phone number,
and whose name contains only letters and spaces; otherwise the call is `422 validation_failed` on
`candidate_ref`. Their name, email address, phone number and first role are copied onto the booking.

address.description:
The street address the training kit is posted to. Required, at most 500 characters. It is kept on the booking
and is not part of the Hub candidate.

city.description: The town or city the training kit is posted to. Required, at most 255 characters.

postcode.description: The postcode the training kit is posted to. Required, at most 20 characters.

pay_option.description:
How the booking is paid for. Required. `credits` takes one booking credit of the course, `balance` takes the
price from the money balance, `invoice` (also accepted as `inv`) charges the account by invoice; all three
confirm the booking at once. `candidate_pays` leaves the booking `pending` and emails the candidate a card
payment link, which is also returned as `payment_url`. A way of paying the account cannot cover (no credit, a
balance below the price, invoicing not open to the account) is `422 booking_rejected`; any other value is
`422 validation_failed`.

agency_contact_name.description: The name of the person at your agency who is the contact for this booking. Required, at most 255 characters.

agency_contact_email.description: The email address of that agency contact. Required, a valid email address, at most 255 characters.

agency_email.description:
An email address at your agency that is kept on the booking as the agency email; some booking emails, such as
late kit notices, are copied to it. Optional, at most 255 characters. When it is left out, the account's
notification email address (`notify_email` in `GET /profile`) is used.

booking_fields.description:
Your answers to the booking questions of the booking form, as an object whose keys are `field_` followed by the
question id (for example `field_3`). Optional unless a question is required: a required question that is not
answered, or an answer that is not one of the question's allowed options, is `422 validation_failed` on
`booking_fields.field_<id>`. A question you leave out is stored as `N/A`. A list answer (a checkbox question)
is sent as an array of strings. The API has no call that lists the questions.

additionalProperties.description: The answer to one booking question: a string, or an array of strings for a checkbox question.

It is sent once per payment. It is never sent for a booking paid with credits, balance or invoice, which is confirmed at once and sends `clinical-appraisals.booking.created` only.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use. Null when the booking's person is not one of your Hub candidates (an older booking with no matching candidate). The candidate's name, email and phone are never sent.

appraisal_type.description: The appraisal type of the booking.

transaction_id.description: The reference of the card payment, as recorded on the booking.

There are no events for later stages (documents, slot, evaluation, report), and none for cancellation or completion.

start_date.description: When the interview starts, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z` (the new start time for a rescheduled booking).

status.description: The booking's status after the event, as `booking_status` in `GET /bookings/{id}`.

interview_status.description: The interview's state after the event, as `interview_status` in `GET /bookings/{id}`.

outcome.description: The result the interviewer recorded: `passed`, `failed` or `re_interview` (the candidate needs another interview). Null when no result was recorded.

score.description: The interview score, 0 to 255. Null when no score was recorded.

by.description: Who caused the event: always `interviewer` for this event.

WebhookClinicalInterviewsBookingReschedu.description: A booking was moved to another time: by `POST /bookings/{id}/reschedule`, on the Hub pages (by you or by the candidate), or by Healthier Business staff. It is sent after the move has been made and the old interviewer released; the booking has no interviewer until a new one is assigned. `start_date` is the new time and `previous_start_date` the old one.

booking_id.description: The booking id: the `id` of the booking in `GET /bookings/{id}`.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use. Null when the booking's person is not one of your Hub candidates (an older booking with no matching candidate). The candidate's name, email and phone are never sent.

interview_type.description: The interview type of the booking.

id.description: The interview type id.

start_date.description: When the interview starts, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z` (the new start time for a rescheduled booking).

status.description: The booking's status after the event, as `booking_status` in `GET /bookings/{id}`.

interview_status.description: The interview's state after the event, as `interview_status` in `GET /bookings/{id}`.

previous_start_date.description: The time the interview was booked for before the move, ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z`.

by.description: Who caused the event. It is always `agency` for this event: the field is fixed and does not say whether the change came from the API, a Hub user, the candidate or Healthier Business staff.

WebhookDbsRtwAlertRaisedData.description: Sent each time a DBS or right to work alert is raised: new DBS information or a certificate that holds information, a right to work check that found no right to work or could not verify a passport or share code, and the reminders before a right to work or share code expires. The same alert is in `GET /alerts/{id}` and is emailed to the account's notification address. Registration alerts are not sent here. Unlike the other events this payload carries text, but none of it names the worker: `title` is the alert type's label and `description` has any DBS certificate number masked to its last four characters (`********7890`). Look the worker up with `worker_id` (`GET /workers/{id}`) or `candidate_ref`.

alert_id.description: The alert id: `GET /alerts/{id}` returns it and `POST /alerts/{id}/acknowledge` acknowledges it.

worker_id.description: The worker id: the `id` of the worker in `GET /workers`. The payload has no worker name, so fetch the worker to see who it is.

candidate_ref.description: The `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid) of the Hub candidate the worker is linked to; null when the worker is not linked to one (workers created through the API, an import or the Hub pages are not). Use it to match the alert to your own candidate record.

type.description: What raised the alert: `dbs_new_info`, `dbs_non_blank`, `rtw_issue`, `rtw_expired`, `rtw_expiry_3_days`, `rtw_expiry_1_month`, `rtw_expiry_3_months`, `rtw_share_code_expired`, `rtw_share_code_expiry_3_days` or `rtw_share_code_expiry_14_days`. The value always starts with `dbs_` or `rtw_`.

severity.description: How serious the alert is: `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`.

title.description: The alert type's label for a person to read, for example `DBS new information` or `Right to work expired`. It never contains the worker's name (the alert's `title` in `GET /alerts/{id}` does).

description.description: What happened, for a person to read. Any DBS certificate number is masked to its last four characters, and the worker's name is not included. A right to work alert gives the reason or the days left.
description.example: The DBS Update Service reports new information for certificate ********7890. Request a new DBS certificate before the worker continues.

example.title: DBS new information
example.description: The DBS Update Service reports new information for certificate ********7890. Request a new DBS certificate before the worker continues.

WebhookDbsRtwDbsStatusChangedData.description: Sent when a completed DBS Update Service check returns a status that differs from the one stored for the worker, including the first successful check of a worker (then `previous_status` is null). A check that failed or was rejected by the service never fires it, because it does not change the status. A change to `NEW_INFO` or `NON_BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO` also raises an alert and sends `dbs-rtw.alert.raised`. The payload holds ids and the two statuses; it has no certificate number, no worker name and no `candidate_ref`.

worker_id.description: The worker id: the `id` of the worker in `GET /workers`. Webhook payloads identify the worker by id only, so fetch the worker to see who it is.

dbs_check_id.description: The id of the DBS check: the `id` of a check in `GET /workers/{id}/verification?track=dbs`; with it, `GET /evidence/dbs/{check}` downloads the certificate PDF and `GET /dbs-checks/{check}/raw-data` gives the service's answer.

previous_status.description: The DBS status the worker had before: `BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO`, `NON_BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO`, `NEW_INFO` or `NO_MATCH_FOUND`. Null for the first successful check.

new_status.description: The DBS status this check returned: `BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO`, `NON_BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO`, `NEW_INFO` or `NO_MATCH_FOUND`. `BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO` is the only status that counts as compliant.

checked_at.description: When the check ran, ISO 8601 UTC with `Z`; null only if the time was not recorded.

WebhookDbsRtwRtwStatusChangedData.description: Sent when a right to work check that reached a result (a share code checked against the Home Office service, or a passport read from its image) leaves the worker with a status that differs from the one stored, including the first result of a worker (then `previous_status` is null). A check that ended in an error (a missing share code or date of birth, or a document type that is not verified automatically) never fires it. A result of `no_right`, or a share code that is invalid or expired, also raises an alert and sends `dbs-rtw.alert.raised`. The payload holds ids, the two statuses and the expiry date; it has no worker name and no `candidate_ref`.

worker_id.description: The worker id: the `id` of the worker in `GET /workers`. Webhook payloads identify the worker by id only, so fetch the worker to see who it is.

rtw_check_id.description: The id of the right to work check: the `id` of a check in `GET /workers/{id}/verification?track=rtw`; with it, `GET /evidence/rtw/{check}` downloads the screenshot and `GET /rtw-checks/{check}/raw-data` gives the stored response.

previous_status.description: The right to work status the worker had before: `has_right` or `no_right`. Null for the first result.

new_status.description: The status this check found: `has_right` or `no_right`.

rtw_expiry_date.description: The date the worker's right to work ends as the check found it, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null for a permanent right or when none was found.

checked_at.description: When the check ran, ISO 8601 UTC with `Z`; null only if the time was not recorded.

WebhookDelivery.description: One delivery: one event sent to one endpoint, with the attempts made so far. A redelivery reuses the same delivery (same id and `event_id`) and restarts the attempts.

id.description: The delivery id (integer); it is the `X-Hub-Delivery-Id` header of every attempt and the `{delivery}` of the redeliver call.

event_type.description: The event name (`{portal}.{event}`), or `webhook.test` for a test event.

event_id.description: The event's unique id (uuid), the `event_id` of the body and the `X-Hub-Event-Id` header. It stays the same on a redelivery, so use it to ignore an event you already handled.

status.description: `pending`: queued, no attempt yet. `retrying`: an attempt failed and the next is scheduled (pauses of 60, 300, 900 and 3600 seconds). `delivered`: your server answered with a 2xx status. `failed`: all 5 attempts failed, or the endpoint was off or removed when the delivery ran.

attempt.description: How many attempts have been made so far, 0 to 5. It goes back to 0 when the delivery is redelivered.

response_code.description: The HTTP status your server returned on the latest attempt, or null if it has not been attempted or got no answer (a timeout, a refused connection or an address Hub refused to call).

delivered_at.description: When the delivery succeeded (ISO 8601 UTC), or null. After a redelivery of a delivered event it keeps the earlier time until the new attempt succeeds.

created_at.description: When the event was queued for this endpoint (ISO 8601 UTC).

WebhookEndpoint.description: A webhook endpoint of the client: an address that receives the events it picked, from any portal, signed with its own secret. The signing secret itself is never part of this object.

id.description: The endpoint id, used in the paths of `/api/v2/webhooks/{webhook}`. An integer.

name.description: A name you chose, up to 100 characters, to recognise the endpoint in lists and on the Developer page.

url.description: The https address Hub sends events to (up to 2048 characters). It must resolve to a public server, carry no username or password, and answer directly: Hub does not follow redirects, so a `3xx` counts as a failed delivery.

events.description: The events the endpoint receives, each `{portal}.{event}`. The list is the whole subscription: an event not in it is not sent. See `GET /api/v2/webhooks/events` for every name.

is_active.description: False when the endpoint is switched off, by you (`is_active: false`) or by Hub after 25 failed deliveries in a row. No events are queued for it and queued deliveries fail while it is off. Switch it on again with `PUT` and `is_active: true`, which also resets `consecutive_failures`.

timeout_seconds.description: How long Hub waits for your server to answer each attempt, 5 to 30 seconds (the connection itself must open within 5). Null means the default of 10 seconds.

secret_prefix.description: The first 12 characters of the signing secret (`whsec_` and six more) followed by bullets, to tell which secret is current after a rotation. It cannot be used to sign or verify anything; the full secret is shown only when the endpoint is created or the secret is rotated.

last_delivered_at.description: When a delivery to this endpoint last succeeded (your server answered 2xx), or null if none has yet.

last_response_code.description: The HTTP status your server returned on the most recent attempt (success or failure), or null if nothing was delivered yet or the last attempt got no answer (a timeout or connection error).

consecutive_failures.description: Deliveries that failed for good, in a row: it counts a delivery once all its attempts have failed (5 attempts), not each attempt, and goes back to 0 on the first success or when the endpoint is switched on again. At 25 Hub switches the endpoint off (`is_active` false).

imported.description: True for an endpoint copied from an old portal API when Hub moved to one webhook system. Such an endpoint is still sent that portal's own event names, body shape and signature headers (in addition to the standard `X-Hub-*` headers), so an existing receiver keeps working.

created_at.description: When the endpoint was created (ISO 8601 UTC).

WebhookEndpointCreated.description: The endpoint plus the signing secret, shown only now: in the answer to creating the endpoint and to rotating its secret. Nothing else ever returns the secret.

signing_secret.description: The secret that signs every delivery: `whsec_` followed by 48 random characters. Store it now, it is not shown again. Compute the HMAC-SHA256 of `{X-Hub-Timestamp}.{raw body}` with it and compare with `X-Hub-Signature` (`sha256=` and the hex digest) to verify a delivery.

notice.description: A reminder to store the secret.
notice.example: Store the signing secret now. It is not shown again.

name.description: A name to recognise the endpoint by, up to 100 characters.

url.description: The https address Hub sends events to, up to 2048 characters. It must be a full `https` URL to a public server: `http`, a username or password in the URL, and addresses on private networks are refused with `422` on `url`. Redirects are not followed.

events.description: The events to receive, each `{portal}.{event}` from `GET /api/v2/webhooks/events`; at least one. On an update this replaces the whole list.

is_active.description: False to create the endpoint switched off (or to switch it off on an update); true to switch it on, which on an update also resets the failure count. Default true when creating.

timeout_seconds.description: How long Hub waits for your server's answer, 5 to 30 seconds. Default 10; null on an update returns to the default.

WebhookEndpointPatch.description: The fields to change; fields left out keep their value.

name.description: A name to recognise the endpoint by, up to 100 characters.

url.description: The https address Hub sends events to, up to 2048 characters. It must be a full `https` URL to a public server: `http`, a username or password in the URL, and addresses on private networks are refused with `422` on `url`. Redirects are not followed.

events.description: The events to receive, each `{portal}.{event}` from `GET /api/v2/webhooks/events`; at least one. On an update this replaces the whole list.

is_active.description: False to create the endpoint switched off (or to switch it off on an update); true to switch it on, which on an update also resets the failure count. Default true when creating.

timeout_seconds.description: How long Hub waits for your server's answer, 5 to 30 seconds. Default 10; null on an update returns to the default.

WebhookEnvelope.description: The body of every webhook delivery. The `data` object depends on `event_type`; it holds ids, statuses, dates and a `candidate_ref`, never a name, email or health data.

event_id.description: Unique id of the event. A redelivery keeps it, so use it to ignore duplicates.

occurred_at.description: When it happened, ISO 8601 UTC with a Z.

WebhookEventGroup.description: The events of one portal, to pick from when you create or update an endpoint.

key.description: The portal key, the first part of its event names (`online-training` in `online-training.course.completed`).

events.description: The events of the portal. Put the `event` value in the `events` of an endpoint.

event.description: The event name to put in `events`.

WebhookMessage.description: A plain confirmation of an action that has no resource to return.

WebhookOccupationalHealthDocumentAvailab.description:
A current Fit to Work certificate or fail letter was recorded for a candidate: the closing document of a clearance. It is sent when the document becomes the current one, once per document, whether it was issued with an outcome (`source` `submission`) or is the candidate's standing certificate (`source` `candidate`). It is usually sent straight after the matching outcome event (`request.full_clearance`, `request.temporary_clearance` or `request.fail`).

Download it with `GET /requests/{id}/ftw/{ftw}`, using `document_id` as `{ftw}` and the same `source` as `?source=`; the key needs the scope `occupational-health:documents:read`. `request_id` and `submission_id` are `null` for a candidate's standing document that belongs to no request. `kind` is `ftw_certificate` or `fail_letter`. The file itself is health data and is never in the body.

request_id.description: The request the document belongs to; null for a candidate's standing document.

submission_id.description: The questionnaire the document belongs to; null for a candidate's standing document.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

document_id.description: The id of the document: the `ftw` path parameter of the download.

source.description: Where the document belongs: `submission` (the request's own) or `candidate` (the candidate's standing document). Pass it as `source` when downloading.

kind.description: `ftw_certificate` for a Fit to Work certificate or `fail_letter` for a fail letter.

WebhookOccupationalHealthRenewalDueData.description:
A candidate's clearance is due for renewal and Hub emailed them a reminder. It is sent once for each renewal window, when the reminder email is sent (not at the instant the clearance falls due), and never for a dry run. `due_at` is the date the clearance expires or expired (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

Use it to start a renewal: create a request with `POST /requests` and `request_type` `renewal` for the same `candidate_ref`. The body has the `candidate_ref` and the date only, because a renewal reminder belongs to the candidate and not to one request.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

due_at.description: The date the clearance is due for renewal, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

WebhookOccupationalHealthRequestAwaiting.description:
A request is waiting for the candidate. It is sent in two situations, and `awaiting` tells them apart. When a request is created with an online questionnaire that Hub has a form for, it is sent straight after `request.submitted`, with `awaiting` set to `questionnaire` and `form` naming the first questionnaire the candidate has to complete; the request is emailed to Healthier Business only once that questionnaire is in. When a reviewer asks the candidate for more information (a request needs a document or an answer), it is sent again with the questionnaire's `submission_reference`, `form` and `has_review_note`, and `awaiting` is absent.

The reviewer's note is health data and is never in the body: `has_review_note` only says whether one exists. Read it with `GET /requests/{id}`. For the first situation you can answer the questionnaire for the candidate with `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers` (see `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`), or leave it to the candidate, who has been emailed. The request leaves this state with `request.questionnaire_completed` or an outcome event.

request_id.description: The request id (see `GET /requests/{id}`). For a questionnaire completed by a candidate, the id the request had while it waited. Null for an older questionnaire that has no request.

submission_id.description: The id of the completed questionnaire; null while the request waits for the candidate or for a paper questionnaire.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

status.description: The client status of the request after the event.

reference.description: The request reference, `OH-{id}`; for a questionnaire with no request, the questionnaire's own reference.

awaiting.description: What the request waits for: `questionnaire`. Present when the request was created awaiting the candidate.

form.description: The shortcode of the questionnaire the candidate must complete (or, when a reviewer asked for more information, the questionnaire concerned).

submission_reference.description: The questionnaire's own reference. Present when a reviewer asked for more information.

has_review_note.description: True when the reviewer left a note; read it with `GET /requests/{id}`. Present when a reviewer asked for more information.

WebhookOccupationalHealthRequestFailData.description:
The assessment ended in a fail: the candidate was found not fit. It is sent once, when the outcome is recorded (or when a fail letter closes a request that was waiting), and the request's client status becomes `fail`. When a fail letter is issued it follows as `document.available` with `kind` `fail_letter`, and the request appears in `GET /alerts` as a critical alert until it is dismissed.

This is the most sensitive event of the portal, so the body is kept to ids and the status. `has_review_note` says whether the reviewer left a note; the note and the letter are health data and are read only with `GET /requests/{id}` and the document endpoints, by a key with the right scopes. Treat the event as a prompt to look the request up, not as the record itself.

request_id.description: The request id (see `GET /requests/{id}`). For a questionnaire completed by a candidate, the id the request had while it waited. Null for an older questionnaire that has no request.

submission_id.description: The id of the completed questionnaire; null while the request waits for the candidate or for a paper questionnaire.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

status.description: The client status of the request after the event.

reference.description: The request reference, `OH-{id}`; for a questionnaire with no request, the questionnaire's own reference.

submission_reference.description: The questionnaire's own reference; null for a request that has no questionnaire.

form.description: The shortcode of the questionnaire; null for a request without one.

has_review_note.description: True when the reviewer left a note; read the note with `GET /requests/{id}`. The note itself is never sent.

WebhookOccupationalHealthRequestFullClea.description:
Full clearance was issued. It is also sent for conditional clearance, which Hub shows to clients as full clearance, and when a standing Fit to Work certificate from the candidate closes a request that was waiting. It is sent once, when the outcome is recorded; the request's client status becomes `full_clearance` and a certificate follows as `document.available`, usually straight after.

For a questionnaire, `next_renewal` is the date the clearance expires (`YYYY-MM-DD`), worked out by the renewal rule from the date the questionnaire was completed; a candidate is reminded when it nears, which causes `renewal.due`. For a request closed by a standing certificate there is no questionnaire, so `submission_id` and `next_renewal` are absent or null. `has_review_note` says whether the reviewer left a note, which you read with `GET /requests/{id}`; the note itself is never in the body.

request_id.description: The request id (see `GET /requests/{id}`). For a questionnaire completed by a candidate, the id the request had while it waited. Null for an older questionnaire that has no request.

submission_id.description: The id of the completed questionnaire; null while the request waits for the candidate or for a paper questionnaire.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

status.description: The client status of the request after the event.

reference.description: The request reference, `OH-{id}`; for a questionnaire with no request, the questionnaire's own reference.

submission_reference.description: The questionnaire's own reference; null for a request that has no questionnaire.

form.description: The shortcode of the questionnaire; null for a request without one.

has_review_note.description: True when the reviewer left a note; read the note with `GET /requests/{id}`. The note itself is never sent.

next_renewal.description: The date the clearance expires and is due for renewal, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Present for a questionnaire.

WebhookOccupationalHealthRequestQuestion.description:
A health questionnaire of a request was completed and sent: by the candidate in Hub, or by you through `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers` on the candidate's behalf. `submitted_by` says which (`candidate` or `client_api`). It is sent once per questionnaire, after the answers are saved and the request has been released to Healthier Business, so reading `GET /requests/{request_id}` straight away shows `has_answers: true`. `request_id` is the id the request had while it waited, so the same number identifies it before and after; it is `null` for a questionnaire that belongs to no request.

`status` is the client status of the questionnaire at that moment, normally `submitted`. `submission_id` and `submission_reference` identify the new questionnaire and `form` is its shortcode. A request with several forms causes one event per form. No answer is ever in the body: they are health data, read with `GET /requests/{id}/answers` and a key that has the scope `occupational-health:requests:read`. An outcome follows later as `request.full_clearance`, `request.temporary_clearance`, `request.rejected` or `request.fail`.

request_id.description: The request id (see `GET /requests/{id}`). For a questionnaire completed by a candidate, the id the request had while it waited. Null for an older questionnaire that has no request.

submission_id.description: The id of the completed questionnaire; null while the request waits for the candidate or for a paper questionnaire.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

status.description: The client status of the request after the event.

reference.description: The request reference, `OH-{id}`; for a questionnaire with no request, the questionnaire's own reference.

submission_reference.description: The questionnaire's own reference (the `submission_ref` of the older agency API).

form.description: The shortcode of the questionnaire that was completed.

submitted_by.description: Who sent the questionnaire: `candidate` (they completed it in Hub) or `client_api` (you submitted the answers for them through `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`).

WebhookOccupationalHealthRequestRejected.description:
A request was rejected: the reviewer could not accept the questionnaire and the request must be sent again. It is sent once, when the rejection is recorded, and the request's client status becomes `rejected`; it also appears in `GET /alerts` as a critical alert until it is dismissed or changes status. The candidate can send the questionnaire again, and so can you with `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`, which accepts a form in the `resubmit` state.

The reviewer's note explains the reason and is health data, so it is never in the body: `has_review_note` says whether there is one, and `GET /requests/{id}` returns it as `review_note`. The body has ids, the status, the references, the form shortcode and `candidate_ref` only.

request_id.description: The request id (see `GET /requests/{id}`). For a questionnaire completed by a candidate, the id the request had while it waited. Null for an older questionnaire that has no request.

submission_id.description: The id of the completed questionnaire; null while the request waits for the candidate or for a paper questionnaire.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

status.description: The client status of the request after the event.

reference.description: The request reference, `OH-{id}`; for a questionnaire with no request, the questionnaire's own reference.

submission_reference.description: The questionnaire's own reference; null for a request that has no questionnaire.

form.description: The shortcode of the questionnaire; null for a request without one.

has_review_note.description: True when the reviewer left a note; read the note with `GET /requests/{id}`. The note itself is never sent.

WebhookOccupationalHealthRequestSubmitte.description:
A request was created, through `POST /requests` or the New Request page in Hub. It is sent once per request, straight after the request is stored, and tells you the request id (`OH-{request_id}` is the `reference`) that every later event and every endpoint will use for it. `status` is always `submitted` here; a request that has to wait for the candidate to complete an online questionnaire also causes `request.awaiting_candidate`, a separate delivery sent straight after this one.

`submission_id` is `null` because no questionnaire exists yet (and never will for a paper questionnaire). The body carries ids, the status, the reference and the `candidate_ref` only: nothing the candidate or you typed, and no file names. Read the request with `GET /requests/{id}`. Because the API call that created the request already returned the same id, a client that created it through the API can use this event to confirm, and one that did not can use it to learn about requests made by colleagues in Hub.

request_id.description: The request id (see `GET /requests/{id}`). For a questionnaire completed by a candidate, the id the request had while it waited. Null for an older questionnaire that has no request.

submission_id.description: The id of the completed questionnaire; null while the request waits for the candidate or for a paper questionnaire.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

status.description: The client status of the request after the event.

reference.description: The request reference, `OH-{id}`; for a questionnaire with no request, the questionnaire's own reference.

WebhookOccupationalHealthRequestTemporar.description:
Temporary clearance was issued for the candidate. It is sent once, when the outcome is recorded, and the request's client status becomes `temporary_clearance`. When the outcome comes with a certificate, it follows as `document.available`. Read the reviewer's note, if there is one (`has_review_note`), with `GET /requests/{id}`.

Temporary clearance is only recorded when the account allows it (`allow_temporary_clearance` in `GET /settings`); you ask for it with `scope` `temporary` when you create a new starter's request for a clearance type that needs immunisations. The body has ids, the status, the references, the form shortcode and `candidate_ref` only.

request_id.description: The request id (see `GET /requests/{id}`). For a questionnaire completed by a candidate, the id the request had while it waited. Null for an older questionnaire that has no request.

submission_id.description: The id of the completed questionnaire; null while the request waits for the candidate or for a paper questionnaire.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

status.description: The client status of the request after the event.

reference.description: The request reference, `OH-{id}`; for a questionnaire with no request, the questionnaire's own reference.

submission_reference.description: The questionnaire's own reference; null for a request that has no questionnaire.

form.description: The shortcode of the questionnaire; null for a request without one.

has_review_note.description: True when the reviewer left a note; read the note with `GET /requests/{id}`. The note itself is never sent.

WebhookOnlineTrainingCertificateIssuedDa.description:
A combined training certificate was supplied for a candidate.

When it fires: when Healthier Business staff supply a combined certificate for the candidate from the admin pages of Hub (a combined certificate of the candidate's completed courses, or of one course). It is not sent when you download a certificate with `GET /candidates/{candidate_ref}/certificate`, and not when a learner downloads their own. Who gets it: every active endpoint of the client that picked `online-training.certificate.issued`.

The data holds the `candidate_ref`, the `type` of certificate and `issued_at`. The certificate itself is not attached: fetch it with `GET /candidates/{candidate_ref}/certificate` using the same `type`.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

type.description: Which certificate was supplied: one of `current`, `assigned`, `all`, `excl-expired`, `incl-expired`, `range`, `course`, `care` or `cstf`.

issued_at.description: When the certificate was supplied, ISO 8601 UTC.

WebhookOnlineTrainingCourseAssignedData.description:
Courses were added to a candidate.

When it fires: after the assignment is saved, whichever way it was made: `PUT /api/v2/online-training/candidates/{candidate_ref}/courses`, the Assign Courses and bulk assignment pages in Hub, a CSV import, or an e-learning account created for a practical or BLS booking. One event is sent per assignment, listing every course added by it; courses that were already assigned are not in `course_ids`, and an assignment that adds nothing (including removals only) sends no event. Who gets it: every active endpoint of the client that picked `online-training.course.assigned`.

The data carries the `candidate_ref`, the course ids and names and `assigned_at`; it never carries the candidate's name or email. Credits are not part of the event: for the credits an assignment took, read the answer of the API call or `GET /credits/transactions`. A failure to queue the event never undoes the assignment.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

course_ids.description: The ids of the courses added.

course_id.description: The course id.

courses.description: The courses added, each with its id and name.

assigned_at.description: When the courses were assigned, ISO 8601 UTC.

WebhookOnlineTrainingCourseCompletedData.description:
A candidate passed a course.

When it fires: when a learner passes a course (the result is recorded), or when staff mark the course complete in Hub. It is the fact the v1 `callback_url` course callback reported, now delivered through the Hub webhook system with a signature and retries. One event per course passed, so a candidate finishing three courses causes three events; the event for the last of their assigned courses is followed by `online-training.training.completed`. Who gets it: every active endpoint of the client that picked `online-training.course.completed`.

The data holds the `candidate_ref`, the course id and name, the dates and the `grade` from 0 to 1 (rounded to four decimals), and `expires_at`, the date the certificate runs out and the course is due for renewal. A renewal completed later sends a new event for the same course. No name or email is included: fetch `GET /candidates/{candidate_ref}/results/{course_id}` for more.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

course_id.description: The course id.

status.description: Always `completed`.

expires_at.description: When the certificate expires and the course is due for renewal.

grade.description: The result, from 0 to 1 (1 is 100 percent); null when no grade was recorded.

WebhookOnlineTrainingTrainingCompletedDa.description:
Every assigned course of the candidate is now complete.

When it fires: when the last of the candidate's assigned courses is completed and Hub marks their training as complete (the fact the v1 training-complete callback reported). It is sent right after the `online-training.course.completed` event of that last course. Who gets it: every active endpoint of the client that picked `online-training.training.completed`. It fires when the candidate's training changes from incomplete to complete, so it fires again if new courses or a renewal made the training incomplete and the candidate then completes it again, but not for every course in between.

The data holds the `candidate_ref`, the number of courses assigned and completed, `completed_at` (the date of the candidate's certificate) and `expires_at`, the date the earliest course is due for renewal. It does not say which courses; read `GET /candidates/{candidate_ref}` for those.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

status.description: Always `complete`.

courses_assigned.description: How many courses the candidate has assigned.

courses_completed.description: How many of them are complete.

completed_at.description: When the last course was completed (the certificate date).

expires_at.description: When the training is due for renewal.

WebhookOnlineTrainingTrainingExpiredData.description:
A candidate's training has expired.

When it fires: only when Hub's renewal reminder job (`online-training.schedule.candidate_renewals`) emails a candidate whose renewal date has already passed. Like `online-training.training.expiring` it covers only candidates on automatic renewal who receive reminders, only while the job runs, and it can repeat on each reminder. It is sent at the time of the reminder, not at the moment of expiry, so `expires_at` can be days in the past. Who gets it: every active endpoint of the client that picked `online-training.training.expired`.

The data holds the `candidate_ref`, the status `expired` and `expires_at`, the renewal date that has passed. Poll `GET /candidates?status=expired` for a complete list.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

status.description: Always `expired`.

expires_at.description: The renewal date that has passed.

WebhookOnlineTrainingTrainingExpiringDat.description:
A candidate's training is due for renewal soon.

When it fires: only when Hub's renewal reminder job (the scheduled `online-training.schedule.candidate_renewals` job) emails the candidate a renewal reminder and their renewal date has not yet passed. So it covers only candidates who are on automatic renewal with reminders switched on, and only while the job is running; a candidate whose training is about to expire but who receives no reminder produces no event. The event is sent each time a reminder is sent, so it can repeat for one candidate on each reminder date. Who gets it: every active endpoint of the client that picked `online-training.training.expiring`.

The data holds the `candidate_ref`, the status `expiring_soon` and `expires_at`. If you need to know about every expiry regardless of reminders, poll `GET /candidates?status=expiring_soon` or `expires_from` and `expires_to`.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

status.description: Always `expiring_soon`.

expires_at.description: When the training is due for renewal.

WebhookPracticalTrainingBalanceDepletedD.description: The booking balance ran out: a withdrawal took it from a positive amount to zero or below. Bookings paid with `balance` are rejected when the balance cannot cover the price, so top up the balance (outside the API). It is sent once per crossing.

balance_pence.description: The booking balance after the withdrawal, in integer pence. Zero, or negative when a fee took it below zero.

currency.description: The currency of the amount: always `GBP`.

WebhookPracticalTrainingBalanceLowData.description: The booking balance fell to or below the low-balance threshold. It is sent when a withdrawal takes the balance from above the threshold to the threshold or less (and the balance is still above zero), so it is sent once per crossing, not on every later booking. The threshold is set by the service configuration (10000 pence, £100, at the time of writing); read it from `threshold_pence`.

balance_pence.description: The booking balance after the withdrawal, in integer pence.

threshold_pence.description: The low-balance threshold, in integer pence.

currency.description: The currency of the amounts: always `GBP`.

WebhookPracticalTrainingBookingAttendanc.description: Attendance was recorded for the last training day of a booking. The event is sent once, when the last day is recorded, not for earlier days of a multi-day course; it is also sent again when Healthier Business sends the attendance notifications again. A candidate marked `absent` also causes `booking.no_show`, and one marked `passed` also causes `booking.certificate_available`, each as its own delivery. The `data` carries ids, names of the course and location, the status, and the `candidate_ref` instead of the candidate's name and email address. Events are sent for every booking of the account, whichever way it was made (this API, the Bookings page, a booking link or an invitation).

booking_id.description: The booking id: the `id` of the booking in `GET /bookings/{booking}`.

candidate_ref.description: The `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid) of the person booked: the Hub candidate of the account with the booking's HB Portal candidate id, otherwise with the same email address. Null when the account has no such Hub candidate, for example a booking made for someone who is not in the account's Hub candidates. The name and email address are never sent; read them from the Hub candidate.

training_event_id.description: The id of the session (training event) the booking is on after the event. For `booking.rescheduled` it is the new session. Use it with `GET /training-events/{event}`.

course_id.description: The id of the course of the session (see `GET /courses`).

location_name.description: The name of the location of the session. Null when the session has no location.

start_date.description: When the session starts: an instant in UTC with a `Z`, the session's UK local time converted to UTC. In British Summer Time it is an hour earlier than the clock in the UK (a 09:00 session on 7 July is `2026-07-07T08:00:00Z`), in winter it is the same (a 09:00 session on 7 November is `2026-11-07T09:00:00Z`).

booking_status.description: The booking's status after the event: `pending`, `booked`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled` (nothing was paid back), `refunded` (cancelled and money or credit was paid back to the original payment method) or `abandoned` (the same values as `booking_status` in the API).

pay_option.description: How the booking is paid for: `credits`, `balance`, `inv` (invoiced), `cc` (by card, including a candidate-pays booking) or `free`.

attendance.description: The attendance result recorded for the last training day: `passed`, `present` or `absent`.

attendance_day.description: The number of the training day the attendance was recorded for. It is the last day of the booking's course, as the event is only sent after the last day.

It is sent after a booking is completed (taking its seat) when the places left on its session are at or below the threshold, so it is sent for every such booking, including the one that fills the session (`remaining_slots` `0`), not only the first. The threshold is set by the service configuration (3 places at the time of writing); read it from `threshold`.

start_date.description: When the session starts: an instant in UTC with a `Z`, the session's UK local time converted to UTC. In British Summer Time it is an hour earlier than the clock in the UK (a 09:00 session on 7 July is `2026-07-07T08:00:00Z`), in winter it is the same (a 09:00 session on 7 November is `2026-11-07T09:00:00Z`).

remaining_slots.description: The places still free after the booking.

A declined referee frees a slot, so you can add a replacement with `POST /requests/{uuid}/referees`.

WebhookReferencesReferenceExpiredData.description: A referee's reference expired without an answer. There is no separate event for a request being cancelled or expiring. The referee's name and email are not in the event.

WebhookReferencesReferenceReminderSentDa.description: A reminder email was sent to a referee: by the scheduled automatic reminders, by `POST /requests/{uuid}/reminders`, by `POST /referees/{uuid}/reminder`, or by a person in Hub. WebhookReferencesReferenceRequestCreated.description: A reference request was created, whether through the API (`POST /requests`), by a person in Hub or by Healthier Business staff. WebhookReferencesReferenceSubmittedData.description: A referee submitted their reference. It is sent after the answers are saved, the PDF is built and the client's own notification email is queued. WebhookRegistrationMonitoringWorkerIniti.description: Sent once for a worker, when its first successful registration check completes: the worker had no status yet and the check returned one. A check that failed does not count, so the event is sent when the first check that works completes. The check also raises an alert (`Initial Verification Completed` for an active registration). After this event every change of status sends `registration-monitoring.worker.status_changed` instead. The payload holds ids, the regulator, the registration number and the status found; it has no worker name and no `candidate_ref`.

worker_id.description: The worker id: the `id` of the worker in `GET /workers`. Webhook payloads identify the worker by id only, so fetch the worker to see who it is.

registration_check_id.description: The id of the first check: the `id` of a check in `GET /workers/{id}/verification`.

regulator.description: The regulator's lower case key: `nmc`, `gmc`, `hcpc`, `gdc`, `goc`, `gphc`, `ahcs`, `swe`, `sssc`, `scw`, `niscc`, `psni`, `gosc` or `gcc`.

registration_number.description: The registration number (PIN) of the worker as monitored. It identifies a person on the regulator's register: treat it as personal data.

status.description: The first status found: `active`, `lapsed`, `suspended`, `conditions`, `caution`, `removed`, `erased`, `registered_no_licence`, `not_found`, `manual_review` or `invalid_pin`.

checked_at.description: When the check ran, ISO 8601 UTC with `Z`; null only if the time was not recorded.

WebhookRegistrationMonitoringWorkerStatu.description: Sent when a completed check of a monitored registration finds a different status from the one the worker had before. It fires for the first change after the initial verification onward (the very first result sends `registration-monitoring.worker.initial_verification` instead) and for checks you asked for with `POST /workers/{id}/verify` as well as scheduled ones. A check that failed (an error, or the regulator's site being unavailable) never fires it, and neither does a regulator warning or condition flag appearing under an unchanged status (that raises an alert only). An alert for the change is raised in the same run. The payload holds ids, the regulator, the registration number and the two statuses; it has no worker name and no `candidate_ref`.

worker_id.description: The worker id: the `id` of the worker in `GET /workers`. Webhook payloads identify the worker by id only, so fetch the worker to see who it is.

registration_check_id.description: The id of the check that found the new status: the `id` of a check in `GET /workers/{id}/verification` and the `registration_check_id` of the alert and evidence files it produced.

regulator.description: The regulator's lower case key: `nmc`, `gmc`, `hcpc`, `gdc`, `goc`, `gphc`, `ahcs`, `swe`, `sssc`, `scw`, `niscc`, `psni`, `gosc` or `gcc`.

BadRequest.description: The JSON body could not be parsed. Error codes: `bad_request`.

example.message: The request could not be understood.

Conflict.description: The request clashes with the current state: an `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body, or a portal rule such as a taken timeslot. Error codes: `conflict`, `idempotency_conflict`, portal codes (`slot_taken`, `hold_exists`, ...).

example.message: This Idempotency-Key was used with a different request body.

Forbidden.description: The key may not do this: it lacks the scope (the message names it), the caller address is not on its allowlist, the key is switched off, the client does not use this portal, or the portal refuses the action. Error codes: `insufficient_scope`, `ip_not_allowed`, `key_inactive`, `portal_unavailable`, `forbidden` and portal codes.

example.message: This API key does not have the scope occupational-health:requests:read.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The method is not allowed for this path; the `Allow` header lists the right ones. Error codes: `method_not_allowed`.

example.message: This method is not allowed for this resource.

NotFound.description: The record does not exist or belongs to another client. Both answer the same, so ids cannot be probed. Error codes: `not_found`.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The body is over the server limit. Error codes: `payload_too_large`.

example.message: The request body is too large.

PaymentRequired.description: The call costs more credits than the balance holds (`required` and `available` say how many), or the candidate must pay first (`payment_url`). Error codes: `insufficient_credits`, `payment_required`.

example.message: There are not enough credits for this action.

RateLimited.description: Over the key's hourly limit or a route's own throttle. `Retry-After` gives the seconds to wait. Error codes: `rate_limited`.

example.message: Too many requests. Try again later.

ServerError.description: Something unexpected failed. The message is generic; quote the `request_id` to support. Error codes: `server_error`.

example.message: Something went wrong on our side.

ServiceUnavailable.description: Maintenance or an unavailable dependency; `Retry-After` is set when known. Error codes: `service_unavailable`.

Unauthenticated.description: No bearer token, or the token, refresh token or API key is unknown, revoked or expired. Error codes: `unauthenticated`, `invalid_token`, `invalid_credentials`.

example.message: A valid bearer token is required.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The body is not JSON, form or multipart. Error codes: `unsupported_media_type`.

example.message: The content type of the request is not supported.

ValidationFailed.description: The input is invalid. `details` maps each field to its messages. Portal rules that are not field errors use their own code with status 422. Error codes: `validation_failed` and portal codes (`booking_rejected`, `verification_refused`, ...).

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

WebhookDeliveryId.name: X-Hub-Delivery-Id
WebhookDeliveryId.description: The id of this delivery (an integer). It is the id you use with `POST /api/v2/webhooks/{webhook}/deliveries/{delivery}/redeliver`.

WebhookEvent.name: X-Hub-Event
WebhookEvent.description: The event name, the same as `event_type` in the body.

WebhookEventId.name: X-Hub-Event-Id
WebhookEventId.description: The unique id of the event, the same as `event_id` in the body. A redelivery keeps it; use it to ignore an event you already handled.

WebhookSignature.name: X-Hub-Signature
WebhookSignature.description: Proof the call came from Hub: `sha256=` followed by the lower case hex HMAC-SHA256 of the text `{X-Hub-Timestamp}.{raw request body}`, keyed with the endpoint's signing secret (shown once when the endpoint is created or its secret rotated). Compute it over the exact bytes received, compare in constant time, and reject a mismatch.

WebhookTimestamp.name: X-Hub-Timestamp
WebhookTimestamp.description: When Hub sent this attempt, in whole seconds since the Unix epoch. It is part of what is signed. We recommend rejecting a delivery whose timestamp is more than five minutes from your clock, to stop replays.

IdempotentReplayed.description: Present with `true` when this answer is the stored first answer for the same `Idempotency-Key` and body.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

XRateLimitLimit.description: How many calls the key may make per hour.

XRateLimitRemaining.description: Calls left in the current hour window.

XRateLimitReset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the window frees.

XRequestId.description: The id of this request. It is the `request_id` of an error body and is written to the API log, so support can trace the call.

bearerAuth.description: A short-lived access token. Get one with `POST /api/v2/auth/token` (body `{ "api_key": "hbk_..." }`; the answer holds `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `expires_in` and `refresh_expires_in`) and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. When it expires, `POST /api/v2/auth/refresh` with the `refresh_token` returns a new pair and revokes the old refresh token. `POST /api/v2/auth/revoke` ends a token early.
